1	// Package engine defines the translation backend abstraction and its
2	// implementations (LLM via OpenAI-compatible APIs, free web APIs, dictionaries).
3	//
4	// The engine layer is pure Go with context.Context and imports zero TUI code:
5	// the one-shot CLI and the Bubble Tea TUI drive the identical Engine values and
6	// diverge only at presentation.
7	package engine
8	
9	import "context"
10	
11	// Mode selects what kind of lookup a Request performs.
12	type Mode int
13	
14	const (
15		// ModeTranslate is register-aware, faithful translation (the default).
16		ModeTranslate Mode = iota
17		// ModeDict is a dictionary/definition lookup.
18		ModeDict
19	)
20	
21	// Request is the single input to every engine. A Source of "" or "auto" asks
22	// the engine to detect the source language.
23	type Request struct {
24		Text    string
25		Source  string // BCP-47-ish code or "auto"/""
26		Target  string // e.g. "en", "zh"
27		Mode    Mode
28		MaxAlts int    // cap on Alternatives; 0 => engine default
29		Stream  bool   // caller wants token streaming (LLM only; others ignore)
30		Model   string // optional per-request model override (LLM engines)
31		// ModelProvider scopes Model to one provider by name; other engines ignore
32		// the override (so a copilot model id never leaks to an Ollama fallback).
33		ModelProvider string
34		Preset        string // LLM prompt style: "" => concise (LLM translate only)
35		Extra         string // extra user instructions appended to the system prompt
36	
37		// Pair marks a bidirectional "pair" request: the text is written in one of
38		// two languages (PairHome/PairAway) and must be translated into the OTHER.
39		// The LLM translate prompt uses this to detect-and-route and, critically, to
40		// never echo the input unchanged. Target still carries the caller's routed
41		// best guess (for history/display and non-LLM engines).
42		Pair     bool
43		PairHome string // one pair language (e.g. the home target, "zh-TW")
44		PairAway string // the other pair language (e.g. "en")
45	
46		// Learn marks a language-learning request. It is bidirectional (implies Pair,
47		// with PairHome=native and PairAway=foreign) and adaptive: native-language input
48		// is translated-and-taught (glosses + examples), foreign-language input is
49		// grammar-corrected-and-explained. The LLM engine answers with a strict JSON
50		// object (parsed into TranslateResult.Learn) and, because the output is
51		// structured, always runs NON-STREAMING regardless of Stream.
52		Learn bool
53	
54		// Bilingual marks a whole-document bilingual ("doc mode") request: Segments
55		// carries the full ordered document (prose to translate + code shown only as
56		// context) and the LLM returns a JSON map of prose-segment number → translation.
57		// Context-aware and single-call. LLM engines only (google/dict ignore it), and
58		// like Learn it always runs NON-STREAMING.
59		Bilingual bool
60		Segments  []Segment
61	}
62	
63	// Segment is one unit of a Bilingual document request: a prose block to translate,
64	// or a command/code block included only as surrounding context (Code == true).
65	type Segment struct {
66		Text string
67		Code bool
68	}
69	
70	// TranslateResult is the "Marvin-lite" typed result. Every engine fills what it
71	// can; zero-value fields are simply absent. It is also the history record shape.
72	type TranslateResult struct {
73		Translation    string   `json:"translation"`
74		DetectedSource string   `json:"detected_source,omitempty"`
75		Target         string   `json:"target"`
76		Alternatives   []string `json:"alternatives,omitempty"`
77		Notes          string   `json:"notes,omitempty"`
78		Confidence     float64  `json:"confidence,omitempty"`
79	
80		// Warnings records non-fatal problems, e.g. a chain engine that failed before
81		// this (fallback) engine served the result — so a downgrade is never silent.
82		Warnings []string `json:"warnings,omitempty"`
83	
84		// Truncated is set when a streamed result ended before the model finished
85		// (no terminal marker, or stop_reason=="max_tokens"). The partial text is
86		// still returned so the caller can show it, but it must not be cached or
87		// persisted as if complete. Transient: not serialized.
88		Truncated bool `json:"-"`
89	
90		// Provenance — stamped by the producing engine / chain.
91		Engine string `json:"engine,omitempty"`
92		Model  string `json:"model,omitempty"`
93	
94		// Dictionary payload (Mode == ModeDict); nil for translate mode.
95		Dictionary *DictEntry `json:"dictionary,omitempty"`
96		// Learn payload (Request.Learn); nil outside learn mode. Translation still holds
97		// the main foreign-language sentence (the corrected sentence, or the translation)
98		// so copy/history/speak keep working unchanged; the structured extras ride here.
99		Learn *LearnResult `json:"learn,omitempty"`
100		// Bilingual is the doc-mode payload: prose-segment number (1-based, as numbered
101		// in the prompt) → translation. nil outside bilingual doc mode. Transient.
102		Bilingual map[int]string `json:"-"`
103		// Suggestions is a ranked "did you mean" list, set by the dictionary engine
104		// when no exact entry was found (Dictionary and Translation stay empty). The
105		// frontend decides how to present/select — the engine no longer auto-picks.
106		Suggestions []string `json:"suggestions,omitempty"`
107	
108		// SuggestDistance is the edit distance of the best entry in Suggestions (English
109		// fuzzy lookups only; 0 when unknown/not applicable, e.g. Chinese prefix matches).
110		// The smart-dict engine reads it to tell a likely typo from a match too far off.
111		// Transient: not serialized.
112		SuggestDistance int `json:"-"`
113	}
114	
115	// DictEntry is a dictionary lookup payload (populated by the dictionary engine).
116	type DictEntry struct {
117		Word      string    `json:"word"`
118		Phonetic  string    `json:"phonetic,omitempty"`
119		Meanings  []Meaning `json:"meanings,omitempty"`
120		SourceURL string    `json:"source_url,omitempty"`
121	}
122	
123	// Meaning groups definitions by part of speech.
124	type Meaning struct {
125		PartOfSpeech string       `json:"part_of_speech"`
126		Definitions  []Definition `json:"definitions"`
127		Synonyms     []string     `json:"synonyms,omitempty"`
128		Antonyms     []string     `json:"antonyms,omitempty"`
129	}
130	
131	// Definition is a single sense of a word.
132	type Definition struct {
133		Text    string `json:"definition"`
134		Example string `json:"example,omitempty"`
135	}
136	
137	// LearnResult is the structured payload for learn/tutor mode (Request.Learn). The
138	// model fills only the fields relevant to the auto-detected direction; all glosses,
139	// explanations, and notes are written in the native (home) language.
140	type LearnResult struct {
141		Direction   string         `json:"direction"`           // "teach" (native→foreign) | "correct" (foreign→native)
142		Original    string         `json:"original"`            // the user's input as received
143		Corrected   string         `json:"corrected,omitempty"` // correct-direction: the fixed foreign sentence
144		Translation string         `json:"translation"`         // teach: foreign translation; correct: native translation of intent
145		Notes       string         `json:"notes,omitempty"`     // short tip/encouragement, in the NATIVE language
146		Issues      []LearnIssue   `json:"issues,omitempty"`    // correct-direction grammar/usage fixes
147		Vocab       []LearnGloss   `json:"vocab,omitempty"`     // teach-direction glosses
148		Examples    []LearnExample `json:"examples,omitempty"`  // teach-direction usage examples
149	}
150	
151	// LearnIssue is one grammar/usage correction (correct-direction).
152	type LearnIssue struct {
153		Span        string `json:"span"`        // the problematic fragment of the input
154		Fix         string `json:"fix"`         // the corrected fragment
155		Explanation string `json:"explanation"` // why — in the NATIVE language
156	}
157	
158	// LearnGloss is one vocabulary explanation (teach-direction).
159	type LearnGloss struct {
160		Term     string `json:"term"`               // foreign word/term
161		Pos      string `json:"pos,omitempty"`      // part of speech
162		Phonetic string `json:"phonetic,omitempty"` // KK/IPA for English, pinyin for Chinese
163		Meaning  string `json:"meaning"`            // meaning in the NATIVE language
164	}
165	
166	// LearnExample is one usage example (teach-direction).
167	type LearnExample struct {
168		Foreign string `json:"foreign"` // example sentence in the foreign language
169		Native  string `json:"native"`  // its native-language translation
170	}
171	
172	// ChunkKind distinguishes streamed tokens from the terminal result/error.
173	type ChunkKind int
174	
175	const (
176		// ChunkToken is one streamed unit of translation text.
177		ChunkToken ChunkKind = iota
178		// ChunkDone carries the final structured result and ends the stream.
179		ChunkDone
180		// ChunkError carries a terminal error and ends the stream.
181		ChunkError
182	)
183	
184	// Chunk is one unit emitted on an engine's result channel.
185	type Chunk struct {
186		Kind   ChunkKind
187		Text   string           // token text (ChunkToken)
188		Result *TranslateResult // final result (ChunkDone)
189		Err    error            // terminal error (ChunkError)
190	}
191	
192	// Engine is the provider abstraction. Every method honors ctx cancellation.
193	//
194	// Translate returns a receive-only channel and MUST close it after sending
195	// exactly one terminal Chunk (ChunkDone or ChunkError). Streaming engines emit
196	// zero or more ChunkToken then one ChunkDone; non-streaming engines emit a
197	// single ChunkDone. This uniform "channel closed == finished" contract lets the
198	// TUI's self-resubscribing reader and the CLI's drain loop share one code path.
199	// The synchronous error return is only for immediate setup failures; all
200	// runtime/network errors flow as a terminal ChunkError.
201	type Engine interface {
202		Name() string
203		Translate(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Chunk, error)
204		Detect(ctx context.Context, text string) (string, error)
205		Available(ctx context.Context) bool
206		Supports(m Mode) bool
207	}
208	
209	// single is a helper for non-streaming engines: it returns a closed channel
210	// carrying exactly one terminal Chunk.
211	func single(res *TranslateResult, err error) <-chan Chunk {
212		ch := make(chan Chunk, 1)
213		if err != nil {
214			ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: err}
215		} else {
216			ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkDone, Result: res}
217		}
218		close(ch)
219		return ch
220	}
221	
222	// Drain consumes an engine channel to completion, returning the final result.
223	// It streams tokens to onToken (if non-nil) as they arrive. Used by the
224	// one-shot CLI path; the TUI drives the channel directly via its Update loop.
225	func Drain(ch <-chan Chunk, onToken func(string)) (*TranslateResult, error) {
226		for c := range ch {
227			switch c.Kind {
228			case ChunkToken:
229				if onToken != nil {
230					onToken(c.Text)
231				}
232			case ChunkDone:
233				return c.Result, nil
234			case ChunkError:
235				return nil, c.Err
236			}
237		}
238		return nil, ErrNoResult
239	}
240

123	const PROBE_DIRS = [
124	  join(homedir(), ".local", "bin"),
125	  "/opt/homebrew/bin",
126	  "/usr/local/bin",

130	let cachedBin: string | undefined;

132	/**
133	 * Resolve an ABSOLUTE path to the translate binary. Raycast runs under launchd
134	 * with a restricted PATH that does not inherit the shell rc, so a bare
135	 * `translate` throws ENOENT — we probe known install dirs (preference first).
136	 */
137	export function resolveBinary(): string {
138	  const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Prefs>();
139	  if (prefs.binaryPath && existsSync(prefs.binaryPath)) return prefs.binaryPath;
140	  if (cachedBin) return cachedBin;
141	  for (const dir of PROBE_DIRS) {
142	    const candidate = join(dir, "translate");
143	    if (existsSync(candidate)) {
144	      cachedBin = candidate;
145	      return candidate;
146	    }
147	  }
148	  throw new Error(
149	    "translate CLI not found. Set the binary path in extension preferences, or install it (just install / brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate).",
150	  );
151	}
152	
153	/** True when an error came from resolveBinary failing to locate the CLI. */
154	export function isBinaryMissing(e: unknown): boolean {
155	  return e instanceof Error && e.message.startsWith("translate CLI not found");
156	}
157	
158	function baseEnv(): NodeJS.ProcessEnv {
159	  // Ensure the CLI can locate its config.toml (providers/API keys) under launchd.
160	  return { ...process.env, HOME: process.env.HOME ?? homedir() };
161	}
162	
163	/**
164	 * Above this many UTF-8 bytes, text goes to the CLI on stdin instead of argv.
165	 *
166	 * macOS caps a whole argument list at ARG_MAX (1 MiB) and fails the spawn with
167	 * E2BIG — measured: 900 KB via argv works, 1.1 MB is "argument list too long".
168	 * The CLI reads stdin when it gets no text argument, and the pipe has no such
169	 * limit, so long documents take that route. The threshold leaves plenty of room
170	 * for multi-byte text (a CJK character is 3 bytes).
171	 */
172	const ARGV_SAFE_BYTES = 128 * 1024;
173	
174	function needsStdin(text: string): boolean {
175	  return Buffer.byteLength(text, "utf8") > ARGV_SAFE_BYTES;
176	}
177	
178	/**
179	 * How long to let a translation run, scaled to the input.
180	 *
181	 * A document-sized translation legitimately takes minutes — measured against
182	 * copilot-proxy: 10 KB of prose took 61 s, 20 KB took 96 s. A flat 60 s killed
183	 * exactly the long inputs Translate Text exists for. ~10 ms per character with a
184	 * 1-minute floor and a 10-minute ceiling (matching the CLI's own backstop).
185	 */
186	function requestTimeout(text: string): number {
187	  return Math.min(600_000, Math.max(60_000, text.length * 10));
188	}
189	
190	/**
191	 * Run the CLI with `input` written to stdin and no text argument, resolving with
192	 * stdout. Mirrors pexecFile's rejection shape (message + `stderr`) so callers
193	 * can keep inspecting stderr the same way.
194	 */
195	function execWithStdin(
196	  bin: string,
197	  args: string[],
198	  input: string,
199	  opts: { timeout?: number; signal?: AbortSignal } = {},
200	): Promise<string> {
201	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
202	    const child = spawn(bin, args, { env: baseEnv() });
203	    let out = "";
204	    let err = "";
205	    let settled = false;
206	
207	    const finish = (fn: () => void) => {
208	      if (settled) return;
209	      settled = true;
210	      clearTimeout(timer);
211	      opts.signal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
212	      fn();
213	    };
214	    const kill = (reason: string) =>
215	      finish(() => {
216	        if (!child.killed) child.kill("SIGTERM");
217	        reject(Object.assign(new Error(reason), { stderr: err }));
218	      });
219	    const onAbort = () => kill("aborted");
220	    const timer = opts.timeout
221	      ? setTimeout(
222	          () => kill(`timed out after ${opts.timeout}ms`),
223	          opts.timeout,
224	        )
225	      : (undefined as unknown as NodeJS.Timeout);
226	
227	    opts.signal?.addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true });
228	
229	    child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
230	    child.stderr?.setEncoding("utf8");
231	    child.stdout?.on("data", (d: string) => (out += d));
232	    child.stderr?.on("data", (d: string) => (err += d));
233	    child.on("error", (e) =>
234	      finish(() => reject(Object.assign(e, { stderr: err }))),
235	    );
236	    child.on("close", (code) =>
237	      finish(() =>
238	        code === 0
239	          ? resolve(out)
240	          : reject(
241	              Object.assign(
242	                new Error(`translate exited ${code}: ${err.trim()}`),
243	                {
244	                  stderr: err,
245	                },
246	              ),
247	            ),
248	      ),
249	    );
250	
251	    child.stdin?.on("error", () => {
252	      /* the child may exit before we finish writing — the close handler reports it */
253	    });
254	    child.stdin?.end(input, "utf8");
255	  });
256	}
257	
258	export interface TranslateOptions {
259	  to?: string;
260	  from?: string;
261	  engine?: string;
262	  tier?: string;
263	  /** Exact model id, overriding engine/tier selection. */
264	  model?: string;
265	  /**
266	   * Direction. Tri-state on purpose:
267	   *   undefined → leave it to the config ([general] pair)
268	   *   true      → --pair: detect and route between the pair languages
269	   *   false     → --no-pair: always translate into `to`
270	   *
271	   * This matters because [general] pair = true silently overrides --to for
272	   * home-language input, so "translate into X" is only true with --no-pair.
273	   */
274	  pair?: boolean;
275	  noHistory?: boolean;
276	  signal?: AbortSignal;
277	}
278	
279	/**
280	 * Turns a target + pair choice into CLI flags.
281	 *
282	 * AUTO_TARGET means "no --to at all": the CLI's own home target and pair_with
283	 * decide the direction. Anything else falls back to the Raycast preference, and
284	 * finally to nothing (letting the CLI config's default_target apply).
285	 */
286	function directionArgs(
287	  to: string | undefined,
288	  pair: boolean | undefined,
289	  prefTarget: string | undefined,
290	): { to?: string; pair?: boolean } {
291	  if (to === AUTO_TARGET) return { to: undefined, pair: true };
292	  return { to: to || prefTarget || undefined, pair };
293	}
294	
295	export async function runTranslate(
296	  text: string,
297	  opts: TranslateOptions = {},
298	): Promise<TranslateResult> {
299	  const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Prefs>();
300	  const bin = resolveBinary();
301	  const dir = directionArgs(opts.to, opts.pair, prefs.defaultTarget);
302	  const viaStdin = needsStdin(text);
303	  // With no text argument the CLI reads stdin, which sidesteps ARG_MAX.
304	  const args = viaStdin ? [] : [text];
305	  // In auto/pair mode we deliberately send no --to: the CLI's own home target
306	  // plus [general] pair_with decide the direction.

394	  if (opts.to) args.push("--to", opts.to);
395	  if (opts.noHistory) args.push("--no-history");

398	      timeout: 60_000,

413	/** True when `define` exited on a hard dictionary miss (no JSON was emitted). */

566	export interface StreamHandlers {

568	  onDone: (code: number | null) => void;

572	/**
573	 * Spawn `translate <text> --to <lang> [--engine] --stream` and stream plain-text
574	 * stdout chunks (the `--stream` flag forces streaming over a pipe). Returns a
575	 * cancel function that kills the child (call it on unmount). Whether output arrives
576	 * progressively depends on the provider — ollama streams; copilot-proxy buffers its
577	 * claude responses. `--no-history` avoids duplicating a history row the live view
578	 * may already have recorded.
579	 */
580	export function spawnTranslateStream(
581	  text: string,
582	  opts: TranslateOptions,
583	  h: StreamHandlers,
584	): () => void {
585	  const bin = resolveBinary();
586	  const dir = directionArgs(opts.to, opts.pair, undefined);
587	  const viaStdin = needsStdin(text);
588	  const args = viaStdin ? [] : [text];
589	  if (dir.to) args.push("--to", dir.to);
590	  args.push("--stream", "--no-history");
591	  if (dir.pair === true) args.push("--pair");
592	  if (dir.pair === false) args.push("--no-pair");
593	  if (opts.engine) args.push("--engine", opts.engine);
594	  if (opts.from) args.push("--from", opts.from);
595	  if (opts.tier) args.push("--tier", opts.tier);
596	  if (opts.model) args.push("--model", opts.model);
597	
598	  const child = spawn(bin, args, { env: baseEnv() });
599	  child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
600	  child.stdout?.on("data", (d: Buffer | string) => h.onData(d.toString()));
601	  child.on("close", (code) => h.onDone(code));
602	  child.on("error", (err) => h.onError(err));
603	  if (viaStdin) {
604	    child.stdin?.on("error", () => {
605	      /* reported via the close/error handlers above */
606	    });
607	    child.stdin?.end(text, "utf8");
608	  }
609	  return () => {
610	    if (!child.killed) child.kill("SIGTERM");
611	  };
612	}

1	import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
2	
3	/** Debounce a value so an expensive call only fires after the user pauses typing. */
4	export function useDebouncedValue<T>(value: T, delayMs: number): T {
5	  const [debounced, setDebounced] = useState(value);
6	  useEffect(() => {
7	    const id = setTimeout(() => setDebounced(value), delayMs);
8	    return () => clearTimeout(id);
9	  }, [value, delayMs]);
10	  return debounced;
11	}

21	// LLMConfig parameterizes an OpenAI-compatible backend (copilot-proxy, Ollama,

23	type LLMConfig struct {

29		// connection hanging a front-end, NOT to bound generation: a document-sized
30		// translation legitimately runs for minutes.
31		Timeout time.Duration

34	// LLMEngine talks to any OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint.
35	type LLMEngine struct {
36		cfg  LLMConfig
37		key  string

39	}
40	
41	// defaultRequestTimeout is the whole-request ceiling when the config sets none.
42	// Generous on purpose: it is a backstop for a wedged connection, and a
43	// document-sized translation legitimately takes minutes.
44	const defaultRequestTimeout = 10 * time.Minute
45	
46	// NewLLM builds an LLM engine, resolving the API key once from the environment.
47	func NewLLM(cfg LLMConfig) *LLMEngine {
48		if cfg.Timeout == 0 {
49			cfg.Timeout = defaultRequestTimeout
50		}
51		key := ""
52		if cfg.APIKeyEnv != "" {
53			key = strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(cfg.APIKeyEnv))
54		}
55		// No http.Client.Timeout, and no Transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout either.
56		//
57		// Client.Timeout covers the *entire* request including reading the body, so a
58		// streamed translation was cut off at exactly that deadline mid-sentence (see
59		// pitfalls/llm-stream-truncation-silently-rendered-as-complete.md).
60		// ResponseHeaderTimeout looks like the right replacement and is not:
61		// copilot-proxy buffers Claude /v1/messages responses and sends no headers
62		// until generation finishes, so a header deadline fails exactly the long
63		// documents this is meant to fix.
64		//
65		// The bound is the per-request context in Translate instead. Probes set their
66		// own short deadlines (Available 800ms, Models 4s) and are unaffected.
67		return &LLMEngine{cfg: cfg, key: key, http: &http.Client{}}
68	}

172	// answer. 1.5 tokens per input rune covers en→CJK, the expensive direction (CJK
173	// output runs close to one token per character).
174	func outputTokenBudget(text string, floor int) int {

235	func (e *LLMEngine) Translate(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Chunk, error) {
236		// A bilingual doc request carries its content in Segments, not Text.
237		if strings.TrimSpace(req.Text) == "" && !(req.Bilingual && len(req.Segments) > 0) {
238			return nil, ErrEmptyInput
239		}
240		model := NormalizeModelID(e.cfg.Model)

247		// they run past this function's return, so cancelling here would kill the
248		// stream immediately.
249		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, e.cfg.Timeout)
250		if isAnthropicModel(model) {

252		}
253		return e.translateOpenAI(ctx, req, cancel, model)
254	}

263			ID                 string   `json:"id"`
264			SupportedEndpoints []string `json:"supported_endpoints"`
265		} `json:"data"`
266	}
267	
268	// Models fetches the provider's model ids, keeping only those usable through the
269	// transports this engine speaks: OpenAI /chat/completions, or (for claude-*) the
270	// Anthropic /v1/messages endpoint. Ids needing only /responses are dropped.
271	func (e *LLMEngine) Models(ctx context.Context) ([]string, error) {
272		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 4*time.Second)
273		defer cancel()
274		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, e.endpoint("/models"), nil)
275		if err != nil {
276			return nil, err
277		}
278		e.auth(req)
279		resp, err := e.http.Do(req)
280		if err != nil {
281			return nil, err
282		}
283		defer resp.Body.Close()
284		if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
285			return nil, e.httpError(resp)
286		}
287		var mr modelsResponse
288		if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&mr); err != nil {
289			return nil, err
290		}
291		var out []string
292		for _, m := range mr.Data {
293			if usableModel(m.ID, m.SupportedEndpoints) {
294				out = append(out, m.ID)
295			}
296		}
297		sort.Strings(out)
298		return out, nil
299	}
300	
301	// usableModel reports whether a model id can be driven by this engine.
302	func usableModel(id string, endpoints []string) bool {
303		if isAnthropicModel(id) {
304			return true // routed via /v1/messages
305		}
306		for _, ep := range endpoints {
307			if ep == "/chat/completions" {
308				return true
309			}
310		}
311		// No endpoint metadata (e.g. Ollama) => assume chat-usable.
312		return len(endpoints) == 0
313	}
314	
315	// finalize builds the terminal result from the accumulated translation text.
316	func (e *LLMEngine) finalize(full, model string, req Request) *TranslateResult {
317		res := &TranslateResult{
318			Translation: strings.TrimSpace(full),
319			Target:      req.Target,
320			Engine:      e.cfg.Name,
321			Model:       model,
322		}
323		// The plain-text prompt returns only the translation, so fill the detected
324		// source offline when the caller asked to auto-detect.
325		if src := strings.TrimSpace(req.Source); src == "" || src == "auto" {
326			res.DetectedSource = lang.Detect(req.Text)
327		}
328		return res
329	}
330	
331	// promptFor picks the (system, user) prompt pair for a request: the structured
332	// tutor prompt for learn mode, else the plain translate prompt.
333	func promptFor(req Request) (system, user string) {
334		switch {
335		case req.Bilingual:
336			return buildBilingualPrompt(req)
337		case req.Learn:
338			return buildLearnPrompt(req)
339		default:
340			return buildTranslatePrompt(req)
341		}
342	}
343	
344	// finalizeResult builds the terminal result, parsing structured learn output when
345	// the request asked for it.
346	func (e *LLMEngine) finalizeResult(full, model string, req Request) *TranslateResult {
347		switch {
348		case req.Bilingual:
349			return e.finalizeBilingual(full, model, req)
350		case req.Learn:
351			return e.finalizeLearn(full, model, req)
352		default:
353			return e.finalize(full, model, req)
354		}
355	}
356	
357	// finalizeLearn parses the model's structured JSON reply into a LearnResult. It is
358	// defensive — it strips a markdown fence and slices to the outermost object before
359	// unmarshalling — and on any failure falls back to the raw text as the translation
360	// (with a warning), so a malformed reply degrades gracefully instead of erroring.
361	// res.Target is set to the FOREIGN (away) language because res.Translation always
362	// holds the foreign sentence (the corrected sentence, or the translation).
363	func (e *LLMEngine) finalizeLearn(full, model string, req Request) *TranslateResult {
364		res := &TranslateResult{
365			Target: req.PairAway,
366			Engine: e.cfg.Name,
367			Model:  model,
368		}
369		if src := strings.TrimSpace(req.Source); src == "" || src == "auto" {
370			res.DetectedSource = lang.Detect(req.Text)
371		}
372		lr, err := parseLearn(full)
373		if err != nil {
374			res.Translation = strings.TrimSpace(full)
375			res.Warnings = append(res.Warnings, "learn: could not parse structured output — showing the raw reply")
376			return res
377		}
378		lr.Direction = learnDirection(req) // trust offline detection over the model's guess
379		if strings.TrimSpace(lr.Original) == "" {
380			lr.Original = req.Text
381		}
382		res.Learn = lr
383		if lr.Direction == "correct" && strings.TrimSpace(lr.Corrected) != "" {
384			res.Translation = strings.TrimSpace(lr.Corrected)
385		} else {
386			res.Translation = strings.TrimSpace(lr.Translation)
387		}
388		return res
389	}
390	
391	// parseLearn extracts and unmarshals a LearnResult from a model reply, returning an
392	// error when the JSON is absent/invalid or carries no main sentence.
393	func parseLearn(full string) (*LearnResult, error) {
394		var lr LearnResult
395		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(extractJSON(full)), &lr); err != nil {
396			return nil, err
397		}
398		if strings.TrimSpace(lr.Translation) == "" && strings.TrimSpace(lr.Corrected) == "" {
399			return nil, fmt.Errorf("learn: empty structured result")
400		}
401		return &lr, nil
402	}
403	
404	// finalizeBilingual parses the model's JSON reply (prose-segment number → translation)
405	// into TranslateResult.Bilingual. Defensive like finalizeLearn: on any parse failure
406	// it returns an empty result + a warning so the caller can fall back to per-block mode.
407	func (e *LLMEngine) finalizeBilingual(full, model string, req Request) *TranslateResult {
408		res := &TranslateResult{
409			Target: req.Target,
410			Engine: e.cfg.Name,
411			Model:  model,
412		}
413		m, err := parseBilingual(full)
414		if err != nil {
415			res.Warnings = append(res.Warnings, "bilingual: could not parse structured output")
416			return res
417		}
418		res.Bilingual = m
419		return res
420	}
421	
422	// parseBilingual extracts a {"<n>": "<translation>"} JSON object from a model reply
423	// and converts it to a map keyed by the integer segment number, ignoring non-numeric
424	// keys defensively.
425	func parseBilingual(full string) (map[int]string, error) {
426		var raw map[string]string
427		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(extractJSON(full)), &raw); err != nil {
428			return nil, err
429		}
430		out := make(map[int]string, len(raw))
431		for k, v := range raw {
432			n, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(k))
433			if err != nil {
434				continue
435			}
436			out[n] = v
437		}
438		if len(out) == 0 {
439			return nil, fmt.Errorf("bilingual: no numeric segment keys")
440		}
441		return out, nil
442	}
443	
444	// extractJSON returns the outermost JSON object in s, tolerating a surrounding
445	// markdown code fence or stray prose around it.
446	func extractJSON(s string) string {
447		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
448		if strings.HasPrefix(s, "```") { // strip ```json … ``` fence
449			if i := strings.IndexByte(s, '\n'); i >= 0 {
450				s = s[i+1:]
451			}
452			s = strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSpace(s), "```"))
453		}
454		start := strings.IndexByte(s, '{')
455		end := strings.LastIndexByte(s, '}')
456		if start >= 0 && end > start {
457			return s[start : end+1]
458		}
459		return s
460	}
461	
462	// markTruncated flags a result whose stream ended before the model finished, so
463	// the caller keeps the partial text but never treats it as a complete answer.
464	func markTruncated(res *TranslateResult) {
465		res.Truncated = true
466		res.Warnings = append(res.Warnings,
467			"output was cut off before completion (stream truncated) — press Enter to retry")
468	}

470	// translateOpenAI uses the OpenAI /chat/completions endpoint.
471	func (e *LLMEngine) translateOpenAI(ctx context.Context, req Request, cancel context.CancelFunc, model string) (<-chan Chunk, error) {
472		// Any early return here abandons the context, so release it now; the
473		// success path hands ownership to the goroutine below.
474		ok := false
475		defer func() {
476			if !ok {
477				cancel()
478			}
479		}()
480		system, user := promptFor(req)
481		stream := req.Stream && !req.Learn && !req.Bilingual // structured JSON output: parse at done
482		body := chatRequest{
483			Model: model,
484			Messages: []chatMessage{
485				{Role: "system", Content: system},
486				{Role: "user", Content: user},
487			},
488			Stream: stream,
489		}
490		buf, err := json.Marshal(body)
491		if err != nil {
492			return nil, err
493		}
494		httpReq, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, e.endpoint("/chat/completions"), bytes.NewReader(buf))
495		if err != nil {
496			return nil, err
497		}
498		httpReq.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
499		if stream {
500			httpReq.Header.Set("Accept", "text/event-stream")
501		}
502		e.auth(httpReq)
503	
504		ch := make(chan Chunk, 32) // buffered so a fast stream doesn't block on renders
505		ok = true
506		go func() {
507			defer cancel()
508			defer close(ch)
509			resp, err := e.http.Do(httpReq)
510			if err != nil {
511				ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", e.cfg.Name, err)}
512				return
513			}
514			defer resp.Body.Close()
515			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
516				ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: e.httpError(resp)}
517				return
518			}
519	
520			var full strings.Builder
521			complete := true
522			if stream {
523				var err error
524				complete, err = e.readSSE(ctx, resp.Body, ch, &full)
525				if err != nil {
526					ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: err}
527					return
528				}
529			} else {
530				var cr chatResponse
531				if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&cr); err != nil {
532					ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: fmt.Errorf("%s: decode response: %w", e.cfg.Name, err)}
533					return
534				}
535				if cr.Error != nil {
536					ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: fmt.Errorf("%s: %s", e.cfg.Name, cr.Error.Message)}
537					return
538				}
539				if len(cr.Choices) == 0 {
540					ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: fmt.Errorf("%s: empty response", e.cfg.Name)}
541					return
542				}
543				full.WriteString(cr.Choices[0].Message.Content)
544				complete = cr.Choices[0].FinishReason != "length" // "length" => hit the cap
545			}
546			res := e.finalizeResult(full.String(), model, req)
547			if !complete {
548				markTruncated(res)
549			}
550			ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkDone, Result: res}
551		}()
552		return ch, nil
553	}

557		// Any early return here abandons the context, so release it now; the

567		floor := anthropicMaxTokens

569			floor = learnMaxTokens

573			MaxTokens: outputTokenBudget(user, floor),
574			System:    system,
575			Messages:  []anthropicMessage{{Role: "user", Content: user}},
576			Stream:    stream,
577		}
578		buf, err := json.Marshal(body)
579		if err != nil {
580			return nil, err
581		}
582		httpReq, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodPost, e.endpoint("/messages"), bytes.NewReader(buf))
583		if err != nil {
584			return nil, err
585		}
586		httpReq.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
587		httpReq.Header.Set("anthropic-version", "2023-06-01")
588		if stream {
589			httpReq.Header.Set("Accept", "text/event-stream")
590		}
591		e.anthropicAuth(httpReq)
592	
593		ch := make(chan Chunk, 32)
594		ok = true
595		go func() {
596			defer cancel()
597			defer close(ch)
598			resp, err := e.http.Do(httpReq)
599			if err != nil {
600				ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", e.cfg.Name, err)}
601				return
602			}
603			defer resp.Body.Close()
604			if resp.StatusCode != http.StatusOK {
605				ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: e.httpError(resp)}
606				return
607			}
608	
609			var full strings.Builder
610			complete := true
611			if stream {
612				var err error
613				complete, err = e.readAnthropicSSE(ctx, resp.Body, ch, &full)
614				if err != nil {
615					ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: err}
616					return
617				}
618			} else {
619				var ar anthropicResponse
620				if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&ar); err != nil {
621					ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: fmt.Errorf("%s: decode response: %w", e.cfg.Name, err)}
622					return
623				}
624				if ar.Error != nil {
625					ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: fmt.Errorf("%s: %s", e.cfg.Name, ar.Error.Message)}
626					return
627				}
628				for _, c := range ar.Content {
629					if c.Type == "text" {
630						full.WriteString(c.Text)
631					}
632				}
633				complete = ar.StopReason != "max_tokens" // "max_tokens" => hit the cap
634			}
635			res := e.finalizeResult(full.String(), model, req)
636			if !complete {
637				markTruncated(res)
638			}
639			ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkDone, Result: res}
640		}()
641		return ch, nil

644	// anthropicAuth sets the Anthropic auth header (x-api-key, not Bearer). The
645	// copilot-proxy needs none, so an empty key yields no header.
646	func (e *LLMEngine) anthropicAuth(r *http.Request) {
647		if e.key != "" {
648			r.Header.Set("x-api-key", e.key)
649		}
650	}
651	
652	// readSSE parses an OpenAI-style event stream, emitting a ChunkToken per content
653	// delta and accumulating the full text into full. It reports complete=true only
654	// when the stream ended on a terminal marker ([DONE] or finish_reason=="stop");
655	// a stream that closes with no marker, or on finish_reason=="length", is treated
656	// as truncated so the caller can flag it rather than silently accept partial text.
657	func (e *LLMEngine) readSSE(ctx context.Context, r io.Reader, ch chan<- Chunk, full *strings.Builder) (bool, error) {
658		sc := bufio.NewScanner(r)
659		sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64<<10), 1<<20) // tolerate long SSE lines
660		sawDone := false
661		finish := ""
662		for sc.Scan() {
663			line := sc.Text()
664			if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "data:") {
665				continue
666			}
667			payload := strings.TrimSpace(line[len("data:"):])
668			if payload == "[DONE]" {
669				sawDone = true
670				break
671			}
672			var d streamDelta
673			if json.Unmarshal([]byte(payload), &d) != nil || len(d.Choices) == 0 {
674				continue
675			}
676			if fr := d.Choices[0].FinishReason; fr != nil && *fr != "" {
677				finish = *fr
678			}
679			tok := d.Choices[0].Delta.Content
680			if tok == "" {
681				continue
682			}
683			full.WriteString(tok)
684			select {
685			case ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkToken, Text: tok}:
686			case <-ctx.Done():
687				return false, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", e.cfg.Name, ctx.Err())
688			}
689		}
690		if err := sc.Err(); err != nil {
691			return false, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", e.cfg.Name, err)
692		}
693		complete := finish != "length" && (sawDone || finish == "stop")
694		return complete, nil
695	}
696	
697	// readAnthropicSSE parses an Anthropic Messages event stream, emitting a
698	// ChunkToken per text_delta and accumulating the full text into full. It reports
699	// complete=true only when a terminal marker arrived (a message_stop event, or a
700	// message_delta with a natural stop_reason); a stream that closes with neither,
701	// or on stop_reason=="max_tokens", is treated as truncated.
702	func (e *LLMEngine) readAnthropicSSE(ctx context.Context, r io.Reader, ch chan<- Chunk, full *strings.Builder) (bool, error) {
703		sc := bufio.NewScanner(r)
704		sc.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64<<10), 1<<20)
705		sawStop := false
706		stopReason := ""
707		for sc.Scan() {
708			line := sc.Text()
709			if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "data:") {
710				continue // ignore "event:" and blank lines
711			}
712			payload := strings.TrimSpace(line[len("data:"):])
713			if payload == "" {
714				continue
715			}
716			var ev anthropicStreamEvent
717			if json.Unmarshal([]byte(payload), &ev) != nil {
718				continue
719			}
720			if ev.Error != nil {
721				return false, fmt.Errorf("%s: %s", e.cfg.Name, ev.Error.Message)
722			}
723			switch ev.Type {
724			case "message_stop":
725				sawStop = true
726				continue
727			case "message_delta":
728				if ev.Delta.StopReason != "" {
729					stopReason = ev.Delta.StopReason
730				}
731				continue
732			}
733			if ev.Type != "content_block_delta" || ev.Delta.Type != "text_delta" || ev.Delta.Text == "" {
734				continue
735			}
736			full.WriteString(ev.Delta.Text)
737			select {
738			case ch <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkToken, Text: ev.Delta.Text}:
739			case <-ctx.Done():
740				return false, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", e.cfg.Name, ctx.Err())
741			}
742		}
743		if err := sc.Err(); err != nil {
744			return false, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", e.cfg.Name, err)
745		}
746		complete := stopReason != "max_tokens" &&
747			(sawStop || stopReason == "end_turn" || stopReason == "stop_sequence")
748		return complete, nil
749	}
750	
751	// httpError reads an error body (best effort) into a descriptive error.
752	func (e *LLMEngine) httpError(resp *http.Response) error {
753		b, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 2<<10))
754		msg := strings.TrimSpace(string(b))
755		if msg == "" {
756			msg = resp.Status
757		}
758		return fmt.Errorf("%s: http %d: %s", e.cfg.Name, resp.StatusCode, msg)
759	}

92	// toolError reports a tool-level failure as content (IsError), per the MCP spec —
93	// not as a protocol error — so the model can see what went wrong.
94	func toolError(err error) *mcp.CallToolResult {
95		return &mcp.CallToolResult{
96			IsError: true,
97			Content: []mcp.Content{&mcp.TextContent{Text: err.Error()}},
98		}
99	}
100	
101	func renderTranslation(res *engine.TranslateResult) string {
102		var b strings.Builder
103		b.WriteString(res.Translation)
104		if len(res.Alternatives) > 0 {
105			b.WriteString("\n\nAlternatives:")
106			for _, a := range res.Alternatives {
107				b.WriteString("\n- " + a)
108			}
109		}
110		if s := strings.TrimSpace(res.Notes); s != "" {
111			b.WriteString("\n\nNotes: " + s)
112		}
113		return strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
114	}
115	
116	func renderDefine(res *engine.TranslateResult) string {
117		d := res.Dictionary
118		if d == nil {
119			if len(res.Suggestions) > 0 {
120				return "No exact match. Did you mean: " + strings.Join(res.Suggestions, ", ")
121			}
122			return res.Translation
123		}
124		var b strings.Builder
125		b.WriteString(d.Word)
126		if d.Phonetic != "" {
127			b.WriteString("  " + d.Phonetic)
128		}
129		for _, m := range d.Meanings {
130			b.WriteString("\n" + m.PartOfSpeech)
131			for i, def := range m.Definitions {
132				if i >= 4 {
133					break
134				}
135				b.WriteString("\n  • " + def.Text)
136				if def.Example != "" {
137					b.WriteString("\n    \"" + def.Example + "\"")
138				}
139			}
140		}
141		return strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
142	}
143	
144	func renderHistory(recs []store.Record) string {
145		if len(recs) == 0 {
146			return "(no history)"
147		}
148		var b strings.Builder
149		for _, r := range recs {
150			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s → %s  [%s→%s]\n", r.Input, r.Output, r.SourceLang, r.TargetLang)
151		}
152		return strings.TrimSpace(b.String())
153	}

1	// Package mcpserver exposes the translate engine as an MCP (Model Context Protocol)
2	// server over stdio, so LLM hosts (Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor, …) can call
3	// translate/define/history as tools. It is a thin adapter over appcore.Service,
4	// built on the official Go MCP SDK.
5	//
6	// stdio is deliberate: the host spawns the binary and speaks newline-delimited
7	// JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout, so there is no port, no token, and history never
8	// crosses a network boundary. stdout is the JSON-RPC channel — callers must send
9	// any diagnostics to stderr.
10	package mcpserver
11	
12	import (
13		"context"
14	
15		"github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk/mcp"
16	
17		"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/appcore"
18		"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/engine"
19		"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/store"
20	)
21	
22	// Service is the subset of appcore.Service the MCP tools depend on.
23	// *appcore.Service satisfies it; tests inject a fake.
24	type Service interface {
25		Translate(ctx context.Context, p appcore.Params) (*engine.TranslateResult, error)
26		Define(ctx context.Context, word string) (*engine.TranslateResult, error)
27		HistoryRecent(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]store.Record, error)
28		HistorySearch(ctx context.Context, query string, limit int) ([]store.Record, error)
29	}
30	
31	// newServer builds the MCP server with the translate/define/history tools.
32	func newServer(svc Service, version string) *mcp.Server {
33		srv := mcp.NewServer(&mcp.Implementation{Name: "translate", Version: version}, nil)
34		mcp.AddTool(srv, &mcp.Tool{
35			Name:        "translate",
36			Description: "Translate text into a target language (faithful, register-aware).",
37		}, translateHandler(svc))
38		mcp.AddTool(srv, &mcp.Tool{
39			Name:        "define",
40			Description: "Look up the dictionary definition of a word or short term.",
41		}, defineHandler(svc))
42		mcp.AddTool(srv, &mcp.Tool{
43			Name:        "history",
44			Description: "List or fuzzy-search recent translation history.",
45		}, historyHandler(svc))
46		return srv
47	}
48	
49	// Serve runs the MCP server over stdio until the host closes the connection or ctx
50	// is cancelled.
51	func Serve(ctx context.Context, svc Service, version string) error {
52		return newServer(svc, version).Run(ctx, &mcp.StdioTransport{})
53	}
54

13	
14	// Service is the warm, transport-agnostic core: it builds the translate/define
15	// engines once at startup and holds the history store for the process lifetime.
16	// A single Service is safe to share across many goroutines — the engines are
17	// concurrency-safe and the store serializes its own writes.
18	//
19	// The Service deliberately never touches state.json (the CLI's remembered pair):
20	// a long-lived server must not fight the interactive CLI over that file.
21	type Service struct {
22		cfg      *config.Config
23		res      config.Resolved
24		trans    engine.Engine   // warm translate engine
25		define   engine.Engine   // warm define engine
26		search   engine.Searcher // headword search; nil when the dictionary is remote
27		store    store.Store     // shared history; nil when disabled / NoHistory
28		provider string          // resolved provider name (for per-request model overrides)
29	
30		source string // resolved default source (usually "auto")
31		home   string // resolved home target
32		away   string // resolved pair "away" language; "" when pair is off
33		pair   bool
34	}
35	
36	// Options tunes Service construction.
37	type Options struct {
38		NoHistory bool // do not open/record history
39	}
40	
41	// Params is one translation request. Empty fields fall back to the Service
42	// defaults resolved at startup; Pair is a tri-state (nil => use the default).
43	type Params struct {
44		Text         string
45		Source       string // "" => service default (usually "auto")
46		Target       string // "" => service home target
47		Preset       string // "" => service default
48		Instructions string // "" => service default
49		Model        string // "" => the warm engine's model
50		MaxAlts      int    // 0 => engine default
51		Pair         *bool  // nil => service default; non-nil overrides
52	}
53	
54	// NewService resolves config (flags empty, env honored) once, warms both engines,
55	// and opens the history store. It fails fast on a misconfigured provider, mirroring
56	// the CLI's guard in runRoot.
57	func NewService(cfg *config.Config, opt Options) (*Service, error) {
58		res := cfg.Resolve(config.Overrides{}, config.ModeCLI)
59		if res.Provider == nil && res.Engine != "auto" {
60			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no provider configured; check %s", config.Path())
61		}
62		trans, err := BuildEngine(res)
63		if err != nil {
64			return nil, err
65		}
66		def := DefineEngine(res, false, false)
67		st := openStore(cfg, opt.NoHistory)
68		return newService(cfg, res, trans, def, st), nil
69	}
70	
71	// newService assembles a Service from already-built parts. It is the unexported
72	// seam used by tests to inject stub engines and an in-memory store (no network).
73	func newService(cfg *config.Config, res config.Resolved, trans, def engine.Engine, st store.Store) *Service {
74		source, home, away, pair := resolveRouting(res)
75		provider := ""
76		if res.Provider != nil {
77			provider = res.Provider.Name
78		}
79		// The headword searcher is a capability of the offline dictionary, not of the
80		// resolved translate engine — build it from config so it works even when the
81		// engine is a plain LLM.
82		search, _ := DictSearcher(cfg)
83		return &Service{
84			cfg: cfg, res: res, trans: trans, define: def, search: search, store: st,
85			provider: provider, source: source, home: home, away: away, pair: pair,
86		}
87	}
88	
89	// resolveRouting fuzzy-resolves the source/target/pair-with languages the same way
90	// the CLI does (resolvePair + lang.Resolve), so "chinese" → "zh" etc.
91	func resolveRouting(res config.Resolved) (source, home, away string, pair bool) {
92		sm, _ := lang.Resolve(res.Source)
93		tm, _ := lang.Resolve(res.Target)
94		source, home = sm.Code, tm.Code
95		pair = res.Pair
96		if res.Pair {
97			pwm, _ := lang.Resolve(res.PairWith)
98			away = pwm.Code
99		}
100		return source, home, away, pair
101	}
102	
103	// Translate performs a non-streaming translation and records it in history.
104	func (s *Service) Translate(ctx context.Context, p Params) (*engine.TranslateResult, error) {
105		return s.translate(ctx, p, false, nil)
106	}
107	
108	// TranslateStream performs a streaming translation, delivering tokens to onToken
109	// as they arrive, and records the final result in history.
110	func (s *Service) TranslateStream(ctx context.Context, p Params, onToken func(string)) (*engine.TranslateResult, error) {
111		return s.translate(ctx, p, true, onToken)
112	}
113	
114	func (s *Service) translate(ctx context.Context, p Params, stream bool, onToken func(string)) (*engine.TranslateResult, error) {
115		req := s.buildRequest(p, stream)
116		ch, err := s.trans.Translate(ctx, req)
117		if err != nil {
118			return nil, err
119		}
120		res, err := engine.Drain(ch, onToken)
121		if err != nil {
122			return nil, err
123		}
124		s.record(ctx, res, req.Text, req.Source, req.Target)
125		return res, nil
126	}
127	
128	// buildRequest maps Params onto an engine.Request, mirroring the CLI's oneShot +
129	// EffectiveTarget so the API and CLI route identically.
130	func (s *Service) buildRequest(p Params, stream bool) engine.Request {
131		source := firstNonEmpty(p.Source, s.source)
132		home := firstNonEmpty(p.Target, s.home)
133		pair := s.pair
134		if p.Pair != nil {
135			pair = *p.Pair
136		}
137		target := EffectiveTarget(pair, home, s.away, p.Text)
138	
139		req := engine.Request{
140			Text:     p.Text,
141			Source:   source,
142			Target:   target,
143			Mode:     engine.ModeTranslate,
144			Stream:   stream,
145			MaxAlts:  p.MaxAlts,
146			Preset:   firstNonEmpty(p.Preset, s.res.Preset),
147			Extra:    firstNonEmpty(p.Instructions, s.res.Instructions),
148			Pair:     pair,
149			PairHome: home,
150			PairAway: s.away,
151		}
152		if p.Model != "" {
153			// Scope the override to the resolved provider so a copilot model id never
154			// leaks into an Ollama fallback (see engine.Request.ModelProvider).
155			req.Model = p.Model
156			req.ModelProvider = s.provider
157		}
158		return req
159	}
160	
161	// Define performs a dictionary/definition lookup (not recorded in history, matching
162	// the CLI's `translate define`).
163	func (s *Service) Define(ctx context.Context, word string) (*engine.TranslateResult, error) {
164		ch, err := s.define.Translate(ctx, engine.Request{Text: word, Mode: engine.ModeDict, Stream: false})
165		if err != nil {
166			return nil, err
167		}
168		return engine.Drain(ch, nil)
169	}
170	
171	// SearchDict returns ranked dictionary headword candidates for a partially-typed
172	// query. It reads local data only (no network, no LLM) and never records history
173	// — it is meant to back a type-ahead picker, where a keystroke must not become a
174	// history row.
175	//
176	// "Nothing found" is not an error; when no local dictionary is configured the
177	// result carries Source "none" plus a Notes hint.
178	func (s *Service) SearchDict(ctx context.Context, q string, limit int) (*engine.SearchResult, error) {
179		if s.search == nil {
180			return &engine.SearchResult{
181				Query:      q,
182				Candidates: []engine.Candidate{},
183				Source:     "none",
184				Notes:      `headword search needs the offline dictionary ([dict] source = "local")`,
185			}, nil
186		}
187		return s.search.Search(ctx, q, limit)
188	}
189	
190	// HistoryRecent returns up to limit history records, newest first (empty when
191	// history is disabled).
192	func (s *Service) HistoryRecent(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]store.Record, error) {
193		if s.store == nil {
194			return nil, nil
195		}
196		return s.store.Recent(ctx, limit)
197	}
198	
199	// HistorySearch fuzzy-searches history (empty when history is disabled).
200	func (s *Service) HistorySearch(ctx context.Context, query string, limit int) ([]store.Record, error) {
201		if s.store == nil {
202			return nil, nil
203		}
204		return s.store.Search(ctx, query, limit)
205	}
206	
207	// Close releases the history store.
208	func (s *Service) Close() error {
209		if s.store != nil {
210			return s.store.Close()
211		}
212		return nil
213	}
214	
215	// record persists a successful, complete result. Truncated results (a stream cut
216	// short) and empty-output results (a dictionary miss) are never recorded, so
217	// neither a partial translation nor a "did you mean" is cached as an answer.
218	func (s *Service) record(ctx context.Context, res *engine.TranslateResult, input, source, target string) {
219		if s.store == nil || !Recordable(res) {
220			return
221		}
222		_, _ = s.store.Add(ctx, ToRecord(res, input, source, target))
223	}
224	
225	// openStore opens the history store, or returns nil when history is disabled or
226	// suppressed. Unlike the CLI helper it stays silent on failure (the server logs
227	// separately); a nil store simply disables history for this process.
228	func openStore(cfg *config.Config, noHistory bool) store.Store {
229		if !cfg.History.Enabled || noHistory {
230			return nil
231		}
232		path := cfg.History.Path
233		if path == "" {
234			path = xdgpath.HistoryFile()
235		}
236		st, err := store.OpenJSONL(path)
237		if err != nil {
238			return nil
239		}
240		return st
241	}
242	
243	func firstNonEmpty(a, b string) string {
244		if a != "" {
245			return a
246		}
247		return b
248	}

20	  TranslateResult,

28	const ENGINES = [
29	  { title: "Auto (fallback chain)", value: "" },
30	  { title: "Google", value: "google" },
31	  { title: "Dictionary (offline)", value: "dict" },
32	  { title: "Copilot", value: "copilot" },
33	  { title: "Ollama", value: "ollama" },
34	];
35	
36	export default function Command(
37	  props: LaunchProps<{ launchContext?: { seed?: string; to?: string } }>,
38	) {
39	  // Use the generated manifest type rather than a hand-written interface: there
40	  // `prefill` is required, so any future drift between package.json's default and
41	  // this file becomes a compile error instead of a silent behaviour change.
42	  const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Preferences.Translate>();
43	  const ctx = props.launchContext;
44	  const prefDebounce = Number(prefs.liveDebounceMs);
45	  const [debounceMs, setDebounceMs] = useState(
46	    prefDebounce > 0 ? Math.max(250, prefDebounce) : 700,
47	  );
48	  const [text, setText] = useState(ctx?.seed ?? "");
49	  const [to, setTo] = useState(ctx?.to || prefs.defaultTarget || "");
50	  const [engine, setEngine] = useState("");
51	  const pair = usePair();
52	
53	  // Inherit the default target + debounce from the CLI config (~/.config/translate)
54	  // when the matching Raycast preference is empty. Falls back to "en"/700ms.
55	  useEffect(() => {
56	    if (to && prefs.liveDebounceMs) return; // nothing to inherit
57	    readConfig()
58	      .then((cfg) => {
59	        if (!to && cfg.general?.default_target)
60	          setTo(cfg.general.default_target);
61	        if (!prefs.liveDebounceMs && cfg.general?.debounce_ms)
62	          setDebounceMs(Math.max(250, cfg.general.debounce_ms));
63	      })
64	      .catch(() => {
65	        /* fall back to defaults */
66	      })
67	      .finally(() => setTo((t) => t || "en"));
68	  }, []);
69	
70	  // On first open, seed the input from the current selection (or clipboard), per the
71	  // "Prefill input from" preference — unless we were launched with a seed (from
72	  // Translate Selection). Empty when there's nothing to grab, so you can also type.
73	  //
74	  // The fallback must match package.json's default ("none"). Note that changing
75	  // that default does NOT reach an install that already stored a value — see
76	  // pitfalls/raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md.
77	  useEffect(() => {
78	    if (ctx?.seed) return;
79	    const mode = prefs.prefill ?? "none";
80	    if (mode === "none") return;
81	    (async () => {
82	      let seed = "";
83	      if (mode === "selection") {
84	        try {
85	          seed = (await getSelectedText()).trim();
86	        } catch {
87	          seed = "";
88	        }
89	      } else if (mode === "clipboard") {
90	        seed = ((await Clipboard.readText()) ?? "").trim();
91	      }
92	      if (seed) setText(seed);
93	    })();
94	  }, []);
95	
96	  // Only translate once the user pauses (debounce) and cancel superseded in-flight
97	  // calls (abortable) — so typing a phrase no longer fires an LLM call per keystroke.
98	  const debouncedText = useDebouncedValue(text, debounceMs);
99	  const abortable = useRef<AbortController>();
100	
101	  const { data, isLoading, error } = usePromise(
102	    async (
103	      q: string,
104	      target: string,
105	      eng: string,
106	    ): Promise<TranslateResult | undefined> => {
107	      const trimmed = q.trim();
108	      if (!trimmed) return undefined;
109	      return runTranslate(trimmed, {
110	        to: target,
111	        // A concrete language means "translate into this": without --no-pair,
112	        // [general] pair reroutes home-language input and quietly ignores it.
113	        pair: target === AUTO_TARGET ? undefined : false,
114	        engine: eng || undefined,
115	        signal: abortable.current?.signal,
116	      });
117	    },
118	    [debouncedText, to, engine],
119	    { abortable },
120	  );
121	
122	  // Keep the loading bar up while the typed text is still ahead of the debounced value.
123	  const pending =
124	    text.trim().length > 0 && text.trim() !== debouncedText.trim();
125	
126	  // A single-word typo routes to the dictionary and comes back with an empty
127	  // translation + fuzzy suggestions — surface them as "did you mean?".
128	  const showSuggestions =
129	    !!data && !data.translation && !!data.suggestions?.length;
130	
131	  return (
132	    <List
133	      isLoading={isLoading || pending}
134	      searchText={text}
135	      onSearchTextChange={setText}
136	      searchBarPlaceholder="Type text to translate…"
137	      isShowingDetail={!!data?.translation}
138	      searchBarAccessory={
139	        <LanguageDropdown value={to} onChange={setTo} auto={pair} />
140	      }
141	    >
142	      {error ? (
143	        isBinaryMissing(error) ? (
144	          <BinaryNotFound />
145	        ) : (
146	          <List.EmptyView
147	            icon={Icon.Warning}
148	            title="Translation failed"
149	            description={String(error.message ?? error)}
150	          />
151	        )
152	      ) : !data ? (
153	        <List.EmptyView
154	          icon={Icon.Globe}
155	          title="Translate"
156	          description="Enter text above and pick a language."
157	        />
158	      ) : showSuggestions ? (
159	        <DidYouMean suggestions={data.suggestions!} onPick={setText} />
160	      ) : data.translation ? (
161	        <List.Item
162	          title={data.translation}
163	          subtitle={data.engine}
164	          detail={
165	            <List.Item.Detail
166	              markdown={renderMarkdown(data)}
167	              metadata={renderMetadata(data)}
168	            />
169	          }
170	          actions={
171	            <ActionPanel>
172	              <Action.CopyToClipboard
173	                title="Copy Translation"
174	                content={data.translation}
175	              />
176	              <Action.Paste
177	                title="Paste Translation"
178	                content={data.translation}
179	              />
180	              <Action.Push
181	                title="Translate (streaming)"
182	                icon={Icon.Text}
183	                shortcut={{ modifiers: ["cmd"], key: "return" }}
184	                target={
185	                  <StreamView
186	                    text={debouncedText.trim()}
187	                    to={to}
188	                    pair={to === AUTO_TARGET ? undefined : false}
189	                    engine={engine}
190	                  />
191	                }
192	              />
193	              <Action.CopyToClipboard
194	                title="Copy Source Text"
195	                content={debouncedText.trim()}
196	                shortcut={{ modifiers: ["cmd"], key: "i" }}
197	              />
198	              <Action
199	                title="Speak"
200	                icon={Icon.SpeakerHigh}
201	                onAction={async () => {

236	  const lines = [r.translation, ""];

240	  if (r.warnings?.length)

1	import {

3	  getSelectedText,
4	  launchCommand,

6	  LaunchType,
7	  showHUD,
8	} from "@raycast/api";
9	
10	interface Args {
11	  to?: string;
12	}
13	
14	/**
15	 * Grab the current selection (or clipboard) and open the editable Translate view
16	 * prefilled with it — rather than translating and pasting blind. Falls back to the
17	 * clipboard, and to an empty Translate when there's nothing to grab. An optional
18	 * `to` argument seeds the target language.
19	 */
20	export default async function Command(props: LaunchProps<{ arguments: Args }>) {
21	  let seed = "";
22	  try {
23	    seed = (await getSelectedText()).trim();
24	  } catch {
25	    // No selection / app doesn't expose it — fall back to the clipboard.
26	    seed = ((await Clipboard.readText()) ?? "").trim();
27	  }
28	
29	  try {
30	    await launchCommand({
31	      name: "translate",
32	      type: LaunchType.UserInitiated,
33	      context: { seed, to: props.arguments?.to || undefined },
34	    });
35	  } catch (e) {
36	    await showHUD(
37	      `Couldn't open Translate: ${String((e as Error).message ?? e)}`,
38	    );
39	  }
40	}

14	export default function Command() {
15	  const [word, setWord] = useState("");
16	  const debounced = useDebouncedValue(word, 500);
17	  const abortable = useRef<AbortController>();
18	
19	  const { data, isLoading, error } = usePromise(
20	    async (w: string): Promise<TranslateResult | undefined> => {
21	      const trimmed = w.trim();
22	      if (!trimmed) return undefined;
23	      // Type-to-lookup fires on every debounced keystroke, so it must not record:
24	      // history belongs to Look Up Word, where you explicitly open a word.
25	      return runDefine(trimmed, {
26	        noHistory: true,
27	        signal: abortable.current?.signal,
28	      });
29	    },
30	    [debounced],
31	    { abortable },
32	  );
33	
34	  const pending = word.trim().length > 0 && word.trim() !== debounced.trim();
35	  const showSuggestions =
36	    !!data && !data.dictionary && !!data.suggestions?.length;
37	
38	  return (
39	    <List
40	      isLoading={isLoading || pending}
41	      searchText={word}
42	      onSearchTextChange={setWord}
43	      searchBarPlaceholder="Look up a word…"
44	      isShowingDetail={!!data && !showSuggestions}
45	    >
46	      {error ? (
47	        isBinaryMissing(error) ? (
48	          <BinaryNotFound />
49	        ) : (
50	          <List.EmptyView
51	            icon={Icon.Warning}
52	            title="Lookup failed"
53	            description={String(error.message ?? error)}
54	          />
55	        )
56	      ) : !data ? (
57	        <List.EmptyView
58	          icon={Icon.Book}
59	          title="Define"
60	          description="Type a word to look it up."
61	        />
62	      ) : showSuggestions ? (
63	        <DidYouMean suggestions={data.suggestions!} onPick={setWord} />
64	      ) : (
65	        <List.Item
66	          title={data.dictionary?.word ?? word}
67	          subtitle={data.engine}
68	          detail={
69	            <List.Item.Detail
70	              markdown={renderDefine(data, word)}
71	              metadata={renderMetadata(data)}
72	            />
73	          }
74	          actions={
75	            <ActionPanel>
76	              <Action.CopyToClipboard
77	                title="Copy Definition"
78	                content={data.translation}
79	              />
80	              <Action.CopyToClipboard
81	                title="Copy Word"
82	                content={data.dictionary?.word ?? word}
83	                shortcut={{ modifiers: ["cmd"], key: "i" }}
84	              />
85	              <Action
86	                title="Speak"
87	                icon={Icon.SpeakerHigh}
88	                onAction={async () => {
89	                  speak(
90	                    data.dictionary?.word ?? word.trim(),
91	                    data.target || "en",
92	                  );
93	                  await showHUD("Speaking…");
94	                }}
95	              />
96	            </ActionPanel>
97	          }
98	        />
99	      )}
100	    </List>
101	  );
102	}
103	
104	function renderDefine(r: TranslateResult, word: string): string {
105	  const d = r.dictionary;
106	  if (d) {
107	    const lines = [`# ${d.word}`];
108	    if (d.phonetic) lines.push(`*/${d.phonetic}/*`);
109	    lines.push("");
110	    for (const m of d.meanings ?? []) {
111	      lines.push(`## ${m.part_of_speech}`);
112	      for (const def of m.definitions ?? []) {
113	        lines.push(
114	          `- ${def.definition}${def.example ? `\n  - _${def.example}_` : ""}`,
115	        );
116	      }
117	      lines.push("");
118	    }
119	    return lines.join("\n");
120	  }
121	  // No dictionary entry — LLM fallback lives in `translation`.
122	  const lines = [`# ${word}`, "", r.translation, ""];
123	  if (r.warnings?.length) lines.push("---", ...r.warnings.map((w) => `> ${w}`));
124	  return lines.join("\n");
125	}

132	        <List.Item.Detail.Metadata.Label

134	          text={r.dictionary.phonetic}

136	      ) : null}
137	      {r.model ? (

139	      ) : null}

143	          target={r.dictionary.source_url}

297	/**
298	 * History rows worth showing next to live results: the ones whose input or output
299	 * contains what was typed. Already in memory, so this costs nothing.
300	 */
301	function matchingHistory(entries: HistoryEntry[], q: string): HistoryEntry[] {
302	  const needle = q.toLowerCase();
303	  return entries
304	    .filter(
305	      (h) =>
306	        h.input.toLowerCase().includes(needle) ||
307	        h.output.toLowerCase().includes(needle),
308	    )
309	    .slice(0, HISTORY_WITH_RESULTS);
310	}

312	/** Pull the `translate …` command out of a notes hint, for the copy action. */
313	function commandFromNotes(notes: string): string {
314	  const m = notes.match(/`([^`]+)`/);
315	  return m ? m[1] : notes;
316	}

16	export function useLanguages(): LangInfo[] {

19	  );

30	/** The configured pair, or null when [general] pair_with isn't set. */
31	export interface PairInfo {
32	  home: string;
33	  away: string;
34	  /** Whether [general] pair is on, i.e. whether this is already the default. */
35	  enabled: boolean;
36	}
37	
38	/**
39	 * Reads the configured bidirectional pair, so a target picker can offer "Auto"
40	 * with real language codes in its label instead of a vague word.
41	 */
42	export function usePair(): PairInfo | null {
43	  const [pair, setPair] = useState<PairInfo | null>(null);
44	  useEffect(() => {
45	    readConfig()
46	      .then((cfg) => {
47	        const g = cfg.general;
48	        if (g?.pair_with && g.default_target) {
49	          setPair({
50	            home: g.default_target,
51	            away: g.pair_with,
52	            enabled: !!g.pair,
53	          });
54	        }
55	      })
56	      .catch(() => {
57	        /* no pair offered */
58	      });
59	  }, []);
60	  return pair;
61	}
62	
63	/** The label for the Auto entry, e.g. "Auto — zh-TW ⇄ en". */
64	export function autoLabel(pair: PairInfo | null): string {
65	  return pair
66	    ? `Auto — ${pair.home} ⇄ ${pair.away}`
67	    : "Auto (detect direction)";
68	}
69	
70	/**
71	 * Target-language picker with an "Auto" entry — the dropdown equivalent of the
72	 * TUI's ^g.
73	 *
74	 * Auto is not cosmetic. With [general] pair = true the CLI already reroutes
75	 * home-language input to pair_with, so picking "Chinese" and pasting Chinese
76	 * gives you English. Making Auto explicit means picking a language can mean what
77	 * it says: a concrete choice sends --no-pair and always translates *into* it.
78	 */
79	export function LanguageDropdown(props: {

99	          value={AUTO_TARGET}
100	          keywords={["auto", "pair", "bidirectional"]}
101	        />
102	      ) : null}
103	      {!known && props.value ? (
104	        <List.Dropdown.Item title={props.value} value={props.value} />
105	      ) : null}
106	      {langs.map((l) => (
107	        <List.Dropdown.Item

109	          title={`${l.name} (${l.code})`}
110	          value={l.code}
111	        />
112	      ))}
113	    </List.Dropdown>

128	// invocationMode reports whether this run is the one-shot CLI (arguments or piped
129	// stdin) or the interactive TUI (a TTY with no arguments). It mirrors the dispatch
130	// switch in runRoot and is computed before Resolve so the [cli]/[tui] overlay applies.
131	func invocationMode(args []string) config.Mode {
132		if len(args) > 0 {
133			return config.ModeCLI
134		}
