143	
144		cfg, created, err := config.Load()
145		if err != nil {
146			return err
147		}
148		if created {
149			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: wrote default config to %s (run `translate init` to customize)\n", config.Path())
150		} else if cfg.Outdated() {
151			// Schema bumps so far are additive: Load already filled any new fields with
152			// their Default() values in memory, so re-saving materializes them on disk
153			// (every existing value preserved) and re-stamps the schema — no wizard
154			// needed. A genuinely breaking change would instead need an explicit
155			// migration here before the re-save.
156			from := cfg.Schema
157			if err := config.Save(cfg); err != nil {
158				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: config is outdated but auto-upgrade failed (%v) — run `translate init`\n", err)
159			} else {
160				fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: upgraded config schema v%d→v%d (new settings use defaults; `translate init` to review)\n", from, config.SchemaVersion)
161			}
162		}
163	
164		res := cfg.Resolve(overrides(), invocationMode(args))
165		if res.Debug {
166			// The one-shot CLI logs to stderr; the TUI logs to a file, since its
167			// alt-screen would be corrupted by stderr writes.
168			if invocationMode(args) == config.ModeCLI {
169				debug.Enable(os.Stderr)
170			} else if w := openDebugLog(); w != nil {
171				debug.Enable(w)
172			}
173		}
174		applyLastPair(cfg, &res) // remember_last_pair: seed source/target from state
175		src, tgt := resolvePair(res.Source, res.Target)
176		pairWith := ""
177		if res.Pair {
178			pwm, _ := lang.Resolve(res.PairWith)
179			pairWith = pwm.Code
180		}
181		// Learn mode is bidirectional; ensure a distinct "away" (foreign) language so
182		// direction routing has two sides to choose between.
183		if res.Learn && (pairWith == "" || strings.EqualFold(pairWith, tgt)) {
184			pairWith = defaultAway(tgt)
185		}
186		debug.Logf("resolved: engine=%s tier=%s preset=%s source=%s target=%s pair=%v pair_with=%s learn=%v",
187			res.Engine, res.Tier, res.Preset, src, tgt, res.Pair, pairWith, res.Learn)
188		if res.Pair && !res.Learn && (pairWith == "" || strings.EqualFold(pairWith, tgt)) {
189			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: warning: pair mode is on but pair-with (%q) equals the target (%q) — pair mode is a no-op; set a different pair_with (run `translate init`)\n", pairWith, tgt)
190		}
191	
192		if res.Provider == nil && res.Engine != "auto" {
193			return fmt.Errorf("no provider configured; check %s", config.Path())
194		}
195		eng, err := appcore.BuildEngine(res)
196		if err != nil {
197			return err
198		}
199	
200		// The one-shot CLI path routes a learn request through a bare LLM engine
201		// (bypassing smart-auto/dictionary); the TUI keeps its normal primary engine and
202		// toggles learn at runtime against Params.LearnEngine.
203		learnCLI := res.Learn && invocationMode(args) == config.ModeCLI
204		if learnCLI && res.Provider == nil {
205			return fmt.Errorf("learn mode requires an LLM provider; check %s", config.Path())
206		}
207		oneShotEng := eng
208		if learnCLI {
209			oneShotEng = appcore.LearnEngineFromConfig(res)
210		}
211	
212		st := openStore(cfg)
213		if st != nil {
214			defer st.Close()
215		}
216	
217		switch {
218		case len(args) > 0:
219			text := strings.Join(args, " ")
220			effTgt := appcore.EffectiveTarget(res.Pair, tgt, pairWith, text)
221			r, err := oneShot(ctx, oneShotEng, text, src, effTgt, res.Stream, res.Preset, res.Instructions, res.Pair, tgt, pairWith, res.Learn)
222			if err != nil {
223				return err
224			}
225			recordAndRemember(ctx, st, cfg, r, text, src, effTgt, tgt)
226			if shouldSpeak(cfg) {
227				speakResult(ctx, cfg, r, text, src, effTgt, speakForeign(cfg, pairWith))
228			}
229			return nil
230	
231		case !term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stdin.Fd())):
232			b, err := io.ReadAll(os.Stdin)
233			if err != nil {
234				return err
235			}
236			// Strip ANSI/SGR escapes so colored piped input (e.g. `tldr rg | translate`)
237			// never pollutes the prompt. The raw bytes are retained only for --bilingual,
238			// which needs the original styling for display.
239			text := strings.TrimSpace(bitext.Strip(string(b)))
240			if text == "" {
241				return fmt.Errorf("no input on stdin")
242			}
243			// Bilingual is a multi-block reading view; --json/--learn keep their own
244			// structured output and take precedence.
245			if flagBilingual && !flagJSON && !res.Learn {
246				// doc mode needs an LLM (structured JSON, empty Text confuses
247				// smartauto/chain routing) — build a bare LLM like learn mode; nil when
248				// no provider, in which case runBilingual falls back to per-block.
249				var docEng engine.Engine
250				if res.Provider != nil {
251					docEng = appcore.LearnEngineFromConfig(res)
252				}
253				return runBilingual(ctx, oneShotEng, docEng, string(b), src, tgt, res.Instructions, flagBilingualMode)
254			}
255			effTgt := appcore.EffectiveTarget(res.Pair, tgt, pairWith, text)
256			r, err := oneShot(ctx, oneShotEng, text, src, effTgt, res.Stream, res.Preset, res.Instructions, res.Pair, tgt, pairWith, res.Learn)
257			if err != nil {
258				return err
259			}
260			recordAndRemember(ctx, st, cfg, r, text, src, effTgt, tgt)
261			if shouldSpeak(cfg) {
262				speakResult(ctx, cfg, r, text, src, effTgt, speakForeign(cfg, pairWith))
263			}
264			return nil
265	
266		default:
267			return runTUI(ctx, eng, res, st, src, tgt, pairWith)
268		}
269	}
270	
271	// openDebugLog opens (append) the TUI debug log file, creating the state dir.
272	// Returns nil on failure (debug simply stays off).
273	func openDebugLog() io.Writer {
274		if err := xdgpath.EnsureDirs(); err != nil {
275			return nil
276		}
277		f, err := os.OpenFile(filepath.Join(xdgpath.StateDir(), "debug.log"),
278			os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY|os.O_APPEND, 0o600)
279		if err != nil {
280			return nil
281		}
282		return f
283	}
284	
285	// applyLastPair overrides the resolved source/target with the persisted last
286	// pair when remember_last_pair is on and the user did not pass flags/env.
287	func applyLastPair(cfg *config.Config, res *config.Resolved) {
288		if !cfg.General.RememberLastPair {
289			return
290		}
291		// Pair (and learn) mode anchors BOTH languages from config: Target is the home
292		// language, PairWith is the away language, and routing is decided per input. A
293		// remembered target must not override the home here — if the last session
294		// happened to translate into the away language, restoring it as the home makes
295		// home == away and pair mode collapses to a no-op (the "en⇄en" bug). Source is
296		// always auto-detected in pair mode too, so skip the whole override.
297		if res.Pair {
298			debug.Logf("remember_last_pair: skipped (pair mode anchors languages from config)")
299			return
300		}
301		stt, err := state.Load()
302		if err != nil || stt == nil {
303			return
304		}
305		if flagFrom == "" && os.Getenv("TRANSLATE_SOURCE") == "" && stt.Source != "" {
306			res.Source = stt.Source
307			debug.Logf("remember_last_pair: source ← %s (from state)", stt.Source)
308		}
309		if flagTo == "" && os.Getenv("TRANSLATE_TARGET") == "" && stt.Target != "" {
310			res.Target = stt.Target
311			debug.Logf("remember_last_pair: target ← %s (from state)", stt.Target)
312		}
313	}
314	
315	// openStore opens the history store, or returns nil when history is disabled or
316	// suppressed with --no-history.
317	func openStore(cfg *config.Config) store.Store {
318		if !cfg.History.Enabled || flagNoHistory {
319			return nil
320		}
321		path := cfg.History.Path
322		if path == "" {
323			path = xdgpath.HistoryFile()
324		}
325		st, err := store.OpenJSONL(path)
326		if err != nil {
327			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: history disabled (%v)\n", err)
328			return nil
329		}
330		return st
331	}
332	
333	// recordAndRemember writes the translation to history and persists the last pair.
334	//
335	// target is the effective target actually used (for history); rememberTarget is
336	// the stable home target (== target unless pair mode redirected this one input),
337	// so persisting it keeps pair mode from drifting its home to the away language.
338	func recordAndRemember(ctx context.Context, st store.Store, cfg *config.Config, res *engine.TranslateResult, input, source, target, rememberTarget string) {
339		if st != nil && appcore.Recordable(res) {
340			_, _ = st.Add(ctx, appcore.ToRecord(res, input, source, target))
341		}
342		if cfg.General.RememberLastPair {
343			saveLastPair(source, rememberTarget, res.Engine)
344		}
345	}
346	
347	// saveLastPair persists the source/target pair and source mode.
348	func saveLastPair(source, target, engineName string) {
349		mode := "fixed"
350		if source == "auto" {
351			mode = "auto"
352		}
353		_ = state.Save(&state.State{
354			Source:     source,
355			Target:     target,
356			SourceMode: mode,
357			Engine:     engineName,
358		})
359	}
360	
361	// runTUI launches the interactive Bubble Tea front-end and persists the last
362	// pair on exit.
363	func runTUI(ctx context.Context, eng engine.Engine, res config.Resolved, st store.Store, source, target, pairWith string) error {
364		// A model source for the ^p model picker: the resolved LLM provider (if any).
365		var modelSrc engine.ModelLister
366		modelProvider := ""
367		if res.Provider != nil {
368			modelSrc = appcore.LLMFromProvider(res.Provider, res.Model)
369			modelProvider = res.Provider.Name
370		}
371		// Learn mode (^n) runs against a bare LLM engine; nil when no provider is
372		// configured, in which case the toggle refuses.
373		var learnEng engine.Engine
374		if res.Provider != nil {
375			learnEng = appcore.LearnEngineFromConfig(res)
376		}
377		p := tui.Params{
378			Engines:       buildEngineSet(res, eng),
379			ModelSource:   modelSrc,
380			ModelProvider: modelProvider,
381			Store:         st,
382			Source:        source,
383			Target:        target,
384			Pair:          res.Pair,
385			PairWith:      pairWith,
386			Learn:         res.Learn,
387			LearnEngine:   learnEng,
388			Model:         res.Model,
389			Preset:        res.Preset,
390			Instructions:  res.Instructions,
391			Live:          res.LiveTranslate,
392			DebounceMs:    res.DebounceMs,
393			Speaker:       tuiSpeaker(res.Cfg),
394			Foreign:       speakForeign(res.Cfg, pairWith),
395		}
396		final, err := tea.NewProgram(tui.New(ctx, p), tea.WithContext(ctx)).Run()
397		if err != nil {
398			return err
399		}
400		if res.Cfg.General.RememberLastPair {
401			if fm, ok := final.(tui.Model); ok {
402				s, t := fm.Pair()
403				saveLastPair(s, t, "")
404			}
405		}
406		return nil
407	}
408	
409	// resolvePair fuzzy-resolves the source and target languages, printing an
410	// "(interpreted X as Y)" note on stderr when a fuzzy correction was applied.
411	func resolvePair(rawSource, rawTarget string) (source, target string) {
412		sm, _ := lang.Resolve(rawSource)
413		tm, _ := lang.Resolve(rawTarget)
414		if !sm.Exact && sm.Score > 0 && !strings.EqualFold(rawSource, sm.Code) {
415			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: interpreted source %q as %s (%s)\n", rawSource, sm.Code, sm.Name)
416		}
417		if !tm.Exact && tm.Score > 0 && !strings.EqualFold(rawTarget, tm.Code) {
418			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: interpreted target %q as %s (%s)\n", rawTarget, tm.Code, tm.Name)
419		}
420		return sm.Code, tm.Code
421	}
422	
423	// oneShot translates text once and prints the result, returning it for history.
424	//
425	// Tokens stream live to stdout only when stdout is a TTY (so `translate x | pbcopy`
426	// stays clean) and --json was not requested. Piped output is the plain translation
427	// with no ANSI; --json emits the full structured result.
428	func oneShot(ctx context.Context, eng engine.Engine, text, source, target string, streamPref bool, preset, instructions string, pair bool, pairHome, pairAway string, learn bool) (*engine.TranslateResult, error) {
429		stdoutTTY := term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stdout.Fd()))
430		// Stream when the config asks for it on a TTY, or when --stream forces it (a
431		// piped consumer like the Raycast extension). --json/--learn are structured
432		// and never stream.
433		stream := (flagStream || (streamPref && stdoutTTY)) && !flagJSON && !learn
434	
435		req := engine.Request{
436			Text:     text,
437			Source:   source,
438			Target:   target,
439			Mode:     engine.ModeTranslate,
440			Stream:   stream,
441			Preset:   preset,
442			Extra:    instructions,
443			Pair:     pair,
444			PairHome: pairHome,
445			PairAway: pairAway,
446			Learn:    learn,
447		}
448		ch, err := eng.Translate(ctx, req)
449		if err != nil {
450			return nil, err
451		}
452	
453		// streamed tracks whether any visible token actually reached stdout. We may
454		// request streaming (stream == true) yet the engine that answers ignores it and
455		// returns a single terminal result with zero tokens — every non-streaming engine
456		// does (the dictionary/smart-dict single-word path, google, a provider that fell
457		// back to a non-streaming completion). In that case nothing was printed during
458		// draining, so the final result must still be emitted below.
459		var onTok func(string)
460		streamed := false
461		if stream {
462			onTok = func(t string) {
463				if t != "" {
464					streamed = true
465				}
466				fmt.Print(t)
467			}
468		}
469		res, err := engine.Drain(ch, onTok)
470		if err != nil {
471			if streamed {
472				fmt.Println() // terminate any partial streamed line before the error surfaces
473			}
474			return nil, err
475		}
476	
477		// Never downgrade silently: if the auto-chain fell back, say which engine
478		// failed and why, and how to switch.
479		for _, w := range res.Warnings {
480			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: warning: %s\n", w)
481		}
482		if len(res.Warnings) > 0 && res.Learn == nil {
483			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: used %q (switch with --engine, or check the model/provider)\n", res.Engine)
484		}
485	
486		switch {
487		case flagJSON:
488			enc := json.NewEncoder(os.Stdout)
489			enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
490			if err := enc.Encode(res); err != nil {
491				return nil, err
492			}
493		case res.Learn != nil:
494			fmt.Print(renderLearnCLI(res))
495		case streamed:
496			fmt.Println() // newline after the streamed tokens
497		default:
498			// Piped output, or a non-streaming engine answered a stream request with no
499			// tokens (dictionary single-word, google, …): emit the full result now.
500			fmt.Println(res.Translation)
501		}
502		return res, nil
503	}
504	
505	// runBilingual renders the "immersive" bilingual view for piped input: every
506	// original block is printed verbatim (ANSI/color intact) and a translation is shown
507	// beneath each prose block; indented command/code blocks are echoed untranslated.
508	// mode "doc" (default) translates the whole document in one context-aware call via
509	// docEng (a bare LLM); "blocks" (or a doc-mode fallback) translates each prose block
510	// in isolation via blockEng. Pair and learn routing are out of scope for this view.
511	func runBilingual(ctx context.Context, blockEng, docEng engine.Engine, raw, source, target, instructions, mode string) error {
512		blocks := bitext.Split(raw)
513		if len(blocks) == 0 {
514			return fmt.Errorf("no input on stdin")
515		}
516	
517		var translations map[int]string
518		switch mode {
519		case "blocks":
520			translations = bilingualBlocks(ctx, blockEng, blocks, source, target, instructions)
521		default: // "doc"
522			if docEng != nil {
523				if t, ok := bilingualDoc(ctx, docEng, blocks, source, target, instructions); ok {
524					translations = t
525				}
526			}
527			if translations == nil { // no LLM provider, or the doc call failed/was unparseable
528				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "translate: bilingual: doc mode unavailable, using per-block")
529				translations = bilingualBlocks(ctx, blockEng, blocks, source, target, instructions)
530			}
531		}
532	
533		dim := dimFunc(term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stdout.Fd())))
534		fmt.Print(bitext.Render(blocks, translations, dim))
535		return nil
536	}
537	
538	// bilingualBlocks translates each prose block in isolation (concurrent, bounded).
539	// The original strategy: works with any engine, but has no cross-block context.
540	func bilingualBlocks(ctx context.Context, eng engine.Engine, blocks []bitext.Block, source, target, instructions string) map[int]string {
541		translations := make(map[int]string)
542		errs := make(map[int]error)
543		var mu sync.Mutex
544		var wg sync.WaitGroup
545		sem := make(chan struct{}, 5) // bound concurrent LLM calls
546	
547		for i, blk := range blocks {
548			if blk.Kind != bitext.Prose {
549				continue
550			}
551			wg.Add(1)
552			go func(i int, plain string) {
553				defer wg.Done()
554				sem <- struct{}{}
555				defer func() { <-sem }()
556	
557				// Force concise (Stream:false, Preset:"") so each block maps to exactly
558				// one translation — contextual/dictionary presets would reshape output.
559				r, err := translateOnce(ctx, eng, engine.Request{
560					Text:   plain,
561					Source: source,
562					Target: target,
563					Mode:   engine.ModeTranslate,
564					Extra:  instructions,
565				})
566				mu.Lock()
567				defer mu.Unlock()
568				if err != nil {
569					errs[i] = err
570					return
571				}
572				tr := strings.TrimSpace(r.Translation)
573				// Drop echoes (proper nouns / already-target text): nothing to add beneath.
574				if tr != "" && !strings.EqualFold(tr, strings.TrimSpace(plain)) {
575					translations[i] = tr
576				}
577			}(i, blk.Plain)
578		}
579		wg.Wait()
580	
581		// Never fail silently: report untranslated blocks (originals still printed).
582		if len(errs) > 0 {
583			var sample error
584			for _, e := range errs {
585				sample = e
586				break
587			}
588			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: warning: %d block(s) not translated (%v)\n", len(errs), sample)
589		}
590		return translations
591	}
592	
593	// bilingualDoc translates the whole document in ONE context-aware structured call:
594	// the model sees every block (prose + code as context) and returns a JSON map of
595	// prose-segment number → translation. Returns ok=false when structured output isn't
596	// available (no LLM, error, or unparseable/empty reply) so the caller falls back.
597	func bilingualDoc(ctx context.Context, eng engine.Engine, blocks []bitext.Block, source, target, instructions string) (map[int]string, bool) {
598		var segs []engine.Segment
599		proseBlock := make(map[int]int) // prose-segment number (1-based) → block index
600		n := 0
601		for i, blk := range blocks {
602			switch blk.Kind {
603			case bitext.Prose:
604				n++
605				proseBlock[n] = i
606				segs = append(segs, engine.Segment{Text: blk.Plain})
607			case bitext.Code:
608				segs = append(segs, engine.Segment{Text: blk.Plain, Code: true})
609			}
610		}
611		if n == 0 {
612			return map[int]string{}, true // nothing to translate
613		}
614	
615		r, err := translateOnce(ctx, eng, engine.Request{
616			Bilingual: true,
617			Segments:  segs,
618			Source:    source,
619			Target:    target,
620			Mode:      engine.ModeTranslate,
621			Extra:     instructions,
622		})
623		if err != nil {
624			debug.Logf("bilingual doc: LLM call failed: %v", err)
625			return nil, false
626		}
627		if r == nil || len(r.Bilingual) == 0 {
628			warn := ""
629			if r != nil && len(r.Warnings) > 0 {
630				warn = r.Warnings[0]
631			}
632			debug.Logf("bilingual doc: empty/unparseable structured result (warnings: %q)", warn)
633			return nil, false
634		}
635	
636		translations := make(map[int]string)
637		for num, tr := range r.Bilingual {
638			bi, ok := proseBlock[num]
639			if !ok {
640				continue
641			}
642			t := strings.TrimSpace(tr)
643			if t != "" && !strings.EqualFold(t, strings.TrimSpace(blocks[bi].Plain)) {
644				translations[bi] = t
645			}
646		}
647		return translations, true
648	}
649	
650	// translateOnce runs a single non-streaming translation and returns the result,
651	// draining the engine channel with no token callback. It is the printing-free core
652	// shared by bilingual mode.
653	func translateOnce(ctx context.Context, eng engine.Engine, req engine.Request) (*engine.TranslateResult, error) {
654		ch, err := eng.Translate(ctx, req)
655		if err != nil {
656			return nil, err
657		}
658		return engine.Drain(ch, nil)
659	}
660	
661	// dimFunc returns the styler for bilingual translation lines. It dims (grey) only
662	// when stdout is a TTY and NO_COLOR is unset, so piping the output onward stays
663	// clean; otherwise it is the identity function. The original block's own ANSI is
664	// never touched — only our added translation lines are styled.
665	func dimFunc(stdoutTTY bool) func(string) string {
666		if !stdoutTTY || os.Getenv("NO_COLOR") != "" {
667			return func(s string) string { return s }
668		}
669		style := lg.NewStyle().Foreground(lg.Color("#6C6C6C"))
670		return func(s string) string { return style.Render(s) }
671	}
672	
673	// defaultAway picks the "away" (foreign) language for learn/pair mode when none is
674	// configured: English speakers default to learning zh-TW, everyone else to en. It
675	// mirrors the TUI ^g heuristic so the CLI and TUI agree.
676	func defaultAway(home string) string {
677		if strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(home), "en") {
678			return "zh-TW"
679		}
680		return "en"
681	}
682	
683	// renderLearnCLI formats a learn-mode result as plain text (no ANSI, pipe-safe).
684	func renderLearnCLI(res *engine.TranslateResult) string {
685		l := res.Learn
686		if l == nil {
687			return res.Translation + "\n"
688		}
689		var b strings.Builder
690		if l.Direction == "correct" {
691			corrected := strings.TrimSpace(l.Corrected)
692			if corrected == "" {
693				corrected = res.Translation
694			}
695			b.WriteString("✔ " + corrected + "\n")
696			if s := strings.TrimSpace(l.Translation); s != "" {
697				b.WriteString("  ↳ " + s + "\n")
698			}
699			for _, is := range l.Issues {
700				frag := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(is.Span+" → "+is.Fix, " → "), " → "))

719			for _, v := range l.Vocab {

=== raycast-extension-uses-installed-binary-not-working-tree.md ===
# Raycast extension shows no models / "unknown flag" after adding a CLI feature

**Symptoms** (grep this section): a new dropdown in the Raycast extension is empty; the Model picker offers only "Default (engine + tier)"; a target/language choice fails with `translate: unknown flag: --no-pair`; `translate models` prints a *translation of the word "models"* instead of a model list; a CLI subcommand you just added behaves as if it doesn't exist; the extension works but ignores a flag you can see in `cmd/`.
**First seen**: 2026-07-26
**Affects**: the Raycast extension (and any front-end using `resolveBinary()`) whenever the repo is ahead of the installed `translate` binary.

## Symptom

After adding `translate models` and `--no-pair` to the CLI and running
`just raycast-dev`, the extension's Model dropdown contained only its own
placeholder, and picking a specific target language failed.

The confusing part is *how* the old binary fails. `translate` takes free text as
its first argument, so an unknown subcommand is not an error — it gets
**translated**:

```console
$ ~/.local/bin/translate models          # v0.5.2, no `models` command
n. 模型( model的名词复数 ); 模特儿; 模式; 典型
```

Exit status 0, plausible-looking output, no JSON. `runModels()` parses it, fails,
and returns `[]` — an empty dropdown with no error anywhere. A naive capability
probe (`translate models --json >/dev/null && echo yes`) reports **yes**.

Flags fail loudly, at least:

```console
$ ~/.local/bin/translate "hi" --to ja --no-pair
translate: unknown flag: --no-pair
```

## Root cause

`just raycast-dev` rebuilds the **extension**, not the **binary**. The extension
never runs `./translate` from the working tree — `resolveBinary()`
(`raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts`) deliberately probes absolute install
directories, because Raycast runs under launchd with a restricted PATH (see
[`raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md`](raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md)):

```
~/.local/bin → /opt/homebrew/bin → /usr/local/bin → ~/go/bin
```

So the extension talks to whatever was last installed:

```console
$ ~/.local/bin/translate --version
translate version v0.5.2                 # 4 days old
$ ./translate --version
translate version v0.5.3-0.20260726…+dirty
```

## Workaround

Install the working tree before testing extension features that depend on new CLI
surface:

```sh
just install            # → ~/.local/bin/translate, first in the probe order
translate --version     # confirm it is the dev build, not the tag
```

Beware a second copy shadowing it — `/usr/local/bin/translate` is the Homebrew
install and is also on the probe list, just later. See
[`duplicate-translate-on-path-dotfiles-bin-shadows-local-bin.md`](duplicate-translate-on-path-dotfiles-bin-shadows-local-bin.md).

## Prevention

- Treat `just install` as part of the loop when a change spans CLI **and**
  extension: `just check && just install && just raycast-dev`.
- Don't probe capability by exit status. `translate <unknown-subcommand>` exits 0
  because it translated the word. Check for the *shape* of the output (this is why
  `runModels`/`runLangs` parse and fall back rather than trusting the exit code).
- Degrade visibly. An empty list is indistinguishable from "nothing configured",
  so `translate-text.tsx` renders an explicit "the installed CLI is probably
  older" note instead of an empty dropdown.
- A published extension faces the same skew with users' installed binaries, only
  permanently — new CLI surface needs a fallback path, not just a newer README.

## Related

- [`raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md`](raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md) — why the extension resolves an absolute install path at all.
- [`raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md`](raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md) — the sibling "you rebuilt the wrong thing" trap (stale `ray develop` bundle).
- `AGENTS.md` — the release/versioning flow that makes the installed binary a tag, not `main`.

=== raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md ===
# Raycast can't find `translate` (`spawn translate ENOENT` / "command not found") though it works in a terminal

**Symptoms** (grep this section): a Raycast Script Command prints `translate: command not found`; a Raycast TS extension throws `Error: spawn translate ENOENT`; the exact same command works fine in a terminal but not from Raycast root search; translation works from the shell but the Raycast command errors or shows nothing.
**First seen**: 2026-07 (anticipated — designed around, not yet hit in prod)
**Affects**: Raycast (macOS) Script Commands + TypeScript extensions on this host; any GUI/launchd-launched process that calls the `translate` binary by bare name.

## Symptom

Calling `translate` by bare name from Raycast fails, e.g. a script's
`translate "$2" --to "$1"` yields `command not found`, or an extension's
`execFile("translate", …)` / `spawn("translate")` throws:

```
Error: spawn translate ENOENT
```

The identical invocation succeeds in Terminal/iTerm, which makes it look like the
binary is "missing" only under Raycast.

## Root cause

Raycast is launched by the macOS GUI (launchd), and GUI-launched processes do
**not** source your interactive shell's rc files (`~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`). So
`process.env.PATH` inside a Raycast extension/script is the minimal launchd PATH
and does **not** include `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, or
`~/go/bin` — exactly where `translate` gets installed (`go install` / `just install`
→ `~/.local/bin`; Homebrew → `/opt/homebrew/bin`). A bare-name lookup then fails.

## Workaround

Resolve an **absolute** path to the binary instead of trusting PATH.

- Script Commands ([`../raycast/script-commands/`](../raycast/script-commands/)) —
  probe known dirs (already baked into every script):

  ```sh
  find_translate() {
    for d in "$HOME/.local/bin" /opt/homebrew/bin /usr/local/bin "$HOME/go/bin"; do
      [ -x "$d/translate" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$d/translate"; return 0; }
    done
    command -v translate 2>/dev/null && return 0
    return 1
  }
  ```

- TS extension ([`../raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts`](../raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts))
  — a `binaryPath` preference first, then the same 4-dir probe (`resolveBinary()`).

Probe order must keep `~/.local/bin` **first** — the blessed install location
(see sibling below) — so a stray copy elsewhere can't win.

## Prevention

- Never call bare `translate` from any Raycast surface; always resolve an absolute
  path (preference or probe).
- **Test from Raycast, not a terminal.** A terminal inherits your full PATH and
  will happily find the binary, masking the bug entirely.

## Related

- Sibling: [duplicate-translate-on-path-dotfiles-bin-shadows-local-bin.md](duplicate-translate-on-path-dotfiles-bin-shadows-local-bin.md)
  (why `~/.local/bin` must be first in the probe)
- Reference: [../docs/raycast-extension.md](../docs/raycast-extension.md) "Gotchas"
- Backlog: `TODO.md` P? "Publish the Raycast extension to the store" ·
  [../backlog/raycast-extension.md](../backlog/raycast-extension.md)

=== raycast-search-bar-refuses-long-paste.md ===
# Raycast refuses a long paste: "The text you are trying to paste is too long"

**Symptoms** (grep this section): pasting a paragraph into a Raycast extension's search bar shows a red footer "The text you are trying to paste is too long"; only part of a long text lands in the search bar; a Raycast `List` command can't accept more than a short phrase; `onSearchTextChange` never sees the full pasted text; translating/processing a long passage is impossible from a Raycast command.
**First seen**: 2026-07-26
**Affects**: any Raycast extension on macOS that takes input via the search bar (`List` / `Grid` with `onSearchTextChange`). Not specific to this extension.

## Symptom

Pasting a long passage into the **Look up Word** (or **Translate**, or **Define**)
search bar is rejected with a red footer message:

```
The text you are trying to paste is too long
```

The text is simply not accepted — there is no partial paste, no error thrown into
the extension, and nothing in `onSearchTextChange`.

## Root cause

The guard belongs to the Raycast **application**, not to the extension API:

```console
$ strings -a /Applications/Raycast.app/Contents/MacOS/Raycast | grep "paste is too long"
The text you are trying to paste is too long

$ grep -r "paste is too long" raycast/extension/node_modules/@raycast/
$        # nothing — not part of the extension API
```

So an extension cannot raise the limit, configure it, or even observe that it
fired: `@raycast/api` exposes no length option on `List`/`Grid`, and the
rejection never reaches `onSearchTextChange`. The search bar is a single-line
launcher input; long documents were never its job.

## Workaround

Give long text an input that is not the search bar. `Form.TextArea` has no such
cap — that is what `raycast/extension/src/translate-text.tsx` (**Translate Text**)
exists for.

```tsx
<Form actions={…}>
  <Form.TextArea id="text" title="Text" value={text} onChange={setText} />
</Form>
```

Two further limits sit behind it, both worth knowing before assuming the CLI is
at fault:

1. **`ARG_MAX` on the exec.** Passing the text as an argv element caps out at
   1 MiB on macOS (`getconf ARG_MAX` → 1048576). Measured: 900 KB works, 1.1 MB
   fails the spawn with `argument list too long`. `src/lib/translate.ts` switches
   to stdin above 128 KB of UTF-8 (`ARGV_SAFE_BYTES`), since `translate` reads
   stdin when given no text argument and a pipe has no such limit.
2. **The provider.** The Google engine puts the text in a GET query string and
   fails around 180 KB with a URL-length error; LLM providers have their own
   token limits (copilot-proxy returned `http 400` at 1.1 MB). These are the real
   ceiling for a genuinely large document, and no client change moves them.

**Also worth trying before writing any code:** *Translate Selection* reads the
selection programmatically and seeds Translate through `launchContext`, so it
never pastes into the search bar at all.

## Prevention

- Treat the search bar as an input for words and short phrases. Any command that
  should accept a paragraph needs a `Form`.
- When something "can't be pasted" in Raycast, check `strings` on the app binary
  before hunting through the extension — an app-level guard produces no error the
  extension can see.

## Related

- [`raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md`](raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md) — the other Raycast-app-vs-extension boundary trap.
- [`../docs/raycast-extension.md`](../docs/raycast-extension.md) — Gotchas.

=== raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md ===
# Raycast Translate still prefills from the clipboard/selection after the manifest default was changed to "Nothing"

**Symptoms** (grep this section): opening the Raycast **Translate** command auto-fills the input box with the clipboard or the selected text even though `package.json` says `"default": "none"`; a Raycast preference change made in `package.json` has no visible effect; a Raycast command behaves per an *old* manifest; `getPreferenceValues()` returns a value you never chose; a Raycast extension keeps doing the thing you just "fixed" in the manifest.
**First seen**: 2026-07-26
**Affects**: any Raycast extension on macOS whose `package.json` preference `default` is changed after the extension has been installed/run once.

## Symptom

Commit `e87db06` changed the `translate` extension's `prefill` preference default
from `"selection"` to `"none"` so plain **Translate** would open with an empty
input box. It did not take effect: opening Translate still seeded the box from the
clipboard.

Confusingly the setting was `"selection"`, not `"clipboard"` — but on macOS
`getSelectedText()` falls back to a copy-and-read-pasteboard path in apps that
don't expose a selection, so with nothing selected it returns *clipboard*
contents. So a stale `"selection"` value looks like clipboard prefill.

## Root cause

Three causes compound; check them in this order.

1. **A stored preference value survives a manifest-default change.** Raycast
   persists a preference value once it has been materialized for a command
   (opening the command, or touching its preference pane). A manifest `default`
   applies **only when nothing is stored**. So changing `default` in `package.json`
   is invisible to any install that already ran the command — and *no code change
   can fix it*, because the stored value is the user's expressed choice as far as
   Raycast is concerned.

   ```console
   $ git show --stat e87db06
    raycast/extension/package.json | 4 ++--
    1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
   ```

   One file changed — nothing that could reach an existing install's stored value.

2. **A stale installed dev build.** `ray develop` leaves the built bundle
   registered with Raycast after you stop dev mode. If `just raycast-dev` /
   `raycast-build` has not been run since the manifest changed, Raycast is still
   executing the *old* manifest, defaults included.

3. **A code default that contradicts the manifest.** `src/translate.tsx` read

   ```ts
   const mode = prefs.prefill ?? "selection";   // manifest default is "none"
   ```

   Whenever `getPreferenceValues()` yields `undefined` — an older API, or a
   manifest/bundle mismatch as in (2) — the code silently re-enabled prefill.
   TypeScript never caught it because a hand-written `interface Prefs { prefill?: string }`
   **shadowed** the generated `Preferences.Translate`, where `prefill` is required.

## Workaround

**First, reset the stored value** (this is usually the whole problem):

> Raycast → Settings → Extensions → Translate → *Translate* → **Prefill input from**
> → "Nothing (type manually)"

Then rebuild so Raycast is running the current manifest:

```sh
just raycast-dev     # or: just raycast-build
```

The code fix, so the two defaults can never disagree again:

```diff
-interface Prefs { defaultTarget?: string; liveDebounceMs?: string; prefill?: string }
-  const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Prefs>();
+  const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Preferences.Translate>();
-    const mode = prefs.prefill ?? "selection";
+    const mode = prefs.prefill ?? "none"; // must match package.json's default
```

`Preferences.Translate` is generated from the manifest by `ray build` into the
(gitignored) `raycast-env.d.ts`, and declares `prefill` as **required** — so a
future manifest/code drift is a compile error rather than a silent behaviour
change.

**Considered and rejected:** renaming the key (`prefill` → `prefillMode`) to force
Raycast to re-apply the new default. It works, but it silently discards a
deliberate opt-in for anyone who chose selection/clipboard on purpose.

## Prevention

- Read preferences through the generated `Preferences.<Command>` type. Never
  hand-write a preferences interface — the hand-written one makes fields optional
  and re-opens exactly this gap.
- When you change a preference `default`, remember the change reaches **new
  installs only**. If the old behaviour was a bug, say so in the release note and
  tell existing users which setting to reset.
- Test from Raycast, not from a terminal, and rebuild first — see
  [`raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md`](raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md)
  for the other half of that rule.

=== duplicate-translate-on-path-dotfiles-bin-shadows-local-bin.md ===
# Two `translate` binaries: ~/.dotfiles/bin shadows ~/.local/bin (edits/reinstalls don't take effect)

**Symptoms** (grep this section): reinstalled or rebuilt `translate` but the
old behaviour persists; `command -v -a translate` prints two paths; a stale
`~/.dotfiles/bin/translate` wins over a fresh `~/.local/bin/translate`; version
mismatch between `which translate` and the just-installed binary.
**First seen**: 2026-07 (anticipated — no live collision yet)
**Affects**: this host's PATH order, where `~/.dotfiles/bin` precedes
`~/.local/bin`; triggered by the Justfile `install` recipe.
**Status**: fixed — `just install` now targets `~/.local/bin` (2026-07-22), so it
no longer creates a shadowing copy; the workaround below still applies if a stale
`~/.dotfiles/bin/translate` lingers from a past run.

## Symptom

The blessed install path is `GOBIN=~/.local/bin go install …`. But the
project `Justfile` also has:

```make
install: build
    install -m 0755 translate ~/.dotfiles/bin/translate
```

On this host PATH is ordered `… ~/.dotfiles/bin (pos 11) … ~/.local/bin (pos 13)`,
so if `just install` has ever run, the copy in `~/.dotfiles/bin` **shadows** the
`go install` copy:

```
$ command -v -a translate
/Users/david/.dotfiles/bin/translate     # stale, wins
/Users/david/.local/bin/translate        # fresh, ignored
```

You then rebuild / `go install` a new version, run `translate`, and see no
change — because a different, older binary earlier on PATH is what runs.

## Root cause

Two independent install mechanisms target two different PATH dirs, and
`~/.dotfiles/bin` (chezmoi-managed scripts dir) sorts before `~/.local/bin`.
Shell PATH resolution takes the first match, so whichever dir is earlier wins
regardless of which binary is newer.

## Workaround

Standardize on one location (`~/.local/bin` via `go install`) and remove the
stray copy:

```sh
rm -f ~/.dotfiles/bin/translate
GOBIN="$HOME/.local/bin" go install github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@latest
command -v -a translate   # should print ONLY ~/.local/bin/translate
```

## Prevention

1	import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
2	import { ActionPanel, Action, Detail } from "@raycast/api";
3	import { spawnTranslateStream } from "./translate";
4	
5	/** A pushed Detail that streams `translate … --stream` output token-by-token.
6	 *  Opt-in from the Translate view (⌘↵) — useful for long text and streaming
7	 *  engines; on a buffering provider it simply appears after first-token latency. */
8	export function StreamView({
9	  text,
10	  to,
11	  engine,
12	  model,
13	  pair,
14	}: {
15	  text: string;
16	  to?: string;
17	  engine?: string;
18	  model?: string;
19	  pair?: boolean;
20	}) {
21	  const [md, setMd] = useState("");
22	  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);
23	  const acc = useRef("");
24	
25	  useEffect(() => {
26	    acc.current = "";
27	    setMd("");
28	    setIsLoading(true);
29	    const cancel = spawnTranslateStream(
30	      text,
31	      { to, engine: engine || undefined, model, pair },
32	      {
33	        onData: (chunk) => {
34	          acc.current += chunk;
35	          setMd(acc.current);
36	        },
37	        onDone: () => setIsLoading(false),
38	        onError: (err) => {
39	          acc.current += `\n\n> error: ${err.message}`;
40	          setMd(acc.current);
41	          setIsLoading(false);
42	        },
43	      },
44	    );
45	    return cancel;
46	  }, [text, to, engine, model, pair]);
47	
48	  return (
49	    <Detail
50	      isLoading={isLoading}
51	      markdown={md || "…"}
52	      navigationTitle={to ? `Translate → ${to}` : "Translate"}
53	      actions={
54	        <ActionPanel>
55	          <Action.CopyToClipboard title="Copy Translation" content={md} />
56	          <Action.Paste title="Paste Translation" content={md} />
57	        </ActionPanel>
58	      }
59	    />
60	  );
61	}

25	  engine?: string;
26	  model?: string;
27	  pair?: boolean;
28	}) {

30	  const { data, isLoading, error } = usePromise(

32	      runTranslate(text, { to, engine, model, pair }),

34	  );
35	
36	  const markdown = error
37	    ? errorMarkdown(error)
38	    : data
39	      ? renderTranslation(data)
40	      : "Translating…";
41	
42	  return (
43	    <Detail
44	      isLoading={isLoading}
45	      navigationTitle={
46	        data?.target ? `Translate → ${data.target}` : "Translate"
47	      }
48	      markdown={markdown}
49	      actions={
50	        <ActionPanel>
51	          {data ? (
52	            <>
53	              <Action.CopyToClipboard
54	                title="Copy Translation"
55	                content={data.translation}
56	              />
57	              <Action.Paste
58	                title="Paste Translation"
59	                content={data.translation}
60	              />
61	              <Action.CopyToClipboard
62	                title="Copy Source Text"
63	                content={text}
64	                shortcut={{ modifiers: ["cmd"], key: "i" }}
65	              />
66	              <Action
67	                title="Speak"
68	                icon={Icon.SpeakerHigh}
69	                onAction={async () => {
70	                  speak(text, data.target || to || "en");
71	                  await showHUD("Speaking…");
72	                }}
73	              />
74	            </>
75	          ) : null}
76	        </ActionPanel>
77	      }
78	    />
79	  );
80	}

82	function errorMarkdown(error: Error): string {
83	  if (isBinaryMissing(error)) {
84	    return [
85	      "# translate CLI not found",
86	      "",
87	      "Set the binary path in the extension preferences, or install it:",
88	      "",
89	      "```sh",

91	      "```",

97	/** Plain paragraph (not an H1) so long translations read comfortably. */
98	export function renderTranslation(r: TranslateResult): string {
99	  const lines = [r.translation, ""];
100	  if (r.alternatives?.length)
101	    lines.push("## Alternatives", ...r.alternatives.map((a) => `- ${a}`), "");
102	  if (r.notes) lines.push("## Notes", r.notes, "");
103	  if (r.warnings?.length)
104	    lines.push("## Warnings", ...r.warnings.map((w) => `> ${w}`), "");
105	  lines.push("---", footer(r));
106	  return lines.join("\n");
107	}
108	
109	/** One dim line at the end of the scroll, in place of a metadata sidebar. */
110	function footer(r: TranslateResult): string {
111	  const bits = [
112	    `${r.detected_source ?? "auto"} → ${r.target}`,
113	    r.engine ?? "—",
114	    r.model,
115	    typeof r.confidence === "number"
116	      ? `confidence ${r.confidence.toFixed(2)}`
117	      : undefined,
118	  ].filter(Boolean);
119	  return `*${bits.join(" · ")}*`;
120	}

126	function definitionText(r: TranslateResult, word: string): string {
127	  const d = r.dictionary;
128	  if (!d) return r.translation;
129	  const lines: string[] = [];
130	  for (const m of d.meanings ?? []) {
131	    for (const def of m.definitions ?? []) lines.push(def.definition);
132	  }
133	  return lines.length > 0 ? lines.join("\n") : r.translation || word;

139	  if (d) {

141	    if (d.phonetic) lines.push(`*/${d.phonetic}/*`);
142	    lines.push("");
143	    for (const m of d.meanings ?? []) {
144	      lines.push(`## ${m.part_of_speech}`);
145	      for (const def of m.definitions ?? []) {
146	        lines.push(
147	          `- ${def.definition}${def.example ? `\n  - _${def.example}_` : ""}`,
148	        );
149	      }
150	      lines.push("");
151	    }
152	    return lines.join("\n");
153	  }
154	  // No dictionary entry — the LLM fallback's definition lives in `translation`.
155	  const lines = [`# ${word}`, "", r.translation, ""];
156	  if (r.warnings?.length) lines.push("---", ...r.warnings.map((w) => `> ${w}`));
157	  return lines.join("\n");

28	          ) : null}

30	        </Detail.Metadata>

35	          <Action.Paste title="Paste Output" content={entry.output} />

46	          />

53	            }}

55	        </ActionPanel>
56	      }

61	export function renderEntry(h: HistoryEntry): string {
62	  return [`# ${h.input}`, "", h.output].join("\n");
63	}

65	export function formatTS(ts: string): string {
66	  const d = new Date(ts);
67	  return isNaN(d.getTime()) ? ts : d.toLocaleString();

70	export function oneline(s: string, n: number): string {
71	  const flat = s.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
72	  return flat.length <= n ? flat : `${flat.slice(0, n - 1)}…`;

1	// Package appcore holds the transport-agnostic core shared by every front-end:
2	// the engine builders (constructed from resolved config) and a Service that wraps
3	// a warm engine + history store behind Translate/Define/History methods. The
4	// one-shot CLI, the HTTP server (translate serve), and the MCP server (translate
5	// mcp) all drive this same core and diverge only at their transport edge.
6	//
7	// It imports only config/engine/store/lang/debug — never tui or cmd — so both cmd
8	// and the server packages can import it without an import cycle.
9	package appcore
10	
11	import (
12		"fmt"
13		"time"
14	
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/config"
16		"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/engine"
17	)
18	
19	// BuildEngine constructs the Engine for an invocation from resolved settings.
20	// engine="auto" builds a fallback Chain over the providers named in chain.order;
21	// engine="smartauto" builds the smart default (dictionary for words, LLM for
22	// phrases, bidirectional); a named provider builds a single LLM engine.
23	func BuildEngine(res config.Resolved) (engine.Engine, error) {
24		cfg := res.Cfg
25	
26		switch res.Engine {
27		case "auto":
28			return BuildAutoChain(res)
29		case "smartauto":
30			// Needs an LLM provider for the word-miss fallback and phrase translation;
31			// without one, behave like the plain auto chain (google/dict).
32			if res.Provider == nil {
33				return BuildAutoChain(res)
34			}
35			return SmartAutoFromConfig(res), nil
36		case "google":
37			return GoogleFromConfig(cfg), nil
38		case "llm":
39			// "llm" means "the resolved provider" (already chosen by Resolve).
40			if res.Provider != nil {
41				return LLMFromProvider(res.Provider, res.Model), nil
42			}
43			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown engine/provider %q (check %s)", res.Engine, config.Path())
44		default:
45			// A named provider (e.g. "copilot", "ollama").
46			if res.Provider != nil {
47				return LLMFromProvider(res.Provider, res.Model), nil
48			}
49			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown engine/provider %q (check %s)", res.Engine, config.Path())
50		}
51	}
52	
53	// BuildAutoChain builds the "auto" fallback Chain over the providers/google named
54	// in chain.order. (google/dict engines otherwise join only via smart-auto or the
55	// TUI ^e cycle.)
56	//
57	// An explicit --model applies only to the *resolved* provider: a chain spans
58	// several backends, and forcing one id onto all of them would send e.g. a Claude
59	// model to Ollama. Every other member keeps its own tier model. Without this the
60	// flag was silently dropped on the default (smartauto/auto) engine — it only
61	// took effect when the caller also named a provider with --engine.
62	func BuildAutoChain(res config.Resolved) (engine.Engine, error) {
63		cfg := res.Cfg
64		var engines []engine.Engine
65		for _, name := range cfg.Chain.Order {
66			switch {
67			case cfg.ProviderByName(name) != nil:
68				p := cfg.ProviderByName(name)
69				model := p.ModelForTier(res.Tier)
70				if res.Model != "" && res.Provider != nil && p.Name == res.Provider.Name {
71					model = res.Model
72				}
73				engines = append(engines, LLMFromProvider(p, model))
74			case name == "google" && cfg.Google.Enabled:
75				engines = append(engines, GoogleFromConfig(cfg))
76			}
77			// "dict" is wired in via smart-auto / the TUI engine cycle.
78		}
79		if len(engines) == 0 {
80			return nil, fmt.Errorf("no engines available in chain.order (check %s)", config.Path())
81		}
82		if len(engines) == 1 {
83			return engines[0], nil
84		}
85		return engine.NewChain(engines, 5*time.Second), nil
86	}
87	
88	// LLMFromProvider builds an LLM engine for a provider using the given model id.
89	func LLMFromProvider(p *config.Provider, model string) *engine.LLMEngine {
90		if model == "" {
91			model = p.Model
92		}
93		return engine.NewLLM(engine.LLMConfig{
94			Name:      p.Name,
95			BaseURL:   p.BaseURL,
96			Model:     model,
97			APIKeyEnv: p.APIKeyEnv,
98		})
99	}
100	
101	// GoogleFromConfig builds the free Google engine from config.
102	func GoogleFromConfig(cfg *config.Config) *engine.GoogleEngine {
103		return engine.NewGoogle(engine.GoogleConfig{
104			Endpoint:  cfg.Google.Endpoint,
105			ExtraDT:   cfg.Google.ExtraDT,
106			UserAgent: cfg.Google.UserAgent,
107			Timeout:   time.Duration(cfg.Google.TimeoutMs) * time.Millisecond,
108		})
109	}
110	
111	// DictFromConfig builds the dictionary engine from config: the offline bilingual
112	// engine (source=local, default) or the dictionaryapi.dev engine (source=api).
113	func DictFromConfig(cfg *config.Config) engine.Engine {
114		if cfg.Dict.Source == "api" {
115			return engine.NewDict(engine.DictConfig{
116				Endpoint: cfg.Dict.Endpoint,
117				Lang:     cfg.Dict.Lang,
118				Fuzzy:    cfg.Dict.Fuzzy,
119				Wordlist: cfg.Dict.Wordlist,
120			})
121		}
122		var apiFb *engine.DictEngine
123		if cfg.Dict.APIFallback {
124			apiFb = engine.NewDict(engine.DictConfig{
125				Endpoint: cfg.Dict.Endpoint,
126				Lang:     cfg.Dict.Lang,
127				Fuzzy:    cfg.Dict.Fuzzy,
128				Wordlist: cfg.Dict.Wordlist,
129			})
130		}
131		return engine.NewLocalDict(engine.LocalDictConfig{
132			Dir:          cfg.Dict.Dir,
133			CedictURL:    cfg.Dict.CedictURL,
134			EcdictURL:    cfg.Dict.EcdictURL,
135			AutoDownload: cfg.Dict.AutoDownload,
136			Fuzzy:        cfg.Dict.Fuzzy,
137			Wordlist:     cfg.Dict.Wordlist,
138			APIFallback:  apiFb,
139		})
140	}
141	
142	// DictSearcher returns the headword searcher behind the configured dictionary, or
143	// (nil, false) when the source is the remote API — dictionaryapi.dev exposes no
144	// headword list, so there is nothing to search locally.
145	func DictSearcher(cfg *config.Config) (engine.Searcher, bool) {
146		s, ok := DictFromConfig(cfg).(engine.Searcher)
147		return s, ok
148	}
149	
150	// SmartDictFromConfig builds the smart-dict engine: the plain dictionary plus an
151	// LLM fallback (resolved provider/model) for misses and too-weak fuzzy matches.
152	// The caller must ensure res.Provider != nil.
153	func SmartDictFromConfig(res config.Resolved) engine.Engine {
154		cfg := res.Cfg
155		return engine.NewSmartDict(DictFromConfig(cfg), LLMFromProvider(res.Provider, res.Model), engine.SmartDictConfig{
156			CloseDistance: cfg.SmartDict.CloseDistance,
157			Preset:        cfg.SmartDict.Preset,
158		})
159	}
160	
161	// SmartAutoFromConfig builds the smart-auto default: a single word/term is a
162	// dictionary lookup (smart-dict, with an LLM fallback), and a phrase is an LLM
163	// translation via the auto chain (so phrases keep provider→google resilience).
164	// The caller must ensure res.Provider != nil.
165	func SmartAutoFromConfig(res config.Resolved) engine.Engine {
166		llm, err := BuildAutoChain(res)
167		if err != nil {
168			// No chain engines (unlikely once a provider exists): fall back to the bare
169			// resolved provider so phrases can still translate.
170			llm = LLMFromProvider(res.Provider, res.Model)
171		}
172		return engine.NewSmartAuto(SmartDictFromConfig(res), llm)
173	}
174	
175	// LearnEngineFromConfig builds the engine for learning mode: a bare LLM engine
176	// (the resolved provider/model), bypassing smart-auto/dictionary routing so a
177	// single word still gets the structured tutor treatment. Caller ensures Provider != nil.
178	func LearnEngineFromConfig(res config.Resolved) engine.Engine {
179		return LLMFromProvider(res.Provider, res.Model)
180	}
181	
182	// DefineEngine picks the dictionary engine for a definition lookup: the plain
183	// offline dictionary, or smart-dict (with an LLM fallback) when a provider is
184	// available and not overridden. plain forces plain; smart forces smart. It is the
185	// single source of truth shared by `translate define` and the Service.
186	func DefineEngine(res config.Resolved, plain, smart bool) engine.Engine {
187		cfg := res.Cfg
188		if plain || res.Provider == nil {
189			return DictFromConfig(cfg)
190		}
191		if smart || cfg.SmartDict.DefineDefault {
192			return SmartDictFromConfig(res)
193		}
194		return DictFromConfig(cfg)
195	}

1	package engine
2	
3	import (
4		"context"

8		"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/debug"

11	
12	// SmartAutoEngine is the "smart" default: it treats a single word/term as a
13	// dictionary lookup (delegating to the smart-dict engine, which itself falls back
14	// to the LLM on a miss) and a phrase or sentence as an LLM translation. It is
15	// bidirectional-friendly — the caller sets Pair/PairHome/PairAway and the routed
16	// Target, and both branches honor them.
17	//
18	// Because dictionary word lookups are direction-agnostic (script routes them to
19	// CC-CEDICT vs ECDICT) and phrase translation uses the pair-aware LLM prompt, a
20	// single word like "test" is answered from the dictionary instead of risking an
21	// LLM echo, and a full sentence is translated into the other pair language.
22	type SmartAutoEngine struct {
23		smart Engine // dictionary + LLM fallback (serves ModeDict)
24		llm   Engine // LLM translate, possibly a fallback chain (serves ModeTranslate)
25	}
26	
27	// NewSmartAuto builds a smart-auto engine over a smart-dict engine (word lookups)
28	// and an LLM/translate engine (phrases).
29	func NewSmartAuto(smart, llm Engine) *SmartAutoEngine {
30		return &SmartAutoEngine{smart: smart, llm: llm}
31	}
32	
33	// Name returns "smart-auto".
34	func (e *SmartAutoEngine) Name() string { return "smart-auto" }
35	
36	// Supports translate mode (the main-path request mode); it dispatches to a
37	// dictionary lookup internally when the input looks like a single word.
38	func (e *SmartAutoEngine) Supports(m Mode) bool { return m == ModeTranslate }
39	
40	// Detect is not meaningful here (the LLM/dict sub-engines own detection).
41	func (e *SmartAutoEngine) Detect(ctx context.Context, text string) (string, error) {
42		return "", nil
43	}
44	
45	// Available reports true when either branch can serve.
46	func (e *SmartAutoEngine) Available(ctx context.Context) bool {
47		return e.smart.Available(ctx) || e.llm.Available(ctx)
48	}
49	
50	// Translate routes a single word/term to the dictionary (smart-dict) and a phrase
51	// to the LLM. Streaming is preserved by returning the chosen sub-engine's channel.
52	func (e *SmartAutoEngine) Translate(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Chunk, error) {
53		if isLookup(req.Text) {
54			debug.Logf("smart-auto: %q → dictionary lookup (smart-dict), target=%s", truncateText(req.Text), req.Target)
55			r := req
56			r.Mode = ModeDict
57			return e.smart.Translate(ctx, r)
58		}
59		debug.Logf("smart-auto: %q → LLM translate, target=%s pair=%v", truncateText(req.Text), req.Target, req.Pair)
60		r := req
61		r.Mode = ModeTranslate
62		return e.llm.Translate(ctx, r)
63	}
64	
65	// isLookup reports whether text should be treated as a dictionary lookup (a
66	// single word or short term) rather than a phrase to translate. Latin/other: one
67	// token of letters (plus '-' / apostrophe), up to 32 runes. CJK: a short run of
68	// Han without spaces (a word or idiom, up to 4 characters). Anything with
69	// internal whitespace is a phrase.
70	func isLookup(text string) bool {
71		t := strings.TrimSpace(text)
72		if t == "" {
73			return false
74		}
75		if strings.ContainsAny(t, " \t\n\r") {
76			return false // multiple tokens → phrase
77		}
78		if lang.IsChinese(t) {
79			return len([]rune(t)) <= 4
80		}
81		for _, r := range t {
82			if !unicode.IsLetter(r) && r != '-' && r != '\'' {
83				return false // digits/punctuation → not a plain word
84			}
85		}
86		return len([]rune(t)) <= 32
87	}
88	
89	// truncateText shortens a string for a single-line debug label.
90	func truncateText(s string) string {
91		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
92		r := []rune(s)
93		if len(r) > 40 {
94			return string(r[:40]) + "…"
95		}
96		return s
97	}
98

12	// SmartDictConfig parameterizes the smart-dict engine.
13	type SmartDictConfig struct {
14		// CloseDistance is the English edit distance at/below which a fuzzy "did you
15		// mean" is treated as a likely typo and returned as-is; a farther match (and
16		// any hard miss) triggers the LLM fallback. 0 disables the typo shortcut, so
17		// every non-exact lookup falls back.
18		CloseDistance int
19		// Preset is the LLM prompt style used for the fallback; "" => PresetDictionary
20		// (a gloss plus example sentences).
21		Preset string
22	}
23	
24	// SmartDictEngine composes a dictionary engine with an LLM: it answers from the
25	// dictionary when it can, and falls back to the LLM when the word is missing or the
26	// fuzzy match is too far off. It is a distinct, selectable engine — the plain
27	// dictionary engine is left untouched.
28	//
29	// This is the first engine to branch on a produced result's quality (the Chain
30	// only fails over on hard errors), so the fallback always stamps a Warning: the
31	// downgrade from an offline lookup to an LLM answer is never silent.
32	type SmartDictEngine struct {
33		dict Engine
34		llm  Engine
35		cfg  SmartDictConfig
36	}
37	
38	// NewSmartDict builds a smart-dict engine over a dictionary and an LLM backend.
39	func NewSmartDict(dict, llm Engine, cfg SmartDictConfig) *SmartDictEngine {
40		return &SmartDictEngine{dict: dict, llm: llm, cfg: cfg}
41	}
42	
43	// Name returns "smart-dict".
44	func (e *SmartDictEngine) Name() string { return "smart-dict" }
45	
46	// Supports reports that this engine handles dictionary lookups.
47	func (e *SmartDictEngine) Supports(m Mode) bool { return m == ModeDict }
48	
49	// Detect is not meaningful for a dictionary engine.
50	func (e *SmartDictEngine) Detect(ctx context.Context, text string) (string, error) {
51		return "", nil
52	}
53	
54	// Available reports true when either backend can serve (a dictionary hit, or the
55	// LLM fallback).
56	func (e *SmartDictEngine) Available(ctx context.Context) bool {
57		return e.dict.Available(ctx) || e.llm.Available(ctx)
58	}
59	
60	// Translate looks the word up in the dictionary and, on a miss or a too-weak fuzzy
61	// match, falls back to the LLM (streaming preserved).
62	func (e *SmartDictEngine) Translate(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Chunk, error) {
63		dictCh, err := e.dict.Translate(ctx, req)
64		if err != nil {
65			// A setup failure (e.g. empty input) — nothing to fall back to.
66			return nil, err
67		}
68	
69		out := make(chan Chunk, 32)
70		go func() {
71			defer close(out)
72			// The dictionary engines are single-shot (no token stream), so drain fully
73			// before deciding whether the answer is good enough.
74			res, derr := Drain(dictCh, nil)
75			if e.dictAnswered(res, derr) {
76				debug.Logf("smart-dict: %q answered from dictionary", strings.TrimSpace(req.Text))
77				out <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkDone, Result: res}
78				return
79			}
80			debug.Logf("smart-dict: %q → LLM fallback (no usable dictionary entry)", strings.TrimSpace(req.Text))
81			e.fallback(ctx, req, derr, out)
82		}()
83		return out, nil
84	}
85	
86	// dictAnswered reports whether the dictionary produced a result good enough to
87	// return without asking the LLM: an exact entry, or a fuzzy suggestion close enough
88	// to be a likely typo (within CloseDistance).
89	func (e *SmartDictEngine) dictAnswered(res *TranslateResult, derr error) bool {
90		if derr != nil || res == nil {
91			return false // hard miss (ErrNoDictEntry) or transport error → fall back
92		}
93		if res.Dictionary != nil {
94			return true // exact hit
95		}
96		// A close typo (distance known and within threshold) stays as "did you mean".
97		// Unknown distance (0, e.g. Chinese prefix matches) counts as too far → fall back.
98		if len(res.Suggestions) > 0 && res.SuggestDistance != 0 && res.SuggestDistance <= e.cfg.CloseDistance {
99			return true
100		}
101		return false // suggestions too far, "not installed" notes, or empty → fall back
102	}
103	
104	// fallback runs the LLM in translate mode and pipes its chunks to out, stamping a
105	// warning on the terminal result so the downgrade is visible.
106	func (e *SmartDictEngine) fallback(ctx context.Context, req Request, derr error, out chan<- Chunk) {
107		word := strings.TrimSpace(req.Text)
108	
109		r := req
110		r.Mode = ModeTranslate
111		r.Preset = e.cfg.Preset
112		if r.Preset == "" {
113			r.Preset = PresetDictionary
114		}
115		r.Target = smartTarget(req.Text, req.Target)
116	
117		llmCh, err := e.llm.Translate(ctx, r)
118		if err != nil {
119			out <- Chunk{Kind: ChunkError, Err: fmt.Errorf("smart-dict: no dictionary entry for %q and LLM fallback failed: %w", word, err)}
120			return
121		}
122		for ch := range llmCh {
123			if ch.Kind == ChunkDone && ch.Result != nil {
124				ch.Result.Warnings = append(ch.Result.Warnings,
125					fmt.Sprintf("no dictionary entry for %q — defined via %s (LLM)", word, ch.Result.Engine))
126			}
127			out <- ch
128		}
129	}
130	
131	// smartTarget picks the LLM fallback's target language, mirroring the bilingual
132	// dictionary (Chinese ↔ English): Chinese input → English; English/other input →
133	// the caller's target, or Chinese when that target is English/unset.
134	func smartTarget(text, target string) string {
135		if lang.IsChinese(text) {
136			return "en"
137		}
138		t := strings.TrimSpace(target)
139		if t == "" || t == "auto" || strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(t), "en") {
140			return "zh"
141		}
142		return t
143	}

```text
1	// Package bitext splits piped terminal input into blank-line-delimited blocks and
2	// renders a bilingual ("immersive") view: each original block is kept verbatim
3	// (ANSI/color intact) and a translation is shown beneath prose blocks. It powers
4	// the CLI's --bilingual pipe mode. ANSI stripping is delegated to
5	// github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi so the tokenizer stays wcwidth/CJK-aware.
6	package bitext
7	
8	import (
9		"strings"
10	
11		"github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi"
12	)
13	
14	// Kind classifies a block of piped input.
15	type Kind int
16	
17	const (
18		// Blank is a whitespace-only line, preserved so original spacing survives.
19		Blank Kind = iota
20		// Prose is natural-language text — the only kind that gets translated.
21		Prose
22		// Code is an indented command/example block — echoed verbatim, not translated.
23		Code
24	)
25	
26	// Block is one unit of piped input: a run of consecutive non-blank lines, or a
27	// single blank line.
28	type Block struct {
29		Raw   string // original line(s) joined by "\n", ANSI escapes intact (for display)
30		Plain string // Raw with all ANSI/SGR escapes stripped (for the LLM + classification)
31		Kind  Kind
32	}
33	
34	// Strip removes every ANSI/SGR escape sequence from s, returning display text.
35	func Strip(s string) string { return ansi.Strip(s) }
36	
37	// codeIndent is how many columns DEEPER than the document's base margin a block
38	// must be indented to count as a command/code example. Tools like tldr indent the
39	// whole body (prose at a base margin, examples deeper), so detection is relative to
40	// that base — an absolute threshold would misread the indented prose as code.
41	const codeIndent = 2
42	
43	// Split breaks raw piped input into blocks. Consecutive non-blank lines coalesce
44	// into one block (grouping soft-wrapped prose so it translates with context); each
45	// blank line becomes its own Blank block so original spacing is reproduced. A
46	// trailing newline is trimmed so it does not yield a spurious final blank block.
47	func Split(raw string) []Block {
48		raw = strings.TrimRight(raw, "\n")
49		if raw == "" {
50			return nil
51		}
52		lines := strings.Split(raw, "\n")
53	
54		// The document's base margin: the minimum leading indentation over all
55		// non-blank lines. tldr/man indent the entire body, so "code" is measured
56		// relative to this, not from column zero.
57		base := -1
58		for _, ln := range lines {
59			p := Strip(ln)
60			if strings.TrimSpace(p) == "" {
61				continue
62			}
63			if c := leadingCols(p); base < 0 || c < base {
64				base = c
65			}
66		}
67		if base < 0 {
68			base = 0
69		}
70	
71		var blocks []Block
72		var cur []string // current run of non-blank raw lines
73	
74		flush := func() {
75			if len(cur) == 0 {
76				return
77			}
78			rawBlk := strings.Join(cur, "\n")
79			blocks = append(blocks, Block{
80				Raw:   rawBlk,
81				Plain: Strip(rawBlk),
82				Kind:  classify(cur, base),
83			})
84			cur = nil
85		}
86	
87		for _, ln := range lines {
88			if strings.TrimSpace(Strip(ln)) == "" {
89				flush()
90				blocks = append(blocks, Block{Raw: ln, Kind: Blank})
91				continue
92			}
93			cur = append(cur, ln)
94		}
95		flush()
96		return blocks
97	}
98	
99	// classify returns Code when every (stripped) line is indented at least codeIndent
100	// columns deeper than the document's base margin, else Prose.
101	func classify(rawLines []string, base int) Kind {
102		for _, ln := range rawLines {
103			if leadingCols(Strip(ln)) < base+codeIndent {
104				return Prose
105			}
106		}
107		return Code
108	}
109	
110	// leadingCols counts leading whitespace columns, treating a tab as codeIndent.
111	func leadingCols(s string) int {
112		n := 0
113		for _, r := range s {
114			switch r {
115			case ' ':
116				n++
117			case '\t':
118				n += codeIndent
119			default:
120				return n
121			}
122		}
123		return n
124	}
125	
126	// Render assembles the bilingual output. Each block's Raw is emitted verbatim; for
127	// Prose blocks whose index has a translation, each translation line is emitted
128	// beneath — the first prefixed "  ↳ ", continuations aligned under it — and passed
129	// through dim (identity when styling is off). Code and Blank blocks pass through
130	// untouched.
131	func Render(blocks []Block, translations map[int]string, dim func(string) string) string {
132		if dim == nil {
133			dim = func(s string) string { return s }
134		}
135		var b strings.Builder
136		for i, blk := range blocks {
137			b.WriteString(blk.Raw)
138			b.WriteByte('\n')
139			tr, ok := translations[i]
140			if !ok || blk.Kind != Prose {
141				continue
142			}
143			for j, ln := range strings.Split(strings.TrimRight(tr, "\n"), "\n") {
144				prefix := "  ↳ "
145				if j > 0 {
146					prefix = "    "
147				}
148				b.WriteString(dim(prefix + ln))
149				b.WriteByte('\n')
150			}
151		}
152		return b.String()
153	}
154
```

14	// handlers holds the shared service and the (optional) bearer token.

16		svc   Service
17		token string
18	}

20	// translateRequest is the POST /v1/translate body. Only text is required; the rest
21	// fall back to the server's resolved defaults.
22	type translateRequest struct {
23		Text         string `json:"text"`
24		Source       string `json:"source,omitempty"`
25		Target       string `json:"target,omitempty"`
26		Preset       string `json:"preset,omitempty"`
27		Instructions string `json:"instructions,omitempty"`
28		Model        string `json:"model,omitempty"`
29		MaxAlts      int    `json:"max_alts,omitempty"`
30		Pair         *bool  `json:"pair,omitempty"`
31	}
32	
33	func (r translateRequest) params() appcore.Params {
34		return appcore.Params{
35			Text:         r.Text,
36			Source:       r.Source,
37			Target:       r.Target,
38			Preset:       r.Preset,
39			Instructions: r.Instructions,
40			Model:        r.Model,
41			MaxAlts:      r.MaxAlts,
42			Pair:         r.Pair,
43		}
44	}
45	
46	func (h *handlers) translate(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
47		var req translateRequest
48		if !decodeJSON(w, r, &req) {
49			return
50		}
51		if strings.TrimSpace(req.Text) == "" {
52			writeError(w, http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, "empty_input", `field "text" is required`)
53			return
54		}
55		res, err := h.svc.Translate(r.Context(), req.params())
56		if err != nil {
57			writeEngineError(w, err)
58			return
59		}
60		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, res)
61	}
62	
63	// defineRequest is the POST /v1/define body.
64	type defineRequest struct {
65		Word string `json:"word"`
66	}
67	
68	func (h *handlers) define(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
69		var req defineRequest
70		if !decodeJSON(w, r, &req) {
71			return
72		}
73		if strings.TrimSpace(req.Word) == "" {
74			writeError(w, http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, "empty_input", `field "word" is required`)
75			return
76		}
77		res, err := h.svc.Define(r.Context(), req.Word)
78		if err != nil {
79			writeEngineError(w, err)
80			return
81		}
82		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, res)

85	// dictSearch serves GET /v1/dict/search?q=&limit= — ranked dictionary headwords
86	// with definition previews, for a type-ahead picker.
87	//
88	// Unlike /v1/define, an empty or unmatched query is 200 with an empty candidate
89	// list rather than 422: this endpoint is called on every keystroke, and "nothing
90	// yet" is a normal answer, not a client error.
91	func (h *handlers) dictSearch(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
92		q := strings.TrimSpace(r.URL.Query().Get("q"))
93		limit := parseLimit(r.URL.Query().Get("limit"), 12)
94		res, err := h.svc.SearchDict(r.Context(), q, limit)
95		if err != nil {
96			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "dict_error", err.Error())
97			return
98		}
99		if res.Candidates == nil {
100			res.Candidates = []engine.Candidate{} // encode [] not null
101		}
102		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, res)
103	}
104	
105	// history serves GET /v1/history?q=&limit=. With q it fuzzy-searches, else it
106	// returns the most recent records. Token-guarded (personal data).
107	func (h *handlers) history(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
108		q := strings.TrimSpace(r.URL.Query().Get("q"))
109		limit := parseLimit(r.URL.Query().Get("limit"), 20)
110		var (
111			recs []store.Record
112			err  error
113		)
114		if q != "" {
115			recs, err = h.svc.HistorySearch(r.Context(), q, limit)
116		} else {
117			recs, err = h.svc.HistoryRecent(r.Context(), limit)
118		}
119		if err != nil {
120			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "history_error", err.Error())
121			return
122		}
123		if recs == nil {
124			recs = []store.Record{} // encode [] not null when history is empty/disabled
125		}
126		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, recs)
127	}
128	
129	func (h *handlers) healthz(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
130		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "ok"})
131	}
132	
133	// requireToken wraps a handler with bearer-token auth when a token is configured.
134	// With no token, it is a pass-through (loopback is the only guard).
135	func (h *handlers) requireToken(next http.HandlerFunc) http.HandlerFunc {
136		return func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
137			if h.token != "" {
138				got := bearerToken(r.Header.Get("Authorization"))
139				if subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(got), []byte(h.token)) != 1 {
140					writeError(w, http.StatusUnauthorized, "unauthorized", "missing or invalid bearer token")
141					return
142				}
143			}
144			next(w, r)
145		}
146	}
147	
148	// bearerToken extracts the token from an "Authorization: Bearer <token>" header.
149	func bearerToken(header string) string {
150		const prefix = "Bearer "
151		if len(header) >= len(prefix) && strings.EqualFold(header[:len(prefix)], prefix) {
152			return strings.TrimSpace(header[len(prefix):])
153		}
154		return ""
155	}
156	
157	// parseLimit parses a positive integer limit, falling back to def.
158	func parseLimit(s string, def int) int {
159		if s == "" {
160			return def
161		}
162		n, err := strconv.Atoi(s)
163		if err != nil || n <= 0 {
164			return def
165		}
166		return n
167	}

10		"strconv"
11		"time"
12	
13		"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/appcore"
14		"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/engine"
15		"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/store"
16	)
17	
18	// Service is the subset of appcore.Service the HTTP handlers depend on.
19	// *appcore.Service satisfies it; tests inject a fake without touching the network.
20	type Service interface {
21		Translate(ctx context.Context, p appcore.Params) (*engine.TranslateResult, error)
22		TranslateStream(ctx context.Context, p appcore.Params, onToken func(string)) (*engine.TranslateResult, error)
23		Define(ctx context.Context, word string) (*engine.TranslateResult, error)
24		SearchDict(ctx context.Context, q string, limit int) (*engine.SearchResult, error)
25		HistoryRecent(ctx context.Context, limit int) ([]store.Record, error)
26		HistorySearch(ctx context.Context, query string, limit int) ([]store.Record, error)
27	}
28	
29	// Options configures the HTTP server.
30	type Options struct {
31		Bind  string // bind address (loopback enforced unless Token is set)
32		Port  int
33		Token string // bearer token guarding /v1/history; "" => no auth
34	}
35	
36	// Server is the translate HTTP API server (loopback-only by default).
37	type Server struct {
38		httpSrv *http.Server
39		addr    string
40	}
41	
42	// New builds the server, enforcing the loopback-or-token rule and wiring routes.
43	func New(svc Service, opt Options) (*Server, error) {
44		if err := checkBind(opt.Bind, opt.Token); err != nil {
45			return nil, err
46		}
47		h := &handlers{svc: svc, token: opt.Token}
48		addr := net.JoinHostPort(opt.Bind, strconv.Itoa(opt.Port))
49		return &Server{
50			httpSrv: &http.Server{
51				Addr:              addr,
52				Handler:           newMux(h),
53				ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
54			},
55			addr: addr,
56		}, nil
57	}
58	
59	// newMux registers every route. Kept separate so tests can exercise the router
60	// directly and later phases (SSE, Swagger) can add routes in one place.
61	func newMux(h *handlers) *http.ServeMux {
62		mux := http.NewServeMux()
63		mux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/translate", h.translate)
64		mux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/translate/stream", h.translateStream)
65		mux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/define", h.define)
66		// Not token-guarded: dictionary headwords are public reference data, unlike
67		// /v1/history which is the user's own text.
68		mux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/dict/search", h.dictSearch)
69		mux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/history", h.requireToken(h.history))
70		mux.HandleFunc("GET /healthz", h.healthz)
71		registerDocs(mux)
72		return mux
73	}
74	
75	// Addr is the resolved listen address (host:port).
76	func (s *Server) Addr() string { return s.addr }
77	
78	// Run serves until ctx is cancelled, then gracefully shuts down (5s drain).
79	func (s *Server) Run(ctx context.Context) error {
80		ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", s.httpSrv.Addr)
81		if err != nil {
82			return err
83		}
84		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "translate: HTTP API on http://%s (docs: /docs)\n", s.addr)
85		errCh := make(chan error, 1)
86		go func() { errCh <- s.httpSrv.Serve(ln) }()
87	
88		select {
89		case <-ctx.Done():
90			shutCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
91			defer cancel()
92			return s.httpSrv.Shutdown(shutCtx)
93		case err := <-errCh:
94			if errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
95				return nil
96			}
97			return err
98		}
99	}
100	
101	// checkBind enforces the loopback-or-token rule: a non-loopback bind is refused
102	// unless a token is configured, since history is personal data.
103	func checkBind(bind, token string) error {
104		if isLoopback(bind) || token != "" {
105			return nil
106		}
107		return fmt.Errorf("refusing to bind non-loopback address %q without a token (history is personal data); bind 127.0.0.1 or set [server].token / token_env", bind)
108	}
109	
110	func isLoopback(bind string) bool {
111		if bind == "localhost" {
112			return true
113		}
114		ip := net.ParseIP(bind)
115		return ip != nil && ip.IsLoopback()
116	}
117
```
</details></tool-use>
