```text
1	package server
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"fmt"
6		"io"
7		"net/http"
8		"strings"
9	
10		"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/appcore"
11	)
12	
13	// translateStream serves GET /v1/translate/stream as Server-Sent Events. It is a
14	// GET (browser EventSource is GET-only) taking query params, and emits:
15	//
16	//	event: token    data: "<json-encoded token>"   (zero or more)
17	//	event: warning  data: "<message>"              (only if the result was truncated)
18	//	event: done     data: <TranslateResult JSON>   (terminal, success)
19	//	event: error    data: "<message>"              (terminal, failure)
20	//
21	// Payloads are always JSON so multi-line tokens survive SSE's line framing.
22	//
23	// Note: visible token cadence depends on the upstream provider — copilot-proxy
24	// buffers Claude /v1/messages, so Claude models still arrive in a burst regardless
25	// of this transport. SSE's win is dict/google/OpenAI-style providers and fan-out.
26	func (h *handlers) translateStream(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
27		q := r.URL.Query()
28		text := strings.TrimSpace(q.Get("text"))
29		if text == "" {
30			writeError(w, http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, "empty_input", `query param "text" is required`)
31			return
32		}
33		flusher, ok := w.(http.Flusher)
34		if !ok {
35			writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "no_flush", "streaming is not supported by this server")
36			return
37		}
38	
39		p := appcore.Params{
40			Text:         text,
41			Source:       q.Get("source"),
42			Target:       q.Get("target"),
43			Preset:       q.Get("preset"),
44			Instructions: q.Get("instructions"),
45			Model:        q.Get("model"),
46			Pair:         parseBoolPtr(q.Get("pair")),
47		}
48	
49		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
50		w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
51		w.Header().Set("Connection", "keep-alive")
52		w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no") // disable proxy buffering (nginx)
53		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
54		flusher.Flush() // commit headers so the client opens the stream immediately
55	
56		onToken := func(tok string) {
57			writeSSEString(w, "token", tok)
58			flusher.Flush()
59		}
60		// r.Context() cancels on client disconnect and is threaded through the engine,
61		// aborting the upstream LLM request — no extra plumbing needed.
62		res, err := h.svc.TranslateStream(r.Context(), p, onToken)
63		if err != nil {
64			writeSSEString(w, "error", err.Error())
65			flusher.Flush()
66			return
67		}
68		// Truncated is transient (json:"-"), so it would vanish from the done payload —
69		// surface it explicitly as a warning before the terminal event.
70		if res.Truncated {
71			writeSSEString(w, "warning", "result was truncated (max_tokens); output is partial")
72			flusher.Flush()
73		}
74		writeSSEJSON(w, "done", res)
75		flusher.Flush()
76	}
77	
78	// writeSSE writes one framed SSE event with an already-JSON data payload.
79	func writeSSE(w io.Writer, event string, data []byte) {
80		fmt.Fprintf(w, "event: %s\ndata: %s\n\n", event, data)
81	}
82	
83	// writeSSEString frames a string payload (JSON-encoded so it stays single-line).
84	func writeSSEString(w io.Writer, event, s string) {
85		b, _ := json.Marshal(s)
86		writeSSE(w, event, b)
87	}
88	
89	// writeSSEJSON frames an arbitrary value as compact JSON.
90	func writeSSEJSON(w io.Writer, event string, v any) {
91		b, err := json.Marshal(v)
92		if err != nil {
93			writeSSEString(w, "error", "failed to encode result: "+err.Error())
94			return
95		}
96		writeSSE(w, event, b)
97	}
98	
99	// parseBoolPtr maps a query flag to a tri-state *bool (absent => nil).
100	func parseBoolPtr(s string) *bool {
101		if s == "" {
102			return nil
103		}
104		v := s == "1" || strings.EqualFold(s, "true") || strings.EqualFold(s, "yes") || strings.EqualFold(s, "on")
105		return &v
106	}
107
```

```text
1	# Raycast integration for `translate`
2	
3	Bring `translate` into [Raycast](https://raycast.com) — translate from root
4	search or a global hotkey, backed by the **existing `translate` binary** (this
5	directory contains no translation logic; it shells out to the CLI).
6	
7	There are two independent tracks. **The TypeScript extension is the primary,
8	full-featured path;** the script commands are an optional zero-Node fallback.
9	
10	| Track | Path | Build | Best for |
11	|---|---|---|---|
12	| **TypeScript extension** (primary) | [`extension/`](extension/) | `npm` / `ray` | full UI: live translate, selection prefill, define, history, engine switch, streaming |
13	| **Script Commands** (bash, optional) | [`script-commands/`](script-commands/) | none | zero-Node fallback; one-shot translate/define |
14	
15	Everything requires the `translate` CLI on the machine:
16	
17	```sh
18	just install                                  # → ~/.local/bin/translate
19	# or
20	brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate
21	```
22	
23	## Track A — Script Commands (optional)
24	
25	The TypeScript extension (Track B) supersedes these; keep them only if you want a
26	zero-Node fallback that runs without `ray develop`.
27	
28	```sh
29	just raycast-scripts   # chmod +x the scripts and print the directory to add
30	```
31	
32	Then, **one time** in Raycast: **Settings → Extensions → Script Commands →
33	Add Script Directory** → select `raycast/script-commands`. (There is no CLI to
34	register a script directory; this step is manual.)
35	
36	Commands: **Translate Text** (language dropdown + text), **Translate & Copy**
37	(copies the result; leave the text blank to translate the clipboard — Script
38	Commands can't read the selection), **Define Word** (dictionary lookup).
39	
40	## Track B — TypeScript extension (local dev)
41	
42	```sh
43	just raycast-dev       # npm install (first run) + `ray develop`
44	```
45	
46	`ray develop` registers the extension with the running Raycast app and hot-reloads.
47	Four commands appear in root search and **stay installed after you stop
48	`ray develop`** — no store publish needed for personal use:
49	**Translate** (type-to-translate, language dropdown, engine-override submenu,
50	streaming ⌘↵, Copy/Paste/Speak), **Translate Selection** (grabs the selection or
51	clipboard and opens Translate prefilled, with an optional target-language argument),
52	**Translate Text** (a `Form.TextArea` for whole paragraphs — Raycast's search bar
53	refuses a long paste, and that limit is the app's, not ours),
54	**Define** (single-result dictionary lookup + LLM fallback), **Look up Word**
55	(a Define Word-style picker: recent lookups when empty, ranked headword candidates
56	with previews as you type, a full definition page on ↵), and **History**
57	(browse/search past translations). `just raycast-build` / `just raycast-lint`
58	type-check and lint.
59	
60	Configure the binary path and defaults in the extension's **Preferences**
61	(the binary is auto-probed in `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`,
62	`/usr/local/bin`, `~/go/bin`; override with an absolute path if it lives elsewhere).
63	Translate-as-you-type is **debounced** (default 700 ms, tunable via the
64	"Live translate debounce" preference) and cancels superseded in-flight requests,
65	so typing a phrase doesn't fire an LLM call per keystroke. Opening **Translate**
66	seeds the input from the current selection (or clipboard) per the "Prefill input
67	from" preference — the shipped default is "Nothing", but note that Raycast applies a
68	default only when no value is stored yet, so an install that ran an older version
69	keeps whatever it saved (change it explicitly in Raycast → Extensions → Translate).
70	
71	**Look up Word** types against the local dictionary only (`translate dict search`,
72	~30 ms), so the LLM is called when you open a word, not per keystroke — and opening
73	a word is also what writes the history row. Run `translate dict update all` once for
74	the offline dictionaries, plus `translate dict reindex` on an existing install to
75	make Chinese lookups ~20× faster without re-downloading.
76	
77	## Gotchas (both tracks)
78	
79	- **Raycast runs under launchd with a restricted PATH** — it does *not* inherit
80	  your shell's PATH, so a bare `translate` fails with `command not found` /
81	  `spawn translate ENOENT`. Both tracks resolve an **absolute** path. Always test
82	  **from Raycast**, not a terminal (a terminal's PATH hides the bug). See
83	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md).
84	- **API keys must live in `translate`'s config**, not shell env — a key exported
85	  in `~/.zshrc` is absent under launchd. Put providers/keys in
86	  `~/.config/translate/config.toml` (run `translate init`); `HOME` is passed
87	  through so the CLI finds it.
88	- **Exit code is 0 even when an engine fails** (it falls back). The extension
89	  surfaces `warnings[]` from `--json`; the plain-text scripts don't show them.
90	
91	See [`../docs/raycast-extension.md`](../docs/raycast-extension.md) for how Raycast
92	extensions work, the full integration-tier comparison, and the competitive
93	landscape. Store publishing is tracked in
94	[`../backlog/raycast-extension.md`](../backlog/raycast-extension.md).
95
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Translate
2	
3	Translate, define, and speak text from Raycast — backed by the local
4	[`translate`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/translate) CLI. Multi-engine
5	auto-fallback (local LLM via copilot-proxy / Ollama, keyless Google, offline
6	CC-CEDICT / ECDICT dictionaries), unified history, and free TTS.
7	
8	## Requirements
9	
10	This extension **shells out to the `translate` CLI** — it does not translate on its
11	own. Install the binary first:
12	
13	```sh
14	brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate
15	# or, with a Go toolchain:
16	go install github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@latest
17	```
18	
19	On first run, `translate init` sets up your providers/config
20	(`~/.config/translate/config.toml`). The extension auto-detects the binary in
21	`~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, and `~/go/bin`; if it lives
22	elsewhere, set **“translate binary path”** in the extension preferences. (If it
23	isn’t found, the extension shows an install-instructions screen instead of failing.)
24	
25	> **Note:** Raycast runs under a restricted `PATH` and reads no shell env, so API
26	> keys must live in `translate`’s config file (via `translate init`), not in
27	> `~/.zshrc`. “Translate Selection” and selection-prefill need macOS **Accessibility**
28	> permission for Raycast (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility).
29	
30	## Commands
31	
32	- **Translate** — type to translate; pick the target language; ⌘↵ for a streaming
33	  view; actions for Copy / Paste / Speak and an engine override.
34	- **Translate Text** — a multi-line box for whole paragraphs. Raycast's search bar
35	  refuses a long paste ("the text you are trying to paste is too long"), and that
36	  limit is the app's, not ours — so long text gets its own form. ⌘⇧S loads the
37	  selection, ⌘⇧V the clipboard, ⌘↵ streams, ⌘⇧A reveals engine + model.
38	- **Translate Selection** — grabs your selection (or clipboard) and opens Translate
39	  prefilled and editable.
40	- **Look up Word** — a dictionary picker: an empty search bar lists your recent
41	  lookups, typing shows ranked headword candidates with definition previews, and ↵
42	  opens a full definition page (which is also what records the lookup in history).
43	  Pick the definition language before opening the command or from the dropdown
44	  inside it. Typing only reads the local dictionary — the LLM is called when you
45	  open a word, not while you type.
46	- **Define** — single-result dictionary lookup with phonetics and meanings (offline
47	  dictionaries, LLM fallback, and suggestions).
48	- **History** — browse and search your past translations.
49	
50	For the best **Look up Word** experience run `translate dict update all` once
51	(offline CC-CEDICT + ECDICT); existing installs should also run
52	`translate dict reindex`, which makes Chinese lookups ~20× faster without
53	re-downloading anything.
54	
55	Every target dropdown leads with **Auto**, which follows the bidirectional pair
56	configured in `translate` (`pair` + `pair_with`) — the equivalent of `^g` in the
57	TUI. Picking a specific language instead always translates *into* it.
58	
59	## Preferences
60	
61	Binary path, default target language, engine, model tier, live-translate debounce,
62	and how Translate prefills its input (selection / clipboard / nothing). Leave
63	**target / tier / debounce** empty to inherit them from the `translate` config
64	(`~/.config/translate/config.toml`, read via `config show --json`) — configure them
65	once and Raycast honors them; set a preference to override the config for Raycast.
66	
67	> Raycast applies a preference's default **only when no value is stored yet**. If a
68	> command still behaves per an older default, change the setting explicitly in
69	> Raycast → Extensions → Translate.
70
```

```text
1	# Raycast integration — reference
2	
3	How `translate` plugs into [Raycast](https://raycast.com), the options we
4	weighed, how the shipped integration works, and how it compares to existing
5	translation extensions. This is present-tense reference reading; the actual code
6	lives in [`../raycast/`](../raycast/), and store-publishing is tracked in
7	[`../backlog/raycast-extension.md`](../backlog/raycast-extension.md).
8	
9	**Core principle: reuse the binary, don't reimplement.** Every tier below shells
10	out to the existing `translate` CLI (`--json`) and renders the result. No
11	translation, engine, or dictionary logic is duplicated in TypeScript/bash.
12	
13	## Integration tiers
14	
15	Raycast offers four ways to surface functionality. We ship the middle two.
16	
17	| Tier | Reuses binary? | Effort | Selection → translate | Persisted defaults | Rich UI / history | Streaming | Distribution |
18	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
19	| **Quick Link** | ✗ (can't exec) | 5 min | via deeplink only | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | launcher only |
20	| **Script Command** (bash) — *shipped* | ✓ | ~0.5 h | ✗ (needs `pbpaste`) | ✗ (no prefs) | ✗ (plain text) | only `fullOutput` | Add Script Directory |
21	| **TS Extension** (`@raycast/api`) — *shipped* | ✓ | 1–2 d | ✓ `getSelectedText()` | ✓ preferences | ✓ List/Detail/Actions | ✓ (manual `spawn`) | `npm run dev` / store |
22	| **AI Extension** (tools) | ✓ | +0.5 d | AI-orchestrated | — | AI Chat | `AI.ask` | store; **Pro-gated** |
23	
24	- **Quick Links** open a URL/file/app/`raycast://` deeplink — they have no
25	  shell-exec surface, so they can't run the CLI directly. Useful only as a hotkey
26	  that deeplinks into a real command.
27	- **AI Extensions** expose "tools" the Raycast AI can call. Feasible (a tool file
28	  can `execFile` the binary and return its `--json`), but the AI API requires
29	  **Raycast Pro**, so it's an additive Pro-only layer — deferred.
30	
31	## How Raycast extensions work
32	
33	- **Manifest** (`package.json`): a `commands[]` array; each command has a
34	  required `mode`:
35	  - `view` — default-exports a React (TSX) component (our `Translate`).
36	  - `no-view` — default-exports an async function; runs and exits, no UI
37	    (our `Translate Selection` → `getSelectedText` → `Clipboard.paste` + `showHUD`).
38	  - `menu-bar` — a persistent `MenuBarExtra` (not used yet).
39	- **Running the binary:** extensions run in a Node runtime, so `child_process`
40	  works. We use `execFile` (typed wrapper in
41	  [`../raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts`](../raycast/extension/src/lib/translate.ts))
42	  rather than the `useExec` hook, because `useExec` buffers with a 10 s default
43	  timeout that LLM engines exceed (and its `timeout: 0` is coerced back to 10000).
44	  The CLI's **`--stream` flag** forces token streaming even when stdout is piped
45	  (which Raycast always is; without it the CLI treats non-TTY as buffered). A
46	  streaming `Detail` view can spawn `translate … --stream` and append `stdout`
47	  chunks into React state bound to `Detail.markdown`. Caveat: visible progressive
48	  output depends on the provider — ollama streams; **copilot-proxy currently buffers
49	  its claude `/v1/messages` responses**, so the result appears after first-token
50	  latency. The default live view uses `--json` (buffered, structured), which returns
51	  fast enough.
52	- **Preferences** (`getPreferenceValues()`): persisted per-extension settings —
53	  our `binaryPath`, `defaultTarget`, `engine`, `tier`.
54	- **Input/UI:** `getSelectedText()` (frontmost app's selection),
55	  `Clipboard.copy/paste`, `Action.CopyToClipboard`/`Action.Paste`; `List` +
56	  `List.Dropdown` (searchBarAccessory, `storeValue` to remember the last target);
57	  `Detail`/`List.Item.Detail` with `.Metadata` for structured fields; `showHUD`/
58	  `showToast` for feedback.
59	- **Tooling:** the `ray` CLI (ships in the extension's dev deps). `ray develop`
60	  (`npm run dev`) registers the extension with the running Raycast app and
61	  hot-reloads; **it persists in root search after you stop dev** — no store
62	  publish needed for personal use. `ray build`/`ray lint` type-check and lint.
63	
64	## Gotchas (learned the hard way)
65	
66	- **launchd PATH:** Raycast launches under launchd and does *not* inherit your
67	  shell PATH, so a bare `translate` fails with `ENOENT` / `command not found`.
68	  Both tracks resolve an **absolute** path (preference first, then probe
69	  `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/go/bin`). Always test
70	  **from Raycast**, not a terminal (a terminal's PATH hides the bug). See
71	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-translate-not-found.md).
72	- **HOME / config, not shell env:** the CLI reads providers/keys from
73	  `~/.config/translate/config.toml`, *not* environment variables. A key exported
74	  in `~/.zshrc` is absent under launchd — put it in the config (`translate init`).
75	  We pass `HOME` through so the CLI finds its config.
76	- **Exit code is 0 even on engine failure** (auto-fallback), so we read
77	  `warnings[]` from `--json` rather than branching on exit codes. The extension
78	  surfaces warnings in the Detail pane / HUD; the plain-text scripts don't.
79	- **Extension icons must be a real PNG** (512×512) — emoji icons work only for
80	  Script Commands. `ray build`/`lint` complains otherwise.
81	- **A preference `default` only applies when no value is stored.** Changing a
82	  `default` in `package.json` does *not* reach an install that has already
83	  materialized that preference — Raycast keeps the stored value, and the new
84	  default is inert. Symptom: a behaviour you "fixed" in the manifest persists. See
85	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-still-prefills-clipboard-after-default-changed-to-nothing.md).
86	  Corollary: read preferences through the generated `Preferences.<Command>` type,
87	  not a hand-written interface — the generated one makes the field required, so a
88	  code default that drifts from the manifest becomes a compile error.
89	- **The extension runs the *installed* binary, not your working tree.**
90	  `resolveBinary()` probes `~/.local/bin` → `/opt/homebrew/bin` → `/usr/local/bin`
91	  → `~/go/bin`, so `just raycast-dev` alone never picks up a CLI change. When a
92	  change spans both, the loop is `just check && just install && just raycast-dev`.
93	  Worse, an old binary fails *silently*: `translate` takes free text as its first
94	  argument, so an unknown subcommand gets translated and exits 0
95	  (`translate models` → "n. 模型…"). Never probe capability by exit status. See
96	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-extension-uses-installed-binary-not-working-tree.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-extension-uses-installed-binary-not-working-tree.md).
97	- **The search bar refuses a long paste** ("The text you are trying to paste is
98	  too long"). That guard is in the Raycast app binary, not `@raycast/api`, so it
99	  can't be raised or caught, and it applies to every search-bar command. Long
100	  text needs a `Form.TextArea` — that is what the `translate-text` command is.
101	  Behind it, argv caps at `ARG_MAX` (1 MiB), so `src/lib/translate.ts` pipes to
102	  stdin above 128 KB. See
103	  [`../pitfalls/raycast-search-bar-refuses-long-paste.md`](../pitfalls/raycast-search-bar-refuses-long-paste.md).
104	- **Command arguments are static manifest data** and can't be populated at
105	  runtime, so a language argument is necessarily a hand-synced subset. In-view
106	  `List.Dropdown`s can call `translate lang list --json` for the full table.
107	
108	## Competitive landscape (2026)
109	
110	The Raycast translation category is crowded, but the field is almost entirely
111	remote-API/cloud-LLM wrappers configured via extension preferences.
112	
113	| Extension | Backend | Streaming | TTS | History | Offline dict |
114	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
115	| gebeto/translate (Google) | Google web (keyless) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
116	| tisfeng/Easydict | 10 remote providers + Apple `say`/Shortcuts | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ (remote) |
117	| douo/openai-translator | multi-LLM incl. Ollama / custom endpoint | ✓ | ✗ (roadmap) | ✓ | ✗ |
118	| deepcast / itranslate | DeepL / multi (BYO API key) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
119	| Raycast built-in Translate | unstated | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ (Pro-gated) |
120	
121	**What `translate` does that they don't:**
122	
123	- **Shells out to a dedicated local translator CLI** — no surveyed extension
124	  wraps a standalone translator binary (Easydict shells to `osascript`/Apple
125	  Shortcuts; none to a CLI like this).
126	- **Automatic multi-engine failover** — competitors that support multiple engines
127	  do *parallel aggregation*, not "try A, on failure fall back to B".
128	- **Offline CC-CEDICT / ECDICT dictionaries** via `translate define` — all
129	  competitors' dictionaries are remote.
130	- **Unified, searchable history** (`translate history [search]`).
131	- **Free local TTS** (`--speak`) — note openai-translator lists TTS as an
132	  unshipped roadmap item, so this is a real gap.
133	- **Fuzzy language resolution** (`translate lang resolve`, `chinees → zh`).
134	
135	Frame differentiation as **offline-resilient + auto-fallback + unified history**,
136	*not* "local LLM" (openai-translator already reaches Ollama) and *not* "study
137	modes" (Anki / Vocabulary Builder already exist in the store).
138	
139	## How ours is built
140	
141	- **Script Commands** — [`../raycast/script-commands/`](../raycast/script-commands/):
142	  `translate-text` (dropdown language + text, `fullOutput`), `translate-and-copy`
143	  (`silent`, copies; blank arg → clipboard), `define-word`. Install:
144	  `just raycast-scripts`, then add the directory in Raycast once.
145	- **TS extension** — [`../raycast/extension/`](../raycast/extension/): commands
146	  `translate` (view: type-to-translate, language dropdown, engine-override submenu,
147	  Copy/Paste/Speak, typo "did you mean?" suggestions, opt-in selection prefill),
148	  `translate-selection` (no-view:
149	  grabs the selection/clipboard and opens Translate prefilled via `launchCommand` —
150	  editable, not blind-paste), `define` (view: dictionary lookup +
151	  LLM fallback + "did you mean" suggestions), `look-up-word` (view: the Define
152	  Word-style picker, below), `translate-text` (view: a `Form.TextArea` for
153	  passages the search bar refuses, below), and `history` (view: browse/search
154	  past translations). All share `src/lib/translate.ts` (binary resolve + typed
155	  `execFile` wrappers mirroring `internal/engine/engine.go`'s `TranslateResult`).
156	  Run: `just raycast-dev` (`build`/`lint` variants exist). Live translate is
157	  debounced + abortable to avoid an LLM call per keystroke, with an opt-in `⌘↵`
158	  streaming view (`spawnTranslateStream` → `translate … --stream` → live `Detail`).
159	  Typo suggestions reuse the engine's fuzzy `suggestions[]` (a shared
160	  `did-you-mean.tsx` component) — no CLI change; single-word lookups route to the
161	  offline dict, full sentences to the LLM which corrects implicitly. Default target,
162	  live-debounce, and tier are inherited from the CLI config (`config show --json`)
163	  when the matching Raycast preference is empty, so `config.toml` is the single
164	  source of truth (a Raycast preference overrides it).
165	
166	### `look-up-word` — the Define Word-style picker
167	
168	Modeled on Raycast's built-in **Define Word**: an empty search bar lists recent
169	history; typing shows ranked headword candidates with definition previews;
170	`⏎` pushes a full-page `Detail`.
171	
172	Three rules shape it, and each is worth preserving:
173	
174	1. **Typing is local-only.** The list is backed by `translate dict search --json`,
175	   which reads the dictionary databases and nothing else (~30 ms). An LLM call per
176	   keystroke would take ~6 s and be unusable, so the LLM fallback is deferred to
177	   `⏎` — either on a fuzzy candidate or on the explicit *Ask the LLM* row that
178	   appears when no local headword matched.
179	2. **Only `⏎` writes history.** `dict search` opens no history store at all, so the
180	   typing path *cannot* record; `DefineDetail` calls `define` without
181	   `--no-history`, so opening a word remembers it. The old `define` command passes
182	   `--no-history` because it looks up on every keystroke.
183	3. **Language is pickable before and after opening.** A command *argument*
184	   dropdown appears in the Raycast root bar; an in-view `List.Dropdown` (populated
185	   from `translate lang list --json`) changes it later. Both only steer the LLM
186	   fallback — the offline tiers are script-fixed (ECDICT en→zh, CC-CEDICT zh→en) —
187	   and the Detail metadata says so rather than letting the choice look ignored.
188	
189	`define` is kept alongside it, unchanged, so the two UXes can be compared.
190	New components: `lib/define-detail.tsx` (full-page definition, the only history
191	writer), `lib/history-detail.tsx` (a stored record as a page — no re-run, instant),
192	`lib/language-dropdown.tsx`. `lib/did-you-mean.tsx` is deliberately *not* reused
193	here: its `⏎` re-runs the search, whereas in this list `⏎` must define.
194	
195	### `translate-text` — the long-passage escape hatch
196	
197	Every other command takes its input in the search bar, which Raycast caps: a long
198	paste is refused outright, and the extension never even sees it. This command is a
199	`Form.TextArea` plus target/engine dropdowns; submitting pushes the same full-page
200	`Detail` (`lib/translation-detail.tsx`), with `⌘↵` for the streaming view.
201	
202	Nothing is prefilled — *Load Selection* (`⌘⇧S`) and *Load Clipboard* (`⌘⇧V`) are
203	explicit actions, keeping the lesson from `e87db06` that auto-grabbing input on
204	open is surprising. `⌘⇧A` reveals **Engine** and **Model**; both stay hidden by
205	default so the common case is two fields.
206	
207	The Model list comes from `translate models --json` — the models the configured
208	providers *declare*, one per tier. Deliberately not a live `/v1/models` probe:
209	copilot-proxy advertises ids it then refuses to serve, so a probed list would
210	offer choices that fail at request time. Picking a model also selects its
211	provider, since `llama3.2:3b` belongs to ollama regardless of chain order.
212	
213	Past 128 KB of UTF-8, `src/lib/translate.ts` stops putting the text in argv and
214	pipes it to stdin (`execWithStdin`), because macOS caps a whole argument list at
215	`ARG_MAX` = 1 MiB. The CLI already reads stdin when given no text argument, so
216	this needed no CLI change. The provider is the real ceiling long before either
217	limit: Google puts the text in a GET query string and fails around 180 KB.
218	
219	Result metadata (engine · model · direction) is a dim footer line at the end of
220	the markdown rather than a `Detail.Metadata` sidebar: the sidebar is a permanent
221	third of the window, which is a lot of width to spend on five short labels when
222	the whole point of the view is reading room.
223	
224	### Target language: the **Auto** entry
225	
226	Both target dropdowns (`translate`, `translate-text`) lead with
227	`Auto — <home> ⇄ <away>`, the dropdown equivalent of the TUI's `^g`. It is not
228	cosmetic:
229	
230	With `[general] pair = true` the CLI reroutes home-language input to `pair_with`
231	regardless of `--to`, so before this the dropdown was quietly lying — picking
232	"Chinese (Traditional)" and pasting Chinese returned *English*. Making the mode
233	explicit lets a concrete choice mean what it says: the extension now sends
234	`--no-pair` whenever a specific language is picked, and no `--to` at all for Auto.
235	`--no-pair` had to be added to the CLI for this; there was previously no way to
236	turn pair off for one run.
237	
238	`lib/language-dropdown.tsx` reads the pair from `config show --json`, so the entry
239	is labelled with the real codes and is omitted when no `pair_with` is configured.
240	
241	## Publishing & distribution
242	
243	The journey from local development to the store, and why we default to
244	local/personal for now.
245	
246	### Three distribution paths
247	
248	| Path | Review | Audience | How | Our stance |
249	|---|---|---|---|---|
250	| **Local dev** | none | just you | `just raycast-dev` (`ray develop`) — persists in root search after you stop dev | **current default** |
251	| **Private / org store** | none (org-gated) | your Raycast org | set `owner` in package.json → `npm run publish`; needs Raycast Pro/Team | option if sharing to a team |
252	| **Public store** | **human review** | everyone | `npm run publish` opens a PR to `raycast/extensions` → CI + Raycast-team review → merge auto-publishes | deferred → [../backlog/raycast-extension.md](../backlog/raycast-extension.md) |
253	
254	### It is *not* like PyPI
255	
256	PyPI is self-service: register + `twine upload`, published instantly, no review.
257	The Raycast **public** store is curated — closer to Homebrew core:
258	
259	- `npm run publish` (= `npx @raycast/api@latest publish`) **authenticates with
260	  GitHub** and auto-opens a pull request into `github.com/raycast/extensions`.
261	- Automated CI checks run, then the **Raycast team reviews** and "request[s] changes
262	  when required"; on merge it auto-publishes. Turnaround is days, not seconds.
263	- Auth is **GitHub** (for the PR). Your **Raycast account** only supplies the
264	  validated `author` handle (ours: `da-wei_lee`).
265	
266	### Public-store requirements (checklist)
267	
268	Verified against developers.raycast.com. `✓` = done in this repo.
269	
270	- `✓` `author` = registered Raycast username; `license: "MIT"`; ≥1 category;
271	  one-sentence description; `platforms`; `package-lock.json`; `npm run build` +
272	  `ray lint` clean.
273	- `✓` **512×512 PNG icon** that reads in light + dark (not the default Raycast icon).
274	- `✓` **`CHANGELOG.md`** at the extension root (h2 headers; `{PR_MERGE_DATE}` placeholder).
275	- `✓` **`README.md`** at the extension root (setup/onboarding; media under a top-level
276	  `media/` folder).
277	- `☐` **≥3 (max 6) screenshots at 2000×1250 PNG** — captured from the *running*
278	  extension (a GUI step; not scriptable here).
279	- `☐` `npm run publish` (GitHub auth) + choose public vs private.
280	
281	### The binary-dependency hurdle
282	
283	The store guideline *"Avoid asking users to perform additional downloads"* is exactly
284	our case — the extension needs a user-installed `translate` (brew / `go install`).
285	"Calling known system binaries" is allowed, but a custom go-install CLI is a gray
286	area reviewers may push back on. Mitigations already in place:
287	
288	- Extension `README.md` documents the dependency + install commands.
289	- A graceful **binary-not-found onboarding** view (`src/lib/binary-not-found.tsx`) with
290	  copyable install commands + a jump to preferences — instead of a bare error.
291	- We do **not** bundle the ~22 MB Go binary (store discourages "heavy" binaries;
292	  shipping release binaries is a separate item — `backlog/release-binaries.md`).
293	
294	This friction is why the public store is deferred and local/private is the current
295	path; the analysis lives in [../backlog/raycast-extension.md](../backlog/raycast-extension.md).
296

300	- `useExec`: https://developers.raycast.com/utilities/react-hooks/useexec
301	- AI Extensions: https://developers.raycast.com/ai
302	- Script Commands: https://github.com/raycast/script-commands
303	- Prepare / Publish / Teams: https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store
304

42	// It is NOT the app version (which is the git tag; see cmd/version.go). History:

5	// TestResolveLearnImpliesPair: enabling learn (via flag) forces pair mode on, since

7	func TestResolveLearnImpliesPair(t *testing.T) {
8		c := Default()
9		c.General.Pair = false
10		got := c.Resolve(Overrides{Learn: true}, ModeCLI)
11		if !got.Learn {
12			t.Error("Learn should resolve on when the flag is set")
13		}
14		if !got.Pair {
15			t.Error("Learn should imply Pair")
16		}
17	}

19	// TestResolveLearnOverlay: a per-front-end [tui] overlay can default learn on for the
20	// TUI while the CLI stays off, mirroring the other overlay knobs.
21	func TestResolveLearnOverlay(t *testing.T) {
22		c := Default()
23		c.TUI = &Overlay{Learn: boolptr(true)}
24		if tui := c.Resolve(Overrides{}, ModeTUI); !tui.Learn || !tui.Pair {
25			t.Errorf("TUI overlay learn=true should resolve Learn && Pair, got learn=%v pair=%v", tui.Learn, tui.Pair)
26		}
27		if cli := c.Resolve(Overrides{}, ModeCLI); cli.Learn {
28			t.Error("CLI should not inherit the [tui] learn overlay")

# Translate Changelog

## [Initial Version] - {PR_MERGE_DATE}

- **Translate** — type-to-translate with a target-language dropdown, debounced live
  translation, an engine-override submenu, an opt-in streaming view (⌘↵), and
  selection/clipboard prefill.
- **Translate Selection** — grabs the current selection (or clipboard) and opens
  Translate prefilled, so you can review/edit before copying.
- **Translate Text** — a multi-line form for whole paragraphs, since Raycast's
  search bar refuses a long paste. Load the selection or clipboard explicitly,
  translate to a full page, or stream with ⌘↵. ⌘⇧A reveals engine and model.
- **Look up Word** — a Define Word-style dictionary picker: recent lookups when the
  search bar is empty, ranked headword candidates with definition previews as you
  type, and a full definition page on ↵ (which is what records the lookup). The
  definition language is pickable as a command argument or from an in-view dropdown.
  Typing reads only local dictionary data; the LLM fallback runs when you open a word.
- **Define** — dictionary lookup (offline CC-CEDICT / ECDICT) with an LLM fallback
  and "did you mean" suggestions.
- **History** — browse and search past translations.
- Target dropdowns lead with **Auto**, following the CLI's configured
  bidirectional pair (like `^g` in the TUI); picking a language always translates
  into it.
- Backed by the local `translate` CLI: multi-engine auto-fallback (local LLM via
  copilot-proxy/Ollama, keyless Google, offline dictionaries) and free TTS.

14	func newServeCmd() *cobra.Command {
15		var (
16			port      int
17			bind      string
18			token     string
19			noHistory bool
20		)
21		c := &cobra.Command{
22			Use:   "serve",
23			Short: "Run the local HTTP API server (loopback; JSON + SSE + OpenAPI)",
24			Long: "serve starts a persistent loopback HTTP service exposing the translate\n" +
25				"engine over JSON (and SSE streaming). It binds 127.0.0.1 by default; a\n" +
26				"non-loopback bind is refused unless a token is set. History is guarded by\n" +
27				"the token when one is configured.\n\n" +
28				"  translate serve                 # http://127.0.0.1:4155\n" +
29				"  translate serve --port 8080\n" +
30				"  translate serve --token \"$TOK\" --bind 0.0.0.0",
31			Args: cobra.NoArgs,
32			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
33				cfg, _, err := config.Load()
34				if err != nil {
35					return err
36				}
37				sc := cfg.ResolveServer(config.ServerOverrides{Port: port, Bind: bind, Token: token})
38				svc, err := appcore.NewService(cfg, appcore.Options{NoHistory: noHistory})
39				if err != nil {
40					return err
41				}
42				defer svc.Close()
43				srv, err := server.New(svc, server.Options{Bind: sc.Bind, Port: sc.Port, Token: sc.Token})
44				if err != nil {
45					return err
46				}
47				// Add SIGTERM to the inherited Ctrl-C context so a daemon stops cleanly.
48				ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(cmd.Context(), syscall.SIGTERM)
49				defer stop()
50				return srv.Run(ctx)
51			},
52		}
53		c.Flags().IntVar(&port, "port", 0, "listen port (default from [server].port, else 4155)")
54		c.Flags().StringVar(&bind, "bind", "", "bind address (default 127.0.0.1; loopback enforced without a token)")
55		c.Flags().StringVar(&token, "token", "", "bearer token guarding /v1/history (overrides config)")
56		c.Flags().BoolVar(&noHistory, "no-history", false, "do not read or write history")
57		return c
58	}

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash

# @raycast.schemaVersion 1
# @raycast.title Translate Text
# @raycast.mode fullOutput
# @raycast.packageName Translate
# @raycast.icon 🌐
# @raycast.argument1 { "type": "dropdown", "placeholder": "Language", "data": [ {"title":"English","value":"en"}, {"title":"Chinese (Traditional)","value":"zh-TW"}, {"title":"Chinese (Simplified)","value":"zh-CN"}, {"title":"Japanese","value":"ja"}, {"title":"Korean","value":"ko"}, {"title":"Spanish","value":"es"}, {"title":"French","value":"fr"}, {"title":"German","value":"de"}, {"title":"Italian","value":"it"}, {"title":"Portuguese","value":"pt"} ] }
# @raycast.argument2 { "type": "text", "placeholder": "Text to translate" }
# @raycast.description Translate text into the chosen language via the translate CLI.
# @raycast.author David Lee
# @raycast.authorURL https://github.com/daviddwlee84

set -euo pipefail

# Raycast runs under launchd and does NOT inherit your shell PATH, so a bare
# `translate` is usually not found. Resolve an absolute path instead.
find_translate() {
  for d in "$HOME/.local/bin" /opt/homebrew/bin /usr/local/bin "$HOME/go/bin"; do
    [ -x "$d/translate" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$d/translate"; return 0; }
  done
  command -v translate 2>/dev/null && return 0
  return 1
}

BIN="$(find_translate)" || {
  echo "translate CLI not found (looked in ~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, ~/go/bin)."
  echo "Install: 'just install' or 'brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate'."
  exit 1
}

# CLI contract: translate <text> --to <lang>. Plain stdout (no ANSI when non-TTY).
"$BIN" "$2" --to "$1"
=== git log raycast ===
9c466ea docs(raycast): the extension runs the installed binary, not your working tree
c2d31ec fix(engine): long translations no longer truncate
814a42a feat(raycast): Auto (pair) target, model picker, and a metadata footer

8d18ac3 fix(raycast): Translate honors the "Nothing" prefill default
9ffdff1 docs(raycast): note config inheritance for target/tier/debounce

1	# Publish the Raycast extension to the store
2	
3	**Status**: P? — local-dev shipped; publish deferred
4	**Effort**: L
5	**Related**: `TODO.md` P? · `raycast/extension/` · [../docs/raycast-extension.md](../docs/raycast-extension.md) · [homebrew-distribution.md](homebrew-distribution.md)
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	2026-07. The Raycast integration shipped as two local tracks (`raycast/script-commands/`
10	bash + `raycast/extension/` TypeScript). The TS extension runs via `just raycast-dev`
11	(`ray develop`) and **persists in root search after dev stops**, so personal use needs
12	no store at all. The open question is whether — and how — to distribute it beyond this
13	machine.
14	
15	## Investigation
16	
17	- **Calling a user-installed binary is a sanctioned pattern** ("✅ Calling known system
18	  binaries"). The store's hard rule targets *bundling opaque/heavy binaries*, which we
19	  don't do — we shell out to a Homebrew/`go install` `translate`.
20	- **Soft guideline friction**: the store discourages requiring users to manually install
21	  external tools ("avoid... automate where possible"). Our binary dependency is exactly
22	  that — advisory, not an auto-reject, but the most likely reviewer comment. Mitigate
23	  with graceful binary detection + a "not installed → install instructions" onboarding
24	  view + README.
25	- **Private org store** (Raycast for Teams/Pro): publish via `owner` in package.json +
26	  `npm run publish`; visible only to org members, **no public human review**. Best fit if
27	  distributing to a controlled group who all have the binary.
28	- **Public store requirements**: `author` = a *registered Raycast username* (currently
29	  fails `ray lint` — `daviddwlee84` 404s against Raycast's user API), `license: MIT`
30	  (wrapper only; the Go binary's license is untouched since we don't bundle it), a custom
31	  512×512 icon (the current one is a placeholder), ≥3 screenshots (2000×1250), a
32	  `CHANGELOG.md`, a Title-Case category, `package-lock.json`, and `ray lint` clean.
33	- **No telemetry, no Keychain**. If published, expose the openrouter API key via the
34	  Raycast preferences API (`required: true`), not by reading `config.toml`.
35	- **Platform**: mark `platforms: ["macOS"]` (already set) — the binary shell-out doesn't
36	  work on Raycast's iOS/Windows clients.
37	
38	## Options considered
39	
40	| Option | What | Verdict |
41	|---|---|---|
42	| A. Local dev only (personal) | `ray develop`, per-machine, no review | current default — done |
43	| B. Private org store (Pro/Team) | `owner` + `npm run publish`, internal-only | best if sharing to a team; needs Pro |
44	| C. Public store | PR to raycast/extensions, automated + human review | widest reach; expect binary-dependency review friction |
45	
46	## Current blocker / open questions
47	
48	- Is public publication worth it given the crowded category, or is local/private enough?
49	  (Differentiators are real — see [../docs/raycast-extension.md](../docs/raycast-extension.md)
50	  competitive section — but the binary dependency is a review headwind.)
51	- What's the binary-not-found onboarding UX (detection + actionable install view)?
52	- Register/confirm the Raycast `author` handle before any publish (blocks `ray lint`).
53	
54	## Decision (if any)
55	
56	`2026-07 deferred` — ship the local-dev extension first and dogfood it; **private/
57	personal is the current path**, public store stays deferred.
58	
59	Publish prerequisites now IN PLACE: registered author (`da-wei_lee`), `license: MIT`,
60	a designed 512×512 icon (`assets/extension-icon.png`, source `.svg`), `CHANGELOG.md`,
61	an extension `README.md`, and a graceful binary-not-found onboarding view. Remaining
62	before a public PR: **3–6 screenshots (2000×1250, GUI capture)** and a decision on the
63	binary-dependency review friction (a private org store sidesteps it entirely). The
64	full dev→publish process is documented in
65	[../docs/raycast-extension.md](../docs/raycast-extension.md) "Publishing & distribution".
66	
67	## References
68	
69	- Prepare for Store: https://developers.raycast.com/basics/prepare-an-extension-for-store
70	- Publish: https://developers.raycast.com/basics/publish-an-extension
71	- Teams / private extensions: https://developers.raycast.com/teams/publish-a-private-extension
72

```text
1	# Bilingual / "immersive" pipe mode + ANSI-strip-on-input
2	
3	**Status**: shipped (2026-07-20)
4	**Effort**: M
5	**Related**: `TODO.md` Done · `cmd/root.go` (`runBilingual`, `translateOnce`, `dimFunc`, pipe branch) · `internal/bitext/` · `.claude/plans/plan-c-strip-enchanted-hummingbird.md`
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	2026-07, surfaced from piping colored docs through the tool:
10	`tldr rg | translate --to zh-TW` produced a clean but **colorless** blob. Two
11	problems hid behind that:
12	
13	1. The piped ANSI escape codes reached the LLM verbatim (`io.ReadAll` →
14	   `TrimSpace` → `Request.Text`; `TrimSpace` only trims edges), wasting tokens and
15	   risking mis-segmentation.
16	2. There was no way to see the translation **alongside** the original — the ask,
17	   inspired by [Immersive Translate](https://immersivetranslate.com/en/), whose
18	   philosophy is "translate in place, keep the original, preserve the element's
19	   own style".
20	
21	## What shipped
22	
23	- **Strip fix (patch):** `bitext.Strip` (wraps `ansi.Strip`) is applied to piped
24	  stdin before it becomes `Request.Text`. Cleaner/cheaper prompt for every piped
25	  run; output unchanged.
26	- **`--bilingual` / `-2` (feat):** opt-in, stdin-only. Splits input into
27	  blank-line-delimited blocks, echoes each block verbatim (ANSI/color intact), and
28	  prints a translation beneath each **prose** block (prefixed `  ↳ `, dimmed grey
29	  on a TTY). Indented **command/code** blocks are echoed untranslated. Prose blocks
30	  translate concurrently (bounded to 5), forced concise so each block maps to
31	  exactly one translation. Echoed translations (proper nouns the model returns
32	  unchanged) are suppressed. `--json`/`--learn` take precedence; with positional
33	  args it falls through to the normal one-shot.
34	
35	## Key finding — what "the Immersive Translate philosophy" actually is
36	
37	Reverse-engineered docs (DeepWiki) + the injected DOM classes show Immersive
38	Translate preserves **block/element-level** style and renders the translation in a
39	**single uniform theme** (grey/underline/dimmed). It inserts the translation into
40	the *same* block element, so a heading stays heading-sized via **CSS inheritance** —
41	it does **not** re-bold or re-color the specific words that were styled in the
42	source. Source inline styling survives only in the retained original copy.
43	
44	Conclusion: "preserve per-word color in the translation" is **not** part of the
45	referenced philosophy. The faithful terminal analog is: keep the original block
46	(with its color) + one uniformly-dimmed translation beneath. That is exactly what
47	shipped.
48	
49	## Options considered
50	
51	| Option | What | Verdict |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| **A. Dominant-color per line** | detect each line's most-common SGR, recolor the translation in it | **Rejected.** tldr/`--help` color is *per-word* (command vs placeholder); "most frequent SGR" is a semantically meaningless color. |
54	| **B. Per-span color transfer** | parse ANSI → styled runs → placeholder tokens → LLM translates keeping markers → re-substitute | **Rejected — over-engineering.** Same problem class as XLIFF inline codes; unreliable across word reordering; defeats streaming. |
55	| **C. Block-interleaved, uniform dim** (shipped) | keep original block verbatim, translation beneath in one dim style; skip code blocks | **Chosen.** Matches the real Immersive Translate philosophy, robust, no alignment problem. |
56	
57	### Why B is a trap (prior art)
58	
59	Preserving inline markup across a translation that **reorders words** is a
60	well-studied hard problem, and the localization industry does **not** trust the
61	engine to reposition the tags:
62	
63	- **XLIFF 2.0** adds `canReorder`/`canCopy`/`canDelete` on inline codes precisely
64	  because reorder/duplication/deletion are the recognized hazards. The split
65	  `<bx/>`/`<ex/>` placeholder design is itself a source of unpairable output.
66	- **DeepL** `tag_handling` **duplicates** tags by design when word order changes;
67	  **Google** `format=HTML` returns tags "to the extent possible" (documented drops,
68	  e.g. vanishing `notranslate` spans).
69	- **MediaWiki Content Translation** *abandoned* delegating tag placement to MT:
70	  they strip markup, translate plain text, then reattach via subsentence alignment
71	  + n-gram fuzzy matching — and still hit inflection/reorder/split failures.
72	- CAT tools (OmegaT, memoQ) rely on **detection** (tag-count validation that blocks
73	  export), not prevention.
74	
75	A single ANSI-colored source word can become many target words or vanish via
76	inflection — there is no reliable "which target span wears the color". And the
77	reattachment step needs the **full** output buffered, defeating the token-by-token
78	streaming hot path (`internal/engine/prompt.go` asks for "ONLY the translated
79	text"; `engine.go` streams `ChunkToken`). Effort ≈ a mini-XLIFF engine for a
80	cosmetic terminal nicety.
81	
82	## Implementation notes
83	
84	- **`internal/bitext`** (pure, tested): `Strip`, `Split` (blank-line blocks +
85	  Prose/Code/Blank classification by ≥2-column indentation), `Render` (interleave;
86	  `dim` supplied as a closure so the package stays presentation-free and testable).
87	- **`github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi`** (was already an indirect dep, now direct)
88	  provides `ansi.Strip` and a CJK/wcwidth-aware tokenizer — no new third-party dep.
89	  Its API also offers `DecodeSequence`/`StringWidth`/`Truncate` if a future
90	  refinement needs per-span parsing.
91	- **`cmd/root.go`**: `--bilingual` is a standalone flag (Pattern B — read directly,
92	  no config/resolve wiring), dispatched only on the stdin pipe branch;
93	  `runBilingual` fans out `translateOnce` over prose blocks with a
94	  `chan struct{}`/`WaitGroup` semaphore; `dimFunc` styles only when
95	  `stdoutTTY && NO_COLOR unset`.
96	
97	## Known limitations (not fixed here)
98	
99	- **Tables/columns** (`ls -l`, `kubectl get`, `git status`): interleaving a
100	  translation beneath each row breaks alignment. Bilingual targets prose docs
101	  (tldr, man, `--help`), not tabular output.
102	- **Uniformly-indented output** (e.g. tldr indents its whole body 2 columns, with
103	  examples deeper) is handled: code detection is **relative to the document's base
104	  margin** (v0.3.2 fix), not an absolute column. A doc with *no* depth variation
105	  (every line at the same indent) is treated as all prose.
106	- **Hard-wrapped prose** split by blank lines loses cross-block context.
107	- Pair/learn routing and `--speak`/history are intentionally out of scope for this
108	  reading view.
109	
110	→ tracked as a `P3 [M]` follow-up in `TODO.md` (table/wrapped-prose-aware bilingual).
111	
112	## Update — context-aware doc mode (v0.4.0)
113	
114	Per-block isolation (each block translated in a separate call) produced three
115	failures on real `tldr rg`: `rg` mistranslated as an abbreviation (no context),
116	Simplified/Traditional drift across blocks, and reasoning leaking into output.
117	Added `--bilingual-mode doc` (now the default): the whole document is sent as
118	numbered segments (prose to translate + commands as context) in **one** call and the
119	model returns a JSON `{n: translation}` map — mirroring the `--learn` structured path
120	(`buildBilingualPrompt` + `finalizeBilingual` + `extractJSON`, which tolerates leaked
121	reasoning). Context-aware, single-variant, and **fewer** tokens than per-block. The
122	old strategy stays as `--bilingual-mode blocks` and is the automatic fallback when no
123	LLM is available or the JSON can't be parsed (e.g. `--engine google`). doc mode needs
124	an LLM provider and is non-streaming.
125	
126	## References
127	
128	- Immersive Translate (DeepWiki, reverse-engineered): content-script DOM insertion
129	  + theme styling system.
130	- XLIFF 1.2 / 2.0 inline codes (OASIS); DeepL `tag_handling` v2; Google Cloud
131	  Translation `format=HTML`; MediaWiki Content Translation markup handling.
132	- `charmbracelet/x/ansi` v0.11.7 (`ansi.Strip`, `DecodeSequence`, `StringWidth`).
133
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Look up Word — a Define Word-style Raycast picker
2	
3	**Status**: shipped (2026-07-26)
4	**Effort**: L
5	**Related**: `TODO.md` Done · `internal/engine/{dictsearch,ecdict,cedictdb}.go` · `cmd/{dictupdate,define,lang}.go` · `raycast/extension/src/look-up-word.tsx` · [`suggestion-ranking.md`](suggestion-ranking.md) · [../docs/raycast-extension.md](../docs/raycast-extension.md)
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	2026-07-26. Raycast's built-in **Define Word** has a shape our extension didn't:
10	empty search bar → recent lookups; type → a ranked list of candidate headwords each
11	with a definition preview as its subtitle; `⏎` → a full page for that word.
12	
13	Our `define` command couldn't do that. It debounced 500 ms, called
14	`translate define <word> --json` once, and rendered **one** result inline via
15	`isShowingDetail`. No candidate list, no history, no full-page view, no language
16	choice. The user's stated motivation for a full page: long content (an LLM
17	fallback definition, or a past sentence translation) is much more readable as
18	markdown on a page than in a narrow list detail pane.
19	
20	Two CLI gaps made the candidate list impossible:
21	
22	1. **No "search headwords by prefix" capability at all.** `define` is an exact point
23	   lookup that returns bare suggestion *strings* on a miss — no previews. The data
24	   was already on disk (ECDICT is a 770k-row SQLite table with a frequency column);
25	   it was simply never queried that way.
26	2. **`define` never wrote history**, so "⏎ records the lookup" had nothing behind it.
27	
28	## Options considered
29	
30	| Decision | Options | Verdict |
31	|---|---|---|
32	| Where the search lives | (a) new `dict search` subcommand · (b) a flag on `define` · (c) reimplement in TypeScript | **(a)**. (b) would overload `define --json`'s contract (one `TranslateResult`) with a second shape. (c) violates "reuse the binary, don't reimplement" and would duplicate ranking in two languages. |
33	| Chinese speed | (a) build a `cedict.db` SQLite index · (b) keep the lazy in-RAM parse · (c) an on-disk preview cache | **(a)**. The plain `.u8` is re-parsed by every process (~1.7 s per Chinese lookup) — unusable for type-ahead, and the index also takes `define 貓` from 1.7 s → 0.03 s for *every* front-end. (b) degrades gracefully and is kept as the fallback with a `notes` hint. |
34	| Auto-build the index | (a) inside `dict update` / an explicit `dict reindex` · (b) lazily inside `dict search` | **(a)**. A keystroke-driven process that Raycast aborts mid-build would never finish. `dict reindex` exists so installs predating the index don't re-download 9.8 MB. |
35	| New command vs rewriting `define` | (a) add `look-up-word`, keep `define` · (b) rewrite `define` in place · (c) add and remove | **(a)**, at the user's request — the two UXes stay side by side for comparison. |
36	| Empty-state list | (a) all history · (b) only word lookups · (c) toggle | **(a)**, at the user's request. Long past translations benefit most from the full-page view, so filtering them out would remove the payoff. |
37	| Language choice | (a) command argument + in-view dropdown · (b) in-view only · (c) config only | **(a)**. The argument is pickable in the Raycast root bar *before* the view opens; the in-view dropdown changes it later and is populated at runtime from the new `lang list --json` (35 languages) rather than the hand-synced 10-item manifest subset. |
38	| LLM fallback timing | (a) on `⏎` only · (b) automatically when the local list is empty | **(a)**. (b) is a ~6 s call per keystroke. An explicit *Ask the LLM* row appears when nothing local matched. |
39	| History write point | (a) `define` records by default, list stage uses `dict search` (no store at all) · (b) a new `history add` command · (c) record from TypeScript | **(a)**. `dict search` opening no store makes "typing cannot record" structural rather than a discipline. |

42	
43	## Non-obvious findings (measured, 2026-07-26)
44	
45	- **ECDICT `frq` is a rank, not a count**, and `LIKE 'x%'` does not use `idx_word_lc`
46	  (435 ms full scan vs 12 ms range scan). Both are written up in
47	  [`../pitfalls/ecdict-prefix-search-ranks-obscure-words-first.md`](../pitfalls/ecdict-prefix-search-ranks-obscure-words-first.md).
48	- Timings after the change: `dict search tes` 4 ms · `te` 20 ms · `a` (worst case)
49	  33 ms warm / 275 ms cold · Chinese 35 ms indexed (was 720 ms) · `define 貓` 32 ms
50	  (was 519 ms). `cedict.db` is 23 MB and builds in ~2 s from the existing download.
51	- `translate define --plain <miss> --json` exits **1** with a plain stderr line and
52	  **no JSON**. The extension tags that case (`isNoDictEntry`) and renders a friendly
53	  page instead of a red error. `dict search` deliberately does the opposite: an empty
54	  candidate list and exit 0, because it runs on every keystroke.
55	- The Raycast **Speak** action used to run a full root translation *and* write a
56	  history row every time. Look up Word uses `translate speak`, which neither
57	  translates nor records; `speak()` gained `--no-history`.
58	- 7 of 72 `engine:"dictionary"` rows in the live history file had `output:""` — a
59	  "did you mean" miss recorded as an answer. `appcore.Recordable` now filters those
60	  at every write site (CLI, Service, define).

2	
3	**Status**: ✅ Shipped 2026-07-22 (`translate serve` + `translate mcp`)
4	**Effort**: L

6	
7	## Outcome (what shipped)
8	
9	Built as thin transport adapters over a new shared core, `internal/appcore.Service`,
10	which lifts the engine builders + the warm engine + history glue out of package
11	`cmd` (so `cmd`, `server`, and `mcpserver` all drive one core, no import cycle):
12	
13	- **`translate serve`** — stdlib `net/http` (Go 1.22 method+path routing, no
14	  framework). `POST /v1/translate`, `POST /v1/define`, `GET /v1/history[?q=&limit=]`,
15	  SSE `GET /v1/translate/stream`, `GET /healthz`. Responses reuse
16	  `engine.TranslateResult` / `store.Record` verbatim. **Security**: loopback-only
17	  bind (fail-closed unless a token is set); optional bearer token guards
18	  `/v1/history` (`crypto/subtle` compare); config via a new `[server]` table
19	  (`port` 4155, `bind`, `token`/`token_env`). Graceful shutdown (SIGINT/SIGTERM →
20	  `http.Server.Shutdown`). History append hardened with `flock` for concurrent
21	  server+CLI writes.
22	- **OpenAPI/Swagger** — hand-written `internal/server/openapi.json` (OpenAPI 3.1) at
23	  `/openapi.json`; vendored `swagger-ui-dist` (`go:embed`) at `/docs`, fully offline.
24	  A reflection test guards schema↔struct drift.
25	- **`translate mcp`** — MCP over **stdio** (no port/token) via the official Go SDK
26	  `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` v1.6.1, exposing `translate` / `define` /
27	  `history` tools (typed structured output inferred from the Go structs). For Claude
28	  Desktop/Code, Cursor, etc.: `{ "command": "translate", "args": ["mcp"] }`.
29	
30	The streaming caveat below still holds: copilot-proxy buffers Claude `/v1/messages`,
31	so *visible* SSE/MCP token cadence stays coarse for Claude regardless of transport.
32	
33	Original investigation & options are preserved below for context.
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Original context (2026-07, pre-build)
38	
39	2026-07, surfaced while building the Raycast extension. Today every client (the
40	Raycast extension, script commands) **spawns the `translate` binary per call**. A
41	persistent local HTTP server (`translate serve`) with an OpenAPI/Swagger page was
42	proposed as "more usable." This doc records whether it is, and how.
43	
44	A related idea — folding `just raycast-dev` into the binary as `translate raycast
45	dev` — is **rejected** here (option C): it couples the Go CLI to the Node/`ray`
46	toolchain and the extension's on-disk location. Dev-tooling orchestration stays in
47	the `Justfile`. The useful subcommand is `translate serve`, not a `ray develop` wrapper.
48	
49	## Investigation
50	
51	- **Latency win is smaller than it looks.** Per-call spawn cost = config load +
52	  sqlite dict open + engine init. But LLM latency (~3–4 s) dominates, so a warm
53	  server mainly speeds up the **local dict/define** path, *not* LLM translation.
54	- **Streaming is the real win.** An HTTP server controls its own flushing → SSE
55	  (`text/event-stream`); clients consume via `fetch`/EventSource. Cleaner than the
56	  TTY / `--stream` / spawn path. (Caveat: upstream copilot-proxy still buffers claude
57	  `/v1/messages`, so visible streaming stays limited there regardless of transport.)
58	- **Multi-client + docs.** One loopback service → Raycast, Alfred, a browser
59	  extension, editor plugins, `curl`, a web UI. OpenAPI/Swagger documents it for all.
60	- **Sidesteps launchd-PATH** for request-time — the extension hits
61	  `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` instead of resolving/spawning the binary. But the *first*
62	  "start the daemon" still needs a spawn/LaunchAgent (PATH problem just moves).
63	- **Cheap to build.** Reuses `internal/engine` (pure Go, context-aware, TUI-free) as
64	  a thin HTTP adapter. stdlib `net/http` suffices (no framework dep). OpenAPI can be a
65	  hand-written `/openapi.json` + `go:embed`-ded Swagger UI, or generated
66	  (`swaggo/swag`, `danielgtaylor/huma`). Endpoints: `POST /v1/translate`,
67	  `POST /v1/define`, `GET /v1/history[?q=]`, SSE `GET /v1/translate/stream`.
68	
69	## Options considered
70	
71	| Option | What | Verdict |
72	|---|---|---|
73	| A. Keep spawn (current) | extension spawns `translate --json` / `--stream` per call | simplest, works, no daemon; per-call startup cost is small vs LLM latency |
74	| B. `translate serve` (HTTP + SSE + OpenAPI) | persistent loopback service; extension opt-in via a "server URL" pref, spawn fallback | best for streaming + multi-client + no-PATH; adds daemon lifecycle + security surface |
75	| C. `translate raycast dev` subcommand | binary shells out to npm/`ray` | rejected — couples Go CLI to Node toolchain + extension location; keep in Justfile |
76	
77	## Current blocker / open questions
78	
79	- **Daemon lifecycle**: how to keep it running — menu-bar app, a `LaunchAgent`, or the
80	  extension auto-starting it (which reintroduces the PATH problem for the first spawn)?
81	- **Security**: loopback-only bind is mandatory (history is personal data); consider a
82	  token for `/v1/history`.
83	- **Concurrent history writes**: server + CLI both appending `history.jsonl` — the
84	  store must be concurrency-safe (append + lock).
85	- **Port**: fixed default (collision risk) vs dynamic (needs discovery). Lean to a
86	  config'd default (e.g. `4155`) + preference.
87	- **Is it worth it vs spawn?** Only if we want a local translation *service* (streaming
88	  UX, multiple clients, web UI). The raw-latency argument is weak (LLM-dominated).
89	
90	## Decision (if any)
91	
92	`2026-07 deferred` — spawn mode works and ships. Revisit if we want a streaming-first
93	UX, multiple clients, or a web UI. If built: start minimal (stdlib `net/http`,
94	loopback, SSE, hand-written OpenAPI + embedded Swagger), extension **opt-in** with a
95	spawn fallback so non-server users are unaffected.
96	
97	## References
98	
99	- stdlib `net/http`; `go:embed` for the Swagger UI assets
100	- OpenAPI generators: https://github.com/swaggo/swag · https://github.com/danielgtaylor/huma
101	- Raycast integration + the streaming caveat: [../docs/raycast-extension.md](../docs/raycast-extension.md)
102
```

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
While the agents work on their tasks, I'm thinking through the design approach. I have the Raycast API version that supports platform-specific features like shortcuts and Windows app IDs, and since this is a local CLI wrapper with mostly shared code between platforms—though binary resolution varies—I need to account for the Go binary's cross-compilation to both Windows architectures.

The SQLite dependency is pure Go with no C bindings, so the history database will work on Windows. The main extension-side work involves updating `resolveBinary()` to find Windows paths, handling `translate.exe`, and using Node's path utilities for Windows-style paths. Text selection appears to already be cross-platform, and there's no menu-bar command tying things to macOS. The real effort isn't the extension itself but shipping a Windows binary and testing it—Homebrew handles macOS/Linux distribution, while Windows users would use `go install` or a released executable.

For the AI integration, I'm weighing two modes: direct translation wrapping the CLI tool, or an interactive learning mode with bilingual explanations. The key question is where the explanatory prompt should live and whether we can reuse existing presets. I'm sketching out the tool definitions: `look-up-word` wraps the dictionary lookup to pull real phonetic data from ECDICT instead of relying on the model to hallucinate it, and there might be a history search tool too. The key insight is that if the `phonetic` field is exposed through `translate define --json`, the model gets authoritative KK音標 directly, which is a strong argument for using tools rather than pure prompting.

The real tension is how to handle the teaching persona — it's currently baked into `ai.yaml` instructions which would apply globally, even when the user just wants a straightforward translation. I'm leaning toward option (c): split into two distinct tools with different descriptions, so the persona only activates when the user explicitly chooses the teaching-focused one, keeping the core translation tool neutral.

But there's another consideration — does the teaching mode even need a tool at all? If someone asks `@translate` with a question, Raycast AI could just answer directly from its own knowledge using the injected instructions, optionally calling our lookup tool for evidence. The key insight is that `@extension` mentions trigger instruction injection regardless of whether tools are invoked, so mode B could be purely instruction-driven with tools as optional support.

This also raises a question about scope: should we add an `explain` command to the Go CLI so the terminal interface gets the same learning experience? The user's phrasing suggests mode A should feel like using our app's LLM directly — meaning it routes through our binary — while mode B is about interactive, explanatory learning rather than literal translation.

I'm leaning toward putting the learn prompt in `ai.yaml` for Raycast's interactive mode, since that avoids double-wrapping through LLMs and keeps the data focused. Though there's merit in adding a `--preset explain` option to Go as well for consistency across the CLI, TUI, and potentially the bilingual immersion mode already in the backlog.

I should also double-check whether Quick AI supports the `@extension-name` syntax for reaching tools, since the docs mention it works in both Quick AI and AI Chat.

Now I'm thinking through whether adding `tools[]` has any Windows compatibility concerns — it's undocumented but has precedent with emoji-kitchen, so combining both questions should be fine.

func newNative(goos string, r runner, voices map[string]string, rate int) *nativeBackend {
	return &nativeBackend{goos: goos, runner: r, voices: voices, rate: rate}
}

func (n *nativeBackend) Name() string { return "native" }

// primaryBinary is the offline TTS binary for this OS, or "" if none is known.
// On Linux it returns the first of espeak-ng/espeak/spd-say found in PATH.
func (n *nativeBackend) primaryBinary() string {
	switch n.goos {
	case "darwin":
		return "say"
	case "linux":
		for _, b := range []string{"espeak-ng", "espeak", "spd-say"} {
			if _, err := n.runner.look(b); err == nil {
				return b
			}
		}
		return ""
	case "windows":
		return "powershell"
	}
	return ""
}

// Available reports whether this OS's native TTS binary is present.
func (n *nativeBackend) Available() bool {
	bin := n.primaryBinary()
	if bin == "" {
		return false
	}
	_, err := n.runner.look(bin)
	return err == nil
}

// Speak synthesizes text in langCode using the native binary, blocking until
// playback finishes (or ctx is cancelled).
func (n *nativeBackend) Speak(ctx context.Context, text, langCode string) error {
	text = strings.TrimSpace(text)
	if text == "" {
		return ErrEmptyText
	}
	switch n.goos {
	case "darwin":
		return n.speakSay(ctx, text, langCode)
	case "linux":
		return n.speakLinux(ctx, text, langCode)
	case "windows":
		return n.runner.run(ctx, "powershell", text,
			"-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-Command", winSpeakScript)
	}
	return ErrNoBackend
}

// New builds a Speaker that tries each configured backend in order.
func New(opt Options) Speaker {
	goos := opt.goos
	if goos == "" {
		goos = runtime.GOOS
	}
	var r runner = opt.runner
	if r == nil {
		r = execRunner{}
	}
	order := opt.Order
	if len(order) == 0 {
		order = []string{"native", "google"}
	}
	pl := player{goos: goos, runner: r, forced: opt.Player}
	build := map[string]Speaker{
		"native": newNative(goos, r, opt.Voices, opt.Rate),
		"google": newGoogle(opt.GoogleURL, opt.UserAgent, opt.CacheDir, opt.Timeout, pl),
	}
	var backends []Speaker
	for _, name := range order {
		if b, ok := build[name]; ok {
			backends = append(backends, b)
		}
	}
	return &fallback{backends: backends}
}

// fallback tries each backend in order, skipping unavailable ones and advancing
// to the next on error. It never panics on an empty backend list.
type fallback struct{ backends []Speaker }

func (f *fallback) Name() string { return "fallback" }

func (f *fallback) Available() bool {
	for _, b := range f.backends {
		if b.Available() {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

100	  text needs a `Form.TextArea` — that is what the `translate-text` command is.
101	  Behind it, argv caps at `ARG_MAX` (1 MiB), so `src/lib/translate.ts` pipes to
102	  stdin above 128 KB. See

104	- **Command arguments are static manifest data** and can't be populated at
105	  runtime, so a language argument is necessarily a hand-synced subset. In-view
106	  `List.Dropdown`s can call `translate lang list --json` for the full table.
107	
108	## Competitive landscape (2026)
109	
110	The Raycast translation category is crowded, but the field is almost entirely
111	remote-API/cloud-LLM wrappers configured via extension preferences.
112	
113	| Extension | Backend | Streaming | TTS | History | Offline dict |
114	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
115	| gebeto/translate (Google) | Google web (keyless) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
116	| tisfeng/Easydict | 10 remote providers + Apple `say`/Shortcuts | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ (remote) |
117	| douo/openai-translator | multi-LLM incl. Ollama / custom endpoint | ✓ | ✗ (roadmap) | ✓ | ✗ |
118	| deepcast / itranslate | DeepL / multi (BYO API key) | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |
119	| Raycast built-in Translate | unstated | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ (Pro-gated) |
120	
121	**What `translate` does that they don't:**
122	
123	- **Shells out to a dedicated local translator CLI** — no surveyed extension
124	  wraps a standalone translator binary (Easydict shells to `osascript`/Apple
125	  Shortcuts; none to a CLI like this).
126	- **Automatic multi-engine failover** — competitors that support multiple engines
127	  do *parallel aggregation*, not "try A, on failure fall back to B".
128	- **Offline CC-CEDICT / ECDICT dictionaries** via `translate define` — all
129	  competitors' dictionaries are remote.
130	- **Unified, searchable history** (`translate history [search]`).
131	- **Free local TTS** (`--speak`) — note openai-translator lists TTS as an
132	  unshipped roadmap item, so this is a real gap.
133	- **Fuzzy language resolution** (`translate lang resolve`, `chinees → zh`).
134	
135	Frame differentiation as **offline-resilient + auto-fallback + unified history**,
136	*not* "local LLM" (openai-translator already reaches Ollama) and *not* "study
137	modes" (Anki / Vocabulary Builder already exist in the store).
138	
139	## How ours is built
140	
141	- **Script Commands** — [`../raycast/script-commands/`](../raycast/script-commands/):
142	  `translate-text` (dropdown language + text, `fullOutput`), `translate-and-copy`
143	  (`silent`, copies; blank arg → clipboard), `define-word`. Install:
144	  `just raycast-scripts`, then add the directory in Raycast once.
145	- **TS extension** — [`../raycast/extension/`](../raycast/extension/): commands
146	  `translate` (view: type-to-translate, language dropdown, engine-override submenu,
147	  Copy/Paste/Speak, typo "did you mean?" suggestions, opt-in selection prefill),
148	  `translate-selection` (no-view:
149	  grabs the selection/clipboard and opens Translate prefilled via `launchCommand` —
150	  editable, not blind-paste), `define` (view: dictionary lookup +
151	  LLM fallback + "did you mean" suggestions), `look-up-word` (view: the Define
152	  Word-style picker, below), `translate-text` (view: a `Form.TextArea` for
153	  passages the search bar refuses, below), and `history` (view: browse/search
154	  past translations). All share `src/lib/translate.ts` (binary resolve + typed
155	  `execFile` wrappers mirroring `internal/engine/engine.go`'s `TranslateResult`).
156	  Run: `just raycast-dev` (`build`/`lint` variants exist). Live translate is
157	  debounced + abortable to avoid an LLM call per keystroke, with an opt-in `⌘↵`
158	  streaming view (`spawnTranslateStream` → `translate … --stream` → live `Detail`).
159	  Typo suggestions reuse the engine's fuzzy `suggestions[]` (a shared
160	  `did-you-mean.tsx` component) — no CLI change; single-word lookups route to the
161	  offline dict, full sentences to the LLM which corrects implicitly. Default target,
162	  live-debounce, and tier are inherited from the CLI config (`config show --json`)
163	  when the matching Raycast preference is empty, so `config.toml` is the single
164	  source of truth (a Raycast preference overrides it).
165	
166	### `look-up-word` — the Define Word-style picker
167	
168	Modeled on Raycast's built-in **Define Word**: an empty search bar lists recent
169	history; typing shows ranked headword candidates with definition previews;
170	`⏎` pushes a full-page `Detail`.
171	
172	Three rules shape it, and each is worth preserving:
173	
174	1. **Typing is local-only.** The list is backed by `translate dict search --json`,
175	   which reads the dictionary databases and nothing else (~30 ms). An LLM call per
176	   keystroke would take ~6 s and be unusable, so the LLM fallback is deferred to
177	   `⏎` — either on a fuzzy candidate or on the explicit *Ask the LLM* row that
178	   appears when no local headword matched.
179	2. **Only `⏎` writes history.** `dict search` opens no history store at all, so the
180	   typing path *cannot* record; `DefineDetail` calls `define` without
181	   `--no-history`, so opening a word remembers it. The old `define` command passes
182	   `--no-history` because it looks up on every keystroke.
183	3. **Language is pickable before and after opening.** A command *argument*
184	   dropdown appears in the Raycast root bar; an in-view `List.Dropdown` (populated
185	   from `translate lang list --json`) changes it later. Both only steer the LLM
186	   fallback — the offline tiers are script-fixed (ECDICT en→zh, CC-CEDICT zh→en) —
187	   and the Detail metadata says so rather than letting the choice look ignored.
188	
189	`define` is kept alongside it, unchanged, so the two UXes can be compared.
190	New components: `lib/define-detail.tsx` (full-page definition, the only history
191	writer), `lib/history-detail.tsx` (a stored record as a page — no re-run, instant),
192	`lib/language-dropdown.tsx`. `lib/did-you-mean.tsx` is deliberately *not* reused
193	here: its `⏎` re-runs the search, whereas in this list `⏎` must define.
194	
195	### `translate-text` — the long-passage escape hatch
196	
197	Every other command takes its input in the search bar, which Raycast caps: a long
198	paste is refused outright, and the extension never even sees it. This command is a
199	`Form.TextArea` plus target/engine dropdowns; submitting pushes the same full-page
200	`Detail` (`lib/translation-detail.tsx`), with `⌘↵` for the streaming view.
201	
202	Nothing is prefilled — *Load Selection* (`⌘⇧S`) and *Load Clipboard* (`⌘⇧V`) are
203	explicit actions, keeping the lesson from `e87db06` that auto-grabbing input on
204	open is surprising. `⌘⇧A` reveals **Engine** and **Model**; both stay hidden by
205	default so the common case is two fields.
206	
207	The Model list comes from `translate models --json` — the models the configured
208	providers *declare*, one per tier. Deliberately not a live `/v1/models` probe:
209	copilot-proxy advertises ids it then refuses to serve, so a probed list would
210	offer choices that fail at request time. Picking a model also selects its
211	provider, since `llama3.2:3b` belongs to ollama regardless of chain order.
212	
213	Past 128 KB of UTF-8, `src/lib/translate.ts` stops putting the text in argv and
214	pipes it to stdin (`execWithStdin`), because macOS caps a whole argument list at
215	`ARG_MAX` = 1 MiB. The CLI already reads stdin when given no text argument, so
216	this needed no CLI change. The provider is the real ceiling long before either
217	limit: Google puts the text in a GET query string and fails around 180 KB.
218	
219	Result metadata (engine · model · direction) is a dim footer line at the end of
220	the markdown rather than a `Detail.Metadata` sidebar: the sidebar is a permanent
221	third of the window, which is a lot of width to spend on five short labels when
222	the whole point of the view is reading room.
223	
224	### Target language: the **Auto** entry
225	
226	Both target dropdowns (`translate`, `translate-text`) lead with
227	`Auto — <home> ⇄ <away>`, the dropdown equivalent of the TUI's `^g`. It is not
228	cosmetic:
229	
230	With `[general] pair = true` the CLI reroutes home-language input to `pair_with`
231	regardless of `--to`, so before this the dropdown was quietly lying — picking
232	"Chinese (Traditional)" and pasting Chinese returned *English*. Making the mode
233	explicit lets a concrete choice mean what it says: the extension now sends
234	`--no-pair` whenever a specific language is picked, and no `--to` at all for Auto.
235	`--no-pair` had to be added to the CLI for this; there was previously no way to
236	turn pair off for one run.
237	
238	`lib/language-dropdown.tsx` reads the pair from `config show --json`, so the entry
239	is labelled with the real codes and is omitted when no `pair_with` is configured.
240	
241	## Publishing & distribution
242	
243	The journey from local development to the store, and why we default to
244	local/personal for now.
