> ⚠️ Using a GitHub Copilot subscription to back non-GitHub tools (copilot-proxy)
> may violate Copilot's Terms of Service. Reorder `chain.order` (drop `copilot`,
> lead with `ollama`/`google`) in the config if that matters to you.

Config lives at `~/.config/translate/config.toml`, history at
`~/.local/share/translate/history.jsonl`, last-pair state at
`~/.local/state/translate/state.json` (XDG-honored on macOS and Linux).

### Smart auto (`smartauto`)

The recommended default (choose it in `translate init`). It routes by input shape:
a **single word/term** is looked up in the dictionary (with the same LLM fallback as
`smart-dict` on a miss), while a **phrase or sentence** is translated by the LLM. Set
`engine = "smartauto"` in `[general]` (or `--engine smartauto`). It composes with
pair mode, so a single word and a full sentence both translate in the right direction.

### Pair mode (bidirectional)

With `pair = true` + `pair_with`, the tool detects which of the two languages your
input is in and translates it into the **other** — one box, both directions
(`你好 → hi`, `test → 測試`). For a CJK/non-CJK pair (e.g. `zh-TW`⇄`en`) direction is
decided by script, so even short input routes correctly; the LLM translate prompt is
also told to detect-and-route and to **never echo** the input. `pair_with` must differ
from the target (`translate init` enforces this; a degenerate config warns).

**Pair overrides `--to`.** With `pair = true`, home-language input is rerouted to
`pair_with` no matter what `--to` says — that is the point of the mode, but it
means `--to ja` does *not* guarantee Japanese output. Use `--no-pair` for a single
one-directional run:

```sh
translate "早安" --to ja                # → en   (pair rerouted it)
translate "早安" --to ja --no-pair      # → ja   (translate INTO ja, as asked)
```

Precedence is `--no-pair` > `--pair` > `TRANSLATE_PAIR` > `[general] pair`. Learn
mode is inherently bidirectional and still implies pair. The TUI toggles the same
thing with `^g`; the Raycast target dropdowns expose it as an **Auto** entry.

### Bilingual mode (`--bilingual` / `-2`)

Pipe colored docs and read both languages at once — inspired by Immersive
Translate. `cmd | translate --to <lang> --bilingual` keeps each original block
verbatim (its ANSI/color intact) and prints the translation beneath each **prose**
block, dimmed on a TTY:

```sh
tldr rg | translate --to zh-TW --bilingual     # or -2
```

Indented command/example blocks are echoed **untranslated** (so `rg pattern` stays
runnable), and blank-line spacing is preserved. It is opt-in and **stdin-only** —
never the pipe default, so plain `cmd | translate | less`/`grep` stays clean
single-output. Best for prose docs (tldr, man, `--help`); tabular output
(`ls -l`, `git status`) and hard-wrapped prose don't interleave cleanly.
`--json`/`--learn` take precedence. Design notes + why per-word recoloring was
rejected: [`backlog/bilingual-immersive-mode.md`](backlog/bilingual-immersive-mode.md).

Two strategies, via `--bilingual-mode`:

- **`doc`** (default) — one **context-aware** call: the whole document is sent as
  numbered segments (prose to translate, commands as context), so the model knows a
  bare `rg` is the command being documented (not an abbreviation), stays in one
  target variant, and doesn't leak reasoning. Fewer tokens than per-block, and needs
  an LLM provider.
- **`blocks`** — the older per-block strategy (each block translated in isolation,
  concurrent, works with any engine). `doc` automatically falls back to this when no
  LLM is available or the structured reply can't be parsed.

Separately, ANSI escapes are now **stripped from piped input** before translating,
so colored input (e.g. `grep --color=always`) no longer pollutes the prompt.

## 2. macOS-only assumptions in `src/`

**Binary resolution** — `src/lib/translate.ts:123-156`, the single hardest Windows blocker:

```ts
const PROBE_DIRS = [
  join(homedir(), ".local", "bin"),
  "/opt/homebrew/bin",
  "/usr/local/bin",
  join(homedir(), "go", "bin"),
];

let cachedBin: string | undefined;

/**
 * Resolve an ABSOLUTE path to the translate binary. Raycast runs under launchd
 * with a restricted PATH that does not inherit the shell rc, so a bare
 * `translate` throws ENOENT — we probe known install dirs (preference first).
 */
export function resolveBinary(): string {
  const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Prefs>();
  if (prefs.binaryPath && existsSync(prefs.binaryPath)) return prefs.binaryPath;
  if (cachedBin) return cachedBin;
  for (const dir of PROBE_DIRS) {
    const candidate = join(dir, "translate");
    if (existsSync(candidate)) {
      cachedBin = candidate;
      return candidate;
    }
  }
  throw new Error(
    "translate CLI not found. Set the binary path in extension preferences, or install it (just install / brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate).",
  );
}
```

## 3. `src/lib/translate.ts` shape

Exports 12 functions + 9 interfaces. Types mirror the Go structs: `TranslateResult` (mirrors `internal/engine/engine.go`), `HistoryEntry`, `Candidate`/`DictSearchResult` (mirror `internal/engine/dictsearch.go`), `LangInfo`, `ModelInfo`, `CliConfig`.

**The argv builder** (`runTranslate`, lines 286-334) — including the `directionArgs` helper it depends on:

```ts
function directionArgs(
  to: string | undefined,
  pair: boolean | undefined,
  prefTarget: string | undefined,
): { to?: string; pair?: boolean } {
  if (to === AUTO_TARGET) return { to: undefined, pair: true };
  return { to: to || prefTarget || undefined, pair };
}

export async function runTranslate(
  text: string,
  opts: TranslateOptions = {},
): Promise<TranslateResult> {
  const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Prefs>();
  const bin = resolveBinary();
  const dir = directionArgs(opts.to, opts.pair, prefs.defaultTarget);
  const viaStdin = needsStdin(text);
  // With no text argument the CLI reads stdin, which sidesteps ARG_MAX.
  const args = viaStdin ? [] : [text];
  // In auto/pair mode we deliberately send no --to: the CLI's own home target
  // plus [general] pair_with decide the direction.
  if (dir.to) args.push("--to", dir.to);
  args.push("--json");
  if (dir.pair === true) args.push("--pair");
  if (dir.pair === false) args.push("--no-pair");
  if (opts.from) args.push("--from", opts.from);
  const engine = opts.engine ?? prefs.engine;
  if (engine) args.push("--engine", engine);
  const tier = opts.tier ?? prefs.tier;
  if (tier) args.push("--tier", tier);
  if (opts.model) args.push("--model", opts.model);
  if (opts.noHistory) args.push("--no-history");

  const timeout = requestTimeout(text);
  if (viaStdin) {
    const stdout = await execWithStdin(bin, args, text, {
      timeout,
      signal: opts.signal,
    });
    return JSON.parse(stdout) as TranslateResult;
  }
  const { stdout } = await pexecFile(bin, args, {
    timeout, // LLM engines routinely exceed useExec's 10s default
    maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024,
    env: baseEnv(),
    signal: opts.signal, // cancel a superseded call when the user keeps typing
  });
  return JSON.parse(stdout) as TranslateResult;
}
```

Flags used across the module: `--json`, `--to`, `--from`, `--pair` / `--no-pair`, `--engine`, `--tier`, `--model`, `--no-history`, `--stream`, `--speak`, `--smart`, `--limit`, `--lang`. **No `--preset` and no `--instructions`** — those don't exist in this extension's surface.

Subcommands invoked: `define <word> --json [--smart] [--to] [--no-history]`; `dict search <q> --limit N --json`; `lang list --json`; `models --json`; `history --json --limit N` / `history search <q> --json`; `config show --json`; `speak <text> [--lang X]`.

**Streaming** (`spawnTranslateStream`, 580-612): `spawn(bin, [text?, --to, --stream, --no-history, ...])`, `stdout.setEncoding("utf8")`, appends raw chunks via `onData`, returns a cancel closure that `SIGTERM`s the child. Note it calls `directionArgs(opts.to, opts.pair, undefined)` — **the `defaultTarget` preference is deliberately not consulted here**, unlike `runTranslate`.

**stdin switchover:** `ARGV_SAFE_BYTES = 128 * 1024`; above that, `args` drops the text and `execWithStdin()` pipes it (documented as macOS `ARG_MAX` = 1 MiB, measured 900 KB OK / 1.1 MB E2BIG). `speak()`/`speakText()` do **not** have this guard — they always put text in argv.

**Timeouts:** `requestTimeout(text) = clamp(text.length * 10, 60_000, 600_000)`; fixed 10 s for `models`/`dict search`/`lang list`/`config show`, 30 s for `history`, 60 s for `define`.

**Error classification:** two tagged predicates. `isBinaryMissing(e)` = `e.message.startsWith("translate CLI not found")` (thrown by `resolveBinary`, rendered as the `BinaryNotFound` onboarding view). `isNoDictEntry(e)` = `e.message.startsWith("no dictionary entry")` — `runDefine` sniffs `e.stderr` for `"no dictionary entry"` and rethrows tagged, because a hard dict miss exits 1 with no JSON. `execWithStdin` deliberately mimics `pexecFile`'s rejection shape (`Error` + `.stderr`) so both paths are inspectable the same way. Everything else falls through as a raw `Error` rendered in an `EmptyView`/markdown code block.

**Module-level caches:** `cachedBin`, `cachedModels`, `cachedLangs`, `cachedConfig` — all per-command-run (a Raycast command process).

## 4. `src/lib/hooks.ts`

12 lines, exactly one hook: `useDebouncedValue<T>(value, delayMs)`. No caching, no `LocalStorage`, no `Cache`. All other state hooks live elsewhere: `useLanguages()` and `usePair()` in `src/lib/language-dropdown.tsx`, and `usePromise` (from `@raycast/utils`, with `abortable` refs) directly in the command files. Caching is the module-level `cached*` variables in `translate.ts`, not a hook.

## 5. Command files

- **`translate.tsx`** (266 lines) — `view`; type-to-translate `List` with debounced+abortable `runTranslate`, target `LanguageDropdown`, engine-override submenu (auto/google/dict/copilot/ollama), Copy/Paste/Speak, `⌘↵` push to `StreamView`. Accepts `launchContext {seed, to}` and optionally prefills from selection/clipboard per the `prefill` pref.
- **`translate-text.tsx`** (264 lines) — `view`; a `Form.TextArea` for long passages the search bar refuses, with Load Selection/Clipboard actions and a `⌘⇧A` advanced section (engine + model from `translate models --json`). Submits by pushing `TranslationDetail` or `StreamView`.
- **`translate-selection.tsx`** (40 lines) — `no-view`; grabs `getSelectedText()` (falling back to clipboard) and `launchCommand`s the `translate` command with `{seed, to}` so the text is editable rather than blind-pasted. **The only `no-view` command.**
- **`look-up-word.tsx`** (317 lines) — `view`; Define Word-style picker: empty bar shows recent history, typing (≥2 chars, 180/300 ms debounce) shows local `dict search` candidates in Dictionary / Did-you-mean sections, `↵` pushes `DefineDetail` (the only history writer).
- **`define.tsx`** (150 lines) — `view`; single-result dictionary lookup, 500 ms debounce, always `--no-history`, renders phonetic/meanings markdown + metadata, falls back to `DidYouMean` on suggestions.
- **`history.tsx`** (112 lines) — `view`; loads 200 rows via `runHistory`, client-side filtering through `keywords`, detail pane with direction/engine/model/timestamp, Copy/Paste/Reload actions.

Support files: `lib/stream-view.tsx`, `lib/translation-detail.tsx`, `lib/define-detail.tsx`, `lib/history-detail.tsx`, `lib/did-you-mean.tsx`, `lib/language-dropdown.tsx`, `lib/binary-not-found.tsx`.

## 6. Menu-bar mode

**None.** No `"mode": "menu-bar"` in the manifest, no `MenuBarExtra` import anywhere in `src/`. `docs/raycast-extension.md:38` explicitly says `menu-bar` is "not used yet".

## 7. `ai.yaml` / `src/tools/`

**Neither exists.** No `ai.yaml`/`ai.yml` anywhere in the repo (including outside the extension), no `src/tools/` directory, no `tools[]` in `package.json`, no `AI.ask` usage, no `@raycast/api` AI imports. `docs/raycast-extension.md:22-29` records this as a deliberate deferral: AI Extensions are judged "feasible (a tool file can `execFile` the binary and return its `--json`)" but "the AI API requires **Raycast Pro**, so it's an additive Pro-only layer — deferred."

## READMEs on install / PATH

**`/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-translate-cli-tui/raycast/README.md`** — covers two tracks (bash script-commands as a zero-Node fallback, TS extension as primary). Install is `just install` → `~/.local/bin/translate`, or `brew install daviddwlee84/tap/translate`. Dev loop is `just raycast-dev` (= `npm install` + `ray develop`); the extension persists in root search after dev stops, so no store publish is needed for personal use. The Gotchas section states the core constraint: **Raycast launches under launchd and does not inherit the shell PATH**, so a bare `translate` fails with `spawn translate ENOENT`; both tracks therefore resolve an absolute path (probing `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/go/bin`), and you must test *from Raycast*, not a terminal. Second: **API keys must live in `~/.config/translate/config.toml`, not shell env**, because a `~/.zshrc` export is absent under launchd — `HOME` is passed through so the CLI finds its config. Third: exit code is 0 even when an engine fails, so `warnings[]` from `--json` is the signal.

**`/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-translate-cli-tui/raycast/extension/README.md`** (store-facing) — leads with "shells out to the `translate` CLI — it does not translate on its own", gives brew/`go install` commands, notes `translate init` writes `~/.config/translate/config.toml`, lists the four auto-probe dirs, points at the "translate binary path" preference for non-standard locations, and mentions the graceful not-found screen. Explicitly says **"Translate Selection" and selection-prefill need macOS Accessibility permission** for Raycast. Also warns that a preference `default` only applies when no value is stored yet.

**`/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-translate-cli-tui/docs/raycast-extension.md`** (19 KB reference) — the integration-tier table, the launchd-PATH and installed-binary-vs-working-tree gotchas (`just check && just install && just raycast-dev`), the search-bar paste limit → `Form.TextArea` → 128 KB stdin switchover chain, why `execFile` beats `useExec` (10 s timeout that `timeout: 0` can't disable), the `--stream` non-TTY rationale, the Auto/`--no-pair` design, the competitive landscape, and a full publishing checklist. `backlog/raycast-extension.md:35-36` is the one place Windows is named: *"**Platform**: mark `platforms: ["macOS"]` (already set) — the binary shell-out doesn't work on Raycast's iOS/Windows clients."*

36	// A dictionary miss produces a result with no translation — only "did you mean"
37	// suggestions, or a "dictionary not installed" note. Those used to land in
38	// history as empty-output rows, which is noise in every history browser. A
39	// truncated stream is likewise not a usable record.
40	func Recordable(res *engine.TranslateResult) bool {
41		if res == nil || res.Truncated {
42			return false
43		}
44		if strings.TrimSpace(res.Translation) != "" {
45			return true
46		}
47		// A dictionary entry can carry its senses in Dictionary with an empty gloss.
48		return res.Dictionary != nil || res.Learn != nil

3	// It deliberately does NOT use github.com/adrg/xdg or os.UserConfigDir(): both

7	// ~/.local/state) on macOS AND Linux alike.

15	// app is the per-tool subdirectory used under each base dir.

17	
18	// base returns $env if set, else $HOME/def.
19	func base(env, def string) string {
20		if v := os.Getenv(env); v != "" {
21			return v
22		}

194	func ecdictResult(en *ecdictEntry) *TranslateResult {
195		d := &DictEntry{Word: en.Word, Phonetic: en.Phonetic}
196		if zh := splitEcdict(en.Translation); len(zh) > 0 {
197			mn := Meaning{PartOfSpeech: "中文"}
198			for _, line := range zh {
199				mn.Definitions = append(mn.Definitions, Definition{Text: line})
200			}
201			d.Meanings = append(d.Meanings, mn)
202		}
203		if de := splitEcdict(en.Definition); len(de) > 0 {
204			mn := Meaning{PartOfSpeech: "definition"}
205			for _, line := range de {
206				mn.Definitions = append(mn.Definitions, Definition{Text: line})
207			}
208			d.Meanings = append(d.Meanings, mn)
209		}
210		gloss := ""
211		if zh := splitEcdict(en.Translation); len(zh) > 0 {
212			gloss = zh[0]
213		}
214		return &TranslateResult{Translation: gloss, Target: ecdictGlossLang, Engine: "dictionary", Dictionary: d}

12	That requires a Go toolchain on every host. The dotfiles fleet is multi-host /

18	## Investigation

20	- Binary is **pure Go, no cgo** (`modernc.org/sqlite` is pure Go), so

27	  `~/.local/bin`.

30	
31	| Option | Pros | Cons |
32	|---|---|---|
33	| A. `go install @version` (current) | zero release infra; always builds for the host | needs Go toolchain per host; version pin is a git tag |

package engine

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"sync"
	"time"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/translate/internal/debug"
)

// Chain is the AUTO fallback router. It tries engines in configured order and
// fails over to the next one when the current engine is known-down or fails
// before producing any token. Once tokens have streamed, a mid-stream error is
// surfaced rather than restarting on another engine (which would garble output);
// the common "provider not running" case fails at connect time, pre-token, and
// switches cleanly.
type Chain struct {
	engines []Engine
	ttl     time.Duration

	mu    sync.Mutex
	avail map[string]probeCache
}

type probeCache struct {
	ok bool
	at time.Time
}

// NewChain builds a chain from engines in priority order. ttl is how long a
// health verdict is cached (default 5s).
func NewChain(engines []Engine, ttl time.Duration) *Chain {
	if ttl <= 0 {
		ttl = 5 * time.Second
	}
	return &Chain{engines: engines, ttl: ttl, avail: map[string]probeCache{}}
}

// Name reports the chain as the "auto" engine.
func (c *Chain) Name() string { return "auto" }

// Engines returns the chain members in fallback order.
func (c *Chain) Engines() []Engine { return c.engines }

// Supports reports true if any member supports the mode.
func (c *Chain) Supports(m Mode) bool {
	for _, e := range c.engines {
		if e.Supports(m) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// skip it without paying a probe on the hot path. Engines are otherwise tried
// optimistically (no pre-probe latency on the happy path).

```text
mcp runs a Model Context Protocol server over stdin/stdout, exposing the
translate, define, and history tools to any MCP host that spawns this binary.
There is no port or token — the transport is a private stdio pipe.

Register it in an MCP host with:
  { "command": "translate", "args": ["mcp"] }

stdout carries JSON-RPC; do not pipe it anywhere but the host.

Usage:
  translate mcp [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help         help for mcp
      --no-history   do not read or write history

Global Flags:
  -2, --bilingual               bilingual pipe mode: keep original (with color) + translation beneath (stdin only)
      --bilingual-mode string   bilingual strategy: doc (context-aware, one LLM call) | blocks (per-block) (default "doc")
      --debug                   log intermediate decisions (routing, engine choice, dict hit/miss)
      --engine string           engine: auto|<provider>|google|dict
  -f, --from string             source language ("auto" to detect)
      --instructions string     extra system-prompt guidance (domain focus, etc.)
      --json                    emit the full result as JSON
      --learn                   learning mode: teach (native→foreign) or grammar-correct (foreign→native)
      --model string            LLM model id override
      --no-pair                 force one-directional: always translate into --to, ignoring [general] pair
      --pair                    bidirectional mode: home-language input → --pair-with, else → --to
      --pair-with string        the other language for --pair (e.g. en)
      --preset string           LLM prompt style: concise|contextual|dictionary
=== serve ===
serve starts a persistent loopback HTTP service exposing the translate
engine over JSON (and SSE streaming). It binds 127.0.0.1 by default; a
non-loopback bind is refused unless a token is set. History is guarded by
the token when one is configured.

  translate serve                 # http://127.0.0.1:4155
  translate serve --port 8080
  translate serve --token "$TOK" --bind 0.0.0.0

Usage:
  translate serve [flags]

Flags:
      --bind string    bind address (default 127.0.0.1; loopback enforced without a token)
  -h, --help           help for serve
      --no-history     do not read or write history
      --port int       listen port (default from [server].port, else 4155)
      --token string   bearer token guarding /v1/history (overrides config)

Global Flags:
  -2, --bilingual               bilingual pipe mode: keep original (with color) + translation beneath (stdin only)
      --bilingual-mode string   bilingual strategy: doc (context-aware, one LLM call) | blocks (per-block) (default "doc")
      --debug                   log intermediate decisions (routing, engine choice, dict hit/miss)
      --engine string           engine: auto|<provider>|google|dict
  -f, --from string             source language ("auto" to detect)
      --instructions string     extra system-prompt guidance (domain focus, etc.)
      --json                    emit the full result as JSON
      --learn                   learning mode: teach (native→foreign) or grammar-correct (foreign→native)
      --model string            LLM model id override
      --no-pair                 force one-directional: always translate into --to, ignoring [general] pair

# Prompt & architecture map — `translate` Go CLI

## 1. Where prompts live — `internal/engine/prompt.go` (the ONLY prompt file)

Every LLM prompt in the project is a package-level `const` in `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-translate-cli-tui/internal/engine/prompt.go` (255 lines). I grepped the whole engine package: no other file constructs prompts. `google.go`, `dict.go`, `localdict.go`, `chain.go`, `smartauto.go` never touch them.

**Preset identifiers** — `internal/engine/prompt.go:12-16` (these are exported; the strings themselves are not):

```go
const (
	PresetConcise    = "concise"    // terse direct translation (default)
	PresetContextual = "contextual" // short list of common-sense translations
	PresetDictionary = "dictionary" // translation + 1-2 example sentences
)
```

### `concise` — `internal/engine/prompt.go:21-33`

```
You are a precise, professional translation engine.
Translate the user's text into the target language faithfully and idiomatically.

Rules:
- Preserve the meaning, tone, and register (formal/informal, technical/casual) of the source.
- The user's text may contain typos, slang, or ungrammatical phrasing. Interpret their
  INTENDED meaning and translate that; do not translate a typo literally, and never refuse.
- Output ONLY the translated text. No quotes, no explanations, no language labels,
  no commentary before or after.
- ALWAYS translate into the target language. A single word, name, technical term, or
  loanword written in a DIFFERENT language must still be translated — never echo it back.
  Only when the text is ALREADY in the target language should you return it (lightly
  corrected if it was misspelled).
```

### `contextual` — `internal/engine/prompt.go:36-47`

```
You are a precise, professional translation engine.
Translate the user's text into the target language, showing how the translation changes
across the most common senses or contexts of the source.

Rules:
- Preserve meaning, tone, and register. The text may contain typos, slang, or ungrammatical
  phrasing — interpret the INTENDED meaning; never refuse and never translate a typo literally.
- Output a SHORT list of 2-4 lines, one line per distinct common sense/context.
- Format each line EXACTLY as: "N. <translation> — <short context label in the TARGET language>".
- Order lines from the most likely/common sense to the least.
- If the text has only one natural sense, output a single line — do not invent senses.
- Output ONLY the list. No preamble, no headings, no commentary before or after.
```

### `dictionary` — `internal/engine/prompt.go:50-63`

```
You are a precise, professional translation engine
that also gives brief usage examples.
Translate the user's text into the target language, then illustrate it with example sentences.

Rules:
- Preserve meaning, tone, and register. Interpret the INTENDED meaning of typos/slang; never refuse.
- The FIRST line is ONLY the translation of the user's text — no label, no quotes.
- Then a blank line, then 1-2 example sentences that use the translation naturally.
- Format each example on two lines:
    line 1: the example sentence in the TARGET language,
    line 2: its translation in the source language (the language of the user's input),
            prefixed with "  ↳ ".
- Keep examples short and idiomatic. Output ONLY the translation and the examples —
  no headings, no numbering of the first line, no commentary.
```

Selection is a plain switch with concise as the default — `internal/engine/prompt.go:66-75`.

### The user turn — `internal/engine/prompt.go:84-88`

```go
const translateUserPrompt = `Source language: %s
Target language: %s

Text:
%s`
```

Language codes are expanded to readable names (`lang.Name(req.Target)` → `"chinese (traditional) (zh-TW)"`) at `prompt.go:93-101`.

### Two more prompt families in the same file

**Bilingual doc mode** — `internal/engine/prompt.go:120-134`:

```
You translate terminal / CLI documentation into %[1]s.

You are given the whole document as a numbered list of SEGMENTS. Some are prose to
translate; others are command/code lines marked "[code — context only]" and are
shown ONLY so you understand the document — never translate or echo them.

Rules:
- Use the WHOLE document as context. A bare token like "rg" or "ls" on its own is
  the COMMAND being documented, not an abbreviation — do not expand or gloss it.
- Keep command names, subcommands, flags, file paths, URLs, and code verbatim.
- Preserve meaning, tone, and register. Interpret the intended meaning of typos; never refuse.
- Translate EVERY prose segment into %[1]s only — one consistent variant, never mixed.
- Respond with ONE JSON object and NOTHING else: keys are the prose segment numbers
  (as strings), values are the translations. No markdown fence, no reasoning, no
  commentary before or after the JSON.
```

**Learn mode** — the two prompts most relevant to your (b) "learn English while you ask" idea. `internal/engine/prompt.go:186-208`:

```
You are a warm, encouraging language tutor helping a native %[1]s speaker learn %[2]s.
The user writes in %[1]s. Translate their text into natural, idiomatic %[2]s, then teach it.

Respond with ONE JSON object and NOTHING else — no markdown code fence, no prose before or after it.
Schema (fill every relevant field; omit a field only when it genuinely has no content):
{
  "direction": "teach",
  "original": "<the user's %[1]s input, verbatim>",
  "translation": "<the idiomatic %[2]s translation>",
  "vocab": [
    {"term": "<key %[2]s word or phrase>", "pos": "<part of speech>", "phonetic": "<KK/IPA for English, pinyin for Chinese>", "meaning": "<concise meaning in %[1]s>"}
  ],
  "examples": [
    {"foreign": "<a short natural %[2]s sentence using the translation>", "native": "<its %[1]s translation>"}
  ],
  "notes": "<one short usage or register tip in %[1]s, optional>"
}

Rules:
- Write every meaning, note, and explanation in %[1]s (the learner's language).
- vocab: only the key content words/phrases worth learning (at most 8); skip trivial function words.
- examples: 1-2, short and idiomatic.
- Interpret the intended meaning of typos/slang; never refuse. Output ONLY the JSON object.
```

`internal/engine/prompt.go:212-232`:

```
You are a warm, encouraging language tutor helping a %[2]s speaker who is learning %[1]s.
The user writes a sentence in %[1]s that may contain mistakes. Correct it and explain, kindly.

Respond with ONE JSON object and NOTHING else — no markdown code fence, no prose before or after it.
Schema (fill every relevant field; omit a field only when it genuinely has no content):
{
  "direction": "correct",
  "original": "<the user's %[1]s input, verbatim>",
  "corrected": "<the grammatically correct, idiomatic %[1]s sentence>",
  "translation": "<a %[2]s translation of the intended meaning>",
  "issues": [
    {"span": "<the problematic fragment of the input>", "fix": "<the corrected fragment>", "explanation": "<why, in %[2]s>"}
  ],
  "notes": "<one short encouraging tip in %[2]s, optional>"
}

Rules:
- Write every explanation and note in %[2]s (the learner's native language).
- If the sentence is already correct, echo it in "corrected" and return "issues": [].
- List each distinct mistake as one issue; keep explanations concise and beginner-friendly.
- Interpret the intended meaning of typos/slang; never refuse. Output ONLY the JSON object.
```

Learn user turn is bare (`internal/engine/prompt.go:236-237`): `Text:\n%s` — the system prompt already names both languages.

### Reusability verdict

The prompt *strings* are **unexported consts** in package `engine`, so a Raycast extension cannot import them; but they are reachable **behaviorally** through the exported `engine.Request` struct, and — crucially — through the **CLI's `--json` output** and the **HTTP API**. Direction selection is decided offline, not by the model (`learnDirection`, `internal/engine/prompt.go:177-182`), using the same script router as pair mode.

---

## 2. `--instructions` — how custom text reaches the prompt

One mechanism, appended to the *system* prompt for all three prompt families:

- Flag declared `cmd/root.go:83`: `f.StringVar(&flagInstructions, "instructions", "", "extra system-prompt guidance (domain focus, etc.)")`
- → `config.Overrides.Instructions` (`cmd/root.go:119`) → resolve precedence flag > env `TRANSLATE_INSTRUCTIONS` > `[cli]`/`[tui]` overlay > `[general] instructions` (`internal/config/resolve.go:148`, `internal/config/config.go:86`)
- → `engine.Request.Extra` (`internal/engine/engine.go:35`)
- → appended verbatim at **`internal/engine/prompt.go:108-110`**:

```go
if extra := strings.TrimSpace(req.Extra); extra != "" {
	system += "\n\nUser preferences (apply where relevant, e.g. domain terminology):\n" + extra
}
```

The identical three lines are repeated in `buildBilingualPrompt` (`prompt.go:155-157`) and `buildLearnPrompt` (`prompt.go:250-252`). So `--instructions` is a **general-purpose system-prompt injection point** — it is your cheapest lever for an "explanatory answer" mode without touching Go code.

Also exposed over HTTP as `instructions` (`internal/server/handlers.go:27`, SSE query param `internal/server/sse.go:44`). **Not** exposed by the MCP server.

## 3. Engine architecture

**Interface** — `internal/engine/engine.go:201-207`:

```go
type Engine interface {
	Name() string
	Translate(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Chunk, error)
	Detect(ctx context.Context, text string) (string, error)
	Available(ctx context.Context) bool
	Supports(m Mode) bool
}
```

Contract (documented `engine.go:192-200`): `Translate` returns a receive-only channel and MUST close it after exactly one terminal `Chunk` (`ChunkDone` or `ChunkError`); streaming engines emit zero or more `ChunkToken` first. `Chunk` is at `engine.go:185-190`.

**Implementations**

| Engine | File | Prompts? | Streams? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LLMEngine` (any OpenAI-compatible: copilot-proxy, ollama, openrouter, litellm, generic) | `internal/engine/llm.go` | yes — the only one | yes |
| `GoogleEngine` (free keyless `translate_a/single`) | `internal/engine/google.go` | no | no |
| `DictEngine` (dictionaryapi.dev) | `internal/engine/dict.go` | no | no |
| `LocalDictEngine` (CC-CEDICT + ECDICT SQLite) | `internal/engine/localdict.go` | no | no |
| `SmartDictEngine` (dict → LLM fallback) | `internal/engine/smartdict.go` | delegates, forces `PresetDictionary` (`smartdict.go:111-114`) | passes through |
| `SmartAutoEngine` (word→dict, phrase→LLM) | `internal/engine/smartauto.go` | delegates | passes through |
| `Chain` (`auto`, ordered failover) | `internal/engine/chain.go` | delegates | passes through |

**Builders** — `internal/appcore/build.go:23-51` (`BuildEngine` switch on `res.Engine`: `auto` → `BuildAutoChain`, `smartauto` → `SmartAutoFromConfig`, `google`, `llm`, or a named provider). Default `chain.order` is `["copilot", "ollama", "google", "dict"]` (`internal/config/config.go:251`); default providers are `copilot` at `http://localhost:4141/v1`, `ollama` at `http://localhost:11434/v1`, `openrouter` (`config.go:254-271`).

**Streaming** — two wire protocols in `llm.go`:
- OpenAI `/chat/completions` SSE — `translateOpenAI` `llm.go:471-553`, parser `readSSE` `llm.go:657-695`
- Anthropic `/v1/messages` SSE — `translateAnthropic` `llm.go:556-642`, parser `readAnthropicSSE` `llm.go:702-749`; routed whenever the model id starts with `claude` (`isAnthropicModel`, `llm.go:228-230`)

Two gotchas worth carrying into a Raycast design:
- **Structured modes never stream** — `llm.go:481` and `llm.go:566`: `stream := req.Stream && !req.Learn && !req.Bilingual`.
- **Truncation is detected, not silently accepted** — `markTruncated` (`llm.go:464-468`) sets a `Warnings` entry `"output was cut off before completion (stream truncated) — press Enter to retry"`; `max_tokens` scales with input via `outputTokenBudget` (`llm.go:174-183`). Also `docs`/`pitfalls/llm-stream-truncation-silently-rendered-as-complete.md`.
- copilot-proxy **buffers** Claude `/v1/messages`, so visible token cadence is coarse for Claude regardless of transport (`internal/server/sse.go:23-25`).

---

## 4. `translate define <word>` — local dictionary first, LLM only as fallback

`cmd/define.go:22-89`. Engine choice via `appcore.DefineEngine` (`internal/appcore/build.go:186-195`): plain offline dict, or `smart-dict` when a provider exists and `[smartdict] define_default` is set; `--plain` / `--smart` force either.

Data is **local**: CC-CEDICT (zh→en) and **ECDICT** (en→zh, 770k-row SQLite) — `internal/engine/localdict.go`, `ecdict.go`, `cedictdb.go`. The gloss language is stamped honestly, not echoed from `--to` (`internal/engine/localdict.go:170-173`):

```go
const (
	cedictGlossLang = "en"    // CC-CEDICT defines Chinese in English
	ecdictGlossLang = "zh-CN" // ECDICT defines English in Simplified Chinese
)
```

On a hard miss the smart-dict engine falls back to the LLM with `PresetDictionary` and stamps a warning `"no dictionary entry for %q — defined via %s (LLM)"` (`internal/engine/smartdict.go:106-129`). A too-far fuzzy match also falls back (`smartdict.go:89-102`).

**Output structs** — `internal/engine/engine.go:116-135`:

```go
type DictEntry struct {
	Word      string    `json:"word"`
	Phonetic  string    `json:"phonetic,omitempty"`
	Meanings  []Meaning `json:"meanings,omitempty"`
	SourceURL string    `json:"source_url,omitempty"`
}

type Meaning struct {
	PartOfSpeech string       `json:"part_of_speech"`
	Definitions  []Definition `json:"definitions"`
	Synonyms     []string     `json:"synonyms,omitempty"`
	Antonyms     []string     `json:"antonyms,omitempty"`
}

type Definition struct {
	Text    string `json:"definition"`
	Example string `json:"example,omitempty"`
}
```

Plain-text rendering is `renderDict` (`cmd/define.go:92-119`), which caps at 4 definitions per part of speech. Note: `translate define --plain <miss>` **exits 1 with no JSON** (documented in `backlog/look-up-word.md:51-54`), while `translate dict search` exits 0 with `[]`.

## 5. `--json` — one struct for both commands

Both `translate <text> --json` (`cmd/root.go:487-492`) and `translate define <word> --json` (`cmd/define.go:75-79`) marshal the **same** `*engine.TranslateResult` with `SetIndent("", "  ")`. Full definition, `internal/engine/engine.go:72-113`:

```go
type TranslateResult struct {
	Translation    string   `json:"translation"`
	DetectedSource string   `json:"detected_source,omitempty"`
	Target         string   `json:"target"`
	Alternatives   []string `json:"alternatives,omitempty"`
	Notes          string   `json:"notes,omitempty"`
	Confidence     float64  `json:"confidence,omitempty"`

	Warnings []string `json:"warnings,omitempty"`

	Truncated bool `json:"-"`

	// Provenance — stamped by the producing engine / chain.
	Engine string `json:"engine,omitempty"`
	Model  string `json:"model,omitempty"`

	Dictionary *DictEntry `json:"dictionary,omitempty"`
	Learn *LearnResult `json:"learn,omitempty"`
	Bilingual map[int]string `json:"-"`
	Suggestions []string `json:"suggestions,omitempty"`

	SuggestDistance int `json:"-"`
}
```

So: `define --json` fills `dictionary` (or `suggestions` on a fuzzy miss); `translate --json` fills `translation` + provenance; **`translate --learn --json` fills `learn`** (see §9). `Truncated` and `Bilingual` are `json:"-"` — SSE re-surfaces truncation as an explicit `warning` event (`internal/server/sse.go:68-73`).

The learn payload — `internal/engine/engine.go:140-170`:

```go
type LearnResult struct {
	Direction   string         `json:"direction"`           // "teach" (native→foreign) | "correct" (foreign→native)
	Original    string         `json:"original"`            // the user's input as received
	Corrected   string         `json:"corrected,omitempty"` // correct-direction: the fixed foreign sentence
	Translation string         `json:"translation"`         // teach: foreign translation; correct: native translation of intent
	Notes       string         `json:"notes,omitempty"`     // short tip/encouragement, in the NATIVE language
	Issues      []LearnIssue   `json:"issues,omitempty"`    // correct-direction grammar/usage fixes
	Vocab       []LearnGloss   `json:"vocab,omitempty"`     // teach-direction glosses
	Examples    []LearnExample `json:"examples,omitempty"`  // teach-direction usage examples
}

type LearnIssue struct {
	Span        string `json:"span"`        // the problematic fragment of the input
	Fix         string `json:"fix"`         // the corrected fragment
	Explanation string `json:"explanation"` // why — in the NATIVE language
}

type LearnGloss struct {
	Term     string `json:"term"`               // foreign word/term
	Pos      string `json:"pos,omitempty"`      // part of speech
	Phonetic string `json:"phonetic,omitempty"` // KK/IPA for English, pinyin for Chinese
	Meaning  string `json:"meaning"`            // meaning in the NATIVE language
}

type LearnExample struct {
	Foreign string `json:"foreign"` // example sentence in the foreign language
	Native  string `json:"native"`  // its native-language translation
}
```

And the headword-search shape (`translate dict search --json`, `GET /v1/dict/search`) — `internal/engine/dictsearch.go:29-49` (`SearchResult{query, script, source, candidates[], notes}` with `Candidate{word, phonetic, preview, pos, rank, match, distance}`).

## 6. `--pair` and `--bilingual` / `-2`

**`--pair`** changes the *prompt* (adds a directive) and the *routing* (target selection), not the output shape.

- Directive appended to whichever preset is active — `internal/engine/prompt.go:81`:
  ```
  Bidirectional mode: the text is written in ONE of %s or %s. Detect which of the two it is, and translate it into the OTHER one. ALWAYS translate — never return the text unchanged, even for a single word, a proper name, a technical term, or a loanword.
  ```
  Applied at `prompt.go:105-107` — deliberately *appended* so the concise/contextual/dictionary output format survives.
- Offline routing: `appcore.EffectiveTarget` (`internal/appcore/record.go:15-22`) → `lang.PairTarget(home, away, text)`, script-based for CJK/non-CJK.
- Pair **overrides `--to`** (README:118-130); `--no-pair` exists specifically so the Raycast dropdown can mean what it says (`docs/raycast-extension.md:224-239`).

**`--bilingual` / `-2`** is a *pipe-only reading view*, not a prompt style. Declared `cmd/root.go:88-89`; dispatched only on the stdin branch and only when `!flagJSON && !res.Learn` (`cmd/root.go:245`). Two strategies via `--bilingual-mode`:
- `doc` (default) — one context-aware call, whole document as numbered segments, model returns `{"1":"…","2":"…"}` (`buildBilingualPrompt` + `finalizeBilingual` at `llm.go:407-442`); requires an LLM provider, non-streaming.
- `blocks` — per-block concurrent (bounded 5) translation, forced concise, any engine; also the automatic fallback (`cmd/root.go:511-591`).

Output: original block verbatim with ANSI intact, translation beneath prefixed `  ↳ `, dimmed on a TTY (`internal/bitext/bitext.go:131-153`, `cmd/root.go:665-671`).

---

## 7. `internal/bitext` — ANSI-safe block splitting for the bilingual view

Package doc, `internal/bitext/bitext.go:1-6`: splits piped terminal input into blank-line-delimited blocks and renders the bilingual view. Three exported functions:

- `Strip(s)` — wraps `charmbracelet/x/ansi.Strip`; applied to **all** piped stdin before it becomes `Request.Text` (`cmd/root.go:239`), so colored input never wastes prompt tokens.
- `Split(raw) []Block` — `Block{Raw, Plain, Kind}` where `Kind` ∈ `Blank|Prose|Code` (`bitext.go:14-32`). Code detection is **relative to the document's base margin** (`codeIndent = 2` deeper), because tldr/man indent their whole body (`bitext.go:41`, `47-108`).
- `Render(blocks, translations, dim)` — interleaves; `dim` is injected as a closure so the package stays presentation-free.

Pure, no engine/TUI imports, unit-tested (`bitext_test.go`). Reusable as-is for any "keep original + translation beneath" surface.

---

## 8. MCP server (`cmd/mcp.go`) and HTTP server (`cmd/serve.go`) — both exist and both shipped

### MCP — stdio, official Go SDK `modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`

`cmd/mcp.go:11-38` registers the command; `internal/mcpserver/mcp.go:32-47` registers exactly three tools:

```go
mcp.AddTool(srv, &mcp.Tool{
	Name:        "translate",
	Description: "Translate text into a target language (faithful, register-aware).",
}, translateHandler(svc))
mcp.AddTool(srv, &mcp.Tool{
	Name:        "define",
	Description: "Look up the dictionary definition of a word or short term.",
}, defineHandler(svc))
mcp.AddTool(srv, &mcp.Tool{
	Name:        "history",
	Description: "List or fuzzy-search recent translation history.",
}, historyHandler(svc))
```

Input schemas are **inferred from Go structs via `jsonschema` tags** — `internal/mcpserver/tools.go:17-32`:

```go
type translateInput struct {
	Text   string `json:"text" jsonschema:"the text to translate"`
	Target string `json:"target,omitempty" jsonschema:"target language code, e.g. en or zh-TW (optional; server default otherwise)"`
	Source string `json:"source,omitempty" jsonschema:"source language code, or auto to detect (optional)"`
}

type defineInput struct {
	Word string `json:"word" jsonschema:"the word or short term to look up"`
}

type historyInput struct {
	Query string `json:"query,omitempty" jsonschema:"fuzzy search query; omit for the most recent entries"`
	Limit int    `json:"limit,omitempty" jsonschema:"maximum number of records to return (default 20)"`
}
```

Structured output is the full `engine.TranslateResult`; text content is a human rendering (`renderTranslation`/`renderDefine`/`renderHistory`, `tools.go:101-153`). **Notable gap: the MCP `translate` tool exposes no `preset`, no `instructions`, no `learn`, no `pair`** — it is the thinnest surface of the three.

### HTTP — `translate serve`, loopback, JSON + SSE + OpenAPI

`cmd/serve.go:14-58` (default port 4155, loopback enforced unless a bearer token is set). Routes — `internal/server/server.go:61-73`:

```go
mux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/translate", h.translate)
mux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/translate/stream", h.translateStream)
mux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/define", h.define)
mux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/dict/search", h.dictSearch)
mux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/history", h.requireToken(h.history))
mux.HandleFunc("GET /healthz", h.healthz)
registerDocs(mux)   // /openapi.json + embedded Swagger UI at /docs
```

Request body — `internal/server/handlers.go:22-31` — carries `text, source, target, preset, instructions, model, max_alts, pair` but **no `learn`**. SSE event grammar is documented at `internal/server/sse.go:13-25` (`token` / `warning` / `done` / `error`, all JSON payloads).

Both adapters sit on `internal/appcore.Service` (`internal/appcore/service.go:21-34`), a warm, transport-agnostic core holding pre-built engines + the history store. `appcore.Params` (`service.go:43-52`) has `Text, Source, Target, Preset, Instructions, Model, MaxAlts, Pair *bool` — again, **no Learn**.

---

## 9. Yes — there is already a full "explain / learn" mode. There is NO `[learn]` config section.

`internal/config/learn_test.go` tests a **boolean**, not a section. The real config surface:

- `internal/config/config.go:79` — `Learn bool \`toml:"learn"\`` inside `[general]`, comment: *"learning mode: teach (native→foreign) or grammar-correct (foreign→native)"*
- `internal/config/config.go:66` — `Learn *bool \`toml:"learn,omitempty"\`` in the per-front-end `[cli]`/`[tui]` `Overlay` (so the TUI can default learn on while the CLI stays off — `learn_test.go:21-30`)
- `internal/config/resolve.go:151` — `Learn: o.Learn || g.Learn || envVal("TRANSLATE_LEARN") != ""`
- `internal/config/resolve.go:159-163` — **learn implies pair**:
  ```go
  // Learning mode is inherently bidirectional; it reuses pair's home/away
  // direction routing, so enabling learn enables pair.
  if r.Learn {
  	r.Pair = true
  }
  ```

How it runs:
- CLI flag `cmd/root.go:87`: `--learn` → *"learning mode: teach (native→foreign) or grammar-correct (foreign→native)"*
- The one-shot CLI **bypasses smart-auto/dictionary** and runs a bare LLM (`cmd/root.go:203-210`, `appcore.LearnEngineFromConfig` at `build.go:178-180`); fails with `"learn mode requires an LLM provider"` when none is configured.
- Away language auto-picked when unset — `defaultAway` (`cmd/root.go:676-681`): English home → `zh-TW`, everyone else → `en`.
- Parsing is defensive: markdown fences and leaked reasoning are tolerated (`extractJSON`, `llm.go:446-460`), and a parse failure degrades to raw text + warning `"learn: could not parse structured output — showing the raw reply"` (`llm.go:363-389`). The model's own `direction` guess is **overwritten** by the offline detection (`llm.go:380`).
- Plain-text rendering: `renderLearnCLI` (`cmd/root.go:684-743`) — `✔ corrected`, `↳ translation`, `✎ issue`, `• vocab`, `ⓘ notes`.
- TUI: `^n` toggles it (`internal/tui/keys.go:35`, `update.go:211-220`), status bar shows `learn zh-TW⇄en` (`view.go:126`), renderer `view.go:249+`.

**The key finding for your Raycast plan:** `translate "<text>" --learn --json` already emits the full structured tutor payload. In `oneShot` the switch at `cmd/root.go:486-501` puts `case flagJSON:` *first*, and `TranslateResult.Learn` is a marshalled field — so a Raycast AI tool can get explanatory output today with zero Go changes. Learn is reachable **only** via the CLI/TUI, though: neither the MCP tool schema nor the HTTP `translateRequest` has a `learn` field (the OpenAPI schema *documents* `LearnResult` at `internal/server/openapi.json:202,254` as a possible response field, but nothing can request it).

Learn mode is also **undocumented in README.md** (no heading; only two incidental mentions at README:130 and :150).

## Bottom line for the two Raycast AI options

**(a) plain-translate tool** — trivially served today. `translate <text> --json` → `TranslateResult`, or `POST /v1/translate` if you want the warm server. An MCP `translate` tool already exists with a usable schema, so if Raycast can bridge to MCP you may not need new Go code at all.

**(b) interactive explanatory / "learn while you ask"** — the prompts, the JSON schema, the offline direction routing, the defensive parser, and the CLI `--json` surface all already exist as `--learn`. The gaps are: (i) `learn` is missing from `appcore.Params`, the HTTP `translateRequest`, and the MCP `translateInput` — three tiny additions if you want it off the server or via MCP; (ii) learn is single-turn and non-streaming by design (`llm.go:481`), so a conversational "ask follow-ups" flow has no existing prompt; (iii) `--instructions` is the zero-code escape hatch for an ad-hoc explanatory tone, injected into the system prompt at `prompt.go:108-110`.

# Prompt &amp; architecture map — `translate` Go CLI

## 1. Where prompts live — `internal/engine/prompt.go` (the ONLY prompt file)

Every LLM prompt in the project is a package-level `const` in `/Users/david/src/tries/2026-07-09-translate-cli-tui/internal/engine/prompt.go` (255 lines). I grepped the whole engine package: no other file constructs prompts. `google.go`, `dict.go`, `localdict.go`, `chain.go`, `smartauto.go` never touch them.

**Preset identifiers** — `internal/engine/prompt.go:12-16` (these are exported; the strings themselves are not):

```go
const (
	PresetConcise    = "concise"    // terse direct translation (default)
	PresetContextual = "contextual" // short list of common-sense translations
	PresetDictionary = "dictionary" // translation + 1-2 example sentences
)
```

### `concise` — `internal/engine/prompt.go:21-33`

```
You are a precise, professional translation engine.
Translate the user's text into the target language faithfully and idiomatically.

Rules:
- Preserve the meaning, tone, and register (formal/informal, technical/casual) of the source.
- The user's text may contain typos, slang, or ungrammatical phrasing. Interpret their
  INTENDED meaning and translate that; do not translate a typo literally, and never refuse.
- Output ONLY the translated text. No quotes, no explanations, no language labels,
  no commentary before or after.
- ALWAYS translate into the target language. A single word, name, technical term, or
  loanword written in a DIFFERENT language must still be translated — never echo it back.
  Only when the text is ALREADY in the target language should you return it (lightly
  corrected if it was misspelled).
```

### `contextual` — `internal/engine/prompt.go:36-47`

```
You are a precise, professional translation engine.
Translate the user's text into the target language, showing how the translation changes
across the most common senses or contexts of the source.

Rules:
- Preserve meaning, tone, and register. The text may contain typos, slang, or ungrammatical
  phrasing — interpret the INTENDED meaning; never refuse and never translate a typo literally.
- Output a SHORT list of 2-4 lines, one line per distinct common sense/context.
- Format each line EXACTLY as: "N. &lt;translation&gt; — &lt;short context label in the TARGET language&gt;".
- Order lines from the most likely/common sense to the least.
- If the text has only one natural sense, output a single line — do not invent senses.
- Output ONLY the list. No preamble, no headings, no commentary before or after.
```

### `dictionary` — `internal/engine/prompt.go:50-63`

```
You are a precise, professional translation engine
that also gives brief usage examples.
Translate the user's text into the target language, then illustrate it with example sentences.

Rules:
- Preserve meaning, tone, and register. Interpret the INTENDED meaning of typos/slang; never refuse.
- The FIRST line is ONLY the translation of the user's text — no label, no quotes.
- Then a blank line, then 1-2 example sentences that use the translation naturally.
- Format each example on two lines:
    line 1: the example sentence in the TARGET language,
    line 2: its translation in the source language (the language of the user's input),
            prefixed with "  ↳ ".
- Keep examples short and idiomatic. Output ONLY the translation and the examples —
  no headings, no numbering of the first line, no commentary.
```

Selection is a plain switch with concise as the default — `internal/engine/prompt.go:66-75`.

### The user turn — `internal/engine/prompt.go:84-88`

```go
const translateUserPrompt = `Source language: %s
Target language: %s

Text:
%s`
```

Language codes are expanded to readable names (`lang.Name(req.Target)` → `"chinese (traditional) (zh-TW)"`) at `prompt.go:93-101`.

### Two more prompt families in the same file

**Bilingual doc mode** — `internal/engine/prompt.go:120-134`:

```
You translate terminal / CLI documentation into %[1]s.

You are given the whole document as a numbered list of SEGMENTS. Some are prose to
translate; others are command/code lines marked "[code — context only]" and are
shown ONLY so you understand the document — never translate or echo them.

Rules:
- Use the WHOLE document as context. A bare token like "rg" or "ls" on its own is
  the COMMAND being documented, not an abbreviation — do not expand or gloss it.
- Keep command names, subcommands, flags, file paths, URLs, and code verbatim.
- Preserve meaning, tone, and register. Interpret the intended meaning of typos; never refuse.
- Translate EVERY prose segment into %[1]s only — one consistent variant, never mixed.
- Respond with ONE JSON object and NOTHING else: keys are the prose segment numbers
  (as strings), values are the translations. No markdown fence, no reasoning, no
  commentary before or after the JSON.
```

**Learn mode** — the two prompts most relevant to your (b) "learn English while you ask" idea. `internal/engine/prompt.go:186-208`:

```
You are a warm, encouraging language tutor helping a native %[1]s speaker learn %[2]s.
The user writes in %[1]s. Translate their text into natural, idiomatic %[2]s, then teach it.

Respond with ONE JSON object and NOTHING else — no markdown code fence, no prose before or after it.
Schema (fill every relevant field; omit a field only when it genuinely has no content):
{
  "direction": "teach",
  "original": "&lt;the user's %[1]s input, verbatim&gt;",
  "translation": "&lt;the idiomatic %[2]s translation&gt;",
  "vocab": [
    {"term": "&lt;key %[2]s word or phrase&gt;", "pos": "&lt;part of speech&gt;", "phonetic": "&lt;KK/IPA for English, pinyin for Chinese&gt;", "meaning": "&lt;concise meaning in %[1]s&gt;"}
  ],
  "examples": [
    {"foreign": "&lt;a short natural %[2]s sentence using the translation&gt;", "native": "&lt;its %[1]s translation&gt;"}
  ],
  "notes": "&lt;one short usage or register tip in %[1]s, optional&gt;"
}

Rules:
- Write every meaning, note, and explanation in %[1]s (the learner's language).
- vocab: only the key content words/phrases worth learning (at most 8); skip trivial function words.
- examples: 1-2, short and idiomatic.
- Interpret the intended meaning of typos/slang; never refuse. Output ONLY the JSON object.
```

`internal/engine/prompt.go:212-232`:

```
You are a warm, encouraging language tutor helping a %[2]s speaker who is learning %[1]s.
The user writes a sentence in %[1]s that may contain mistakes. Correct it and explain, kindly.

Respond with ONE JSON object and NOTHING else — no markdown code fence, no prose before or after it.
Schema (fill every relevant field; omit a field only when it genuinely has no content):
{
  "direction": "correct",
  "original": "&lt;the user's %[1]s input, verbatim&gt;",
  "corrected": "&lt;the grammatically correct, idiomatic %[1]s sentence&gt;",
  "translation": "&lt;a %[2]s translation of the intended meaning&gt;",
  "issues": [
    {"span": "&lt;the problematic fragment of the input&gt;", "fix": "&lt;the corrected fragment&gt;", "explanation": "&lt;why, in %[2]s&gt;"}
  ],
  "notes": "&lt;one short encouraging tip in %[2]s, optional&gt;"
}

Rules:
- Write every explanation and note in %[2]s (the learner's native language).
- If the sentence is already correct, echo it in "corrected" and return "issues": [].
- List each distinct mistake as one issue; keep explanations concise and beginner-friendly.
- Interpret the intended meaning of typos/slang; never refuse. Output ONLY the JSON object.
```

Learn user turn is bare (`internal/engine/prompt.go:236-237`): `Text:\n%s` — the system prompt already names both languages.

### Reusability verdict

The prompt *strings* are **unexported consts** in package `engine`, so a Raycast extension cannot import them; but they are reachable **behaviorally** through the exported `engine.Request` struct, and — crucially — through the **CLI's `--json` output** and the **HTTP API**. Direction selection is decided offline, not by the model (`learnDirection`, `internal/engine/prompt.go:177-182`), using the same script router as pair mode.

---

## 2. `--instructions` — how custom text reaches the prompt

One mechanism, appended to the *system* prompt for all three prompt families:

- Flag declared `cmd/root.go:83`: `f.StringVar(&amp;flagInstructions, "instructions", "", "extra system-prompt guidance (domain focus, etc.)")`
- → `config.Overrides.Instructions` (`cmd/root.go:119`) → resolve precedence flag &gt; env `TRANSLATE_INSTRUCTIONS` &gt; `[cli]`/`[tui]` overlay &gt; `[general] instructions` (`internal/config/resolve.go:148`, `internal/config/config.go:86`)
- → `engine.Request.Extra` (`internal/engine/engine.go:35`)
- → appended verbatim at **`internal/engine/prompt.go:108-110`**:

```go
if extra := strings.TrimSpace(req.Extra); extra != "" {
	system += "\n\nUser preferences (apply where relevant, e.g. domain terminology):\n" + extra
}
```

The identical three lines are repeated in `buildBilingualPrompt` (`prompt.go:155-157`) and `buildLearnPrompt` (`prompt.go:250-252`). So `--instructions` is a **general-purpose system-prompt injection point** — it is your cheapest lever for an "explanatory answer" mode without touching Go code.

Also exposed over HTTP as `instructions` (`internal/server/handlers.go:27`, SSE query param `internal/server/sse.go:44`). **Not** exposed by the MCP server.

---

## 3. Engine architecture

**Interface** — `internal/engine/engine.go:201-207`:

```go
type Engine interface {
	Name() string
	Translate(ctx context.Context, req Request) (&lt;-chan Chunk, error)
	Detect(ctx context.Context, text string) (string, error)
	Available(ctx context.Context) bool
	Supports(m Mode) bool
}
```

Contract (documented `engine.go:192-200`): `Translate` returns a receive-only channel and MUST close it after exactly one terminal `Chunk` (`ChunkDone` or `ChunkError`); streaming engines emit zero or more `ChunkToken` first. `Chunk` is at `engine.go:185-190`.

**Implementations**

| Engine | File | Prompts? | Streams? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LLMEngine` (any OpenAI-compatible: copilot-proxy, ollama, openrouter, litellm, generic) | `internal/engine/llm.go` | yes — the only one | yes |
| `GoogleEngine` (free keyless `translate_a/single`) | `internal/engine/google.go` | no | no |
| `DictEngine` (dictionaryapi.dev) | `internal/engine/dict.go` | no | no |
| `LocalDictEngine` (CC-CEDICT + ECDICT SQLite) | `internal/engine/localdict.go` | no | no |
| `SmartDictEngine` (dict → LLM fallback) | `internal/engine/smartdict.go` | delegates, forces `PresetDictionary` (`smartdict.go:111-114`) | passes through |
| `SmartAutoEngine` (word→dict, phrase→LLM) | `internal/engine/smartauto.go` | delegates | passes through |
| `Chain` (`auto`, ordered failover) | `internal/engine/chain.go` | delegates | passes through |

**Builders** — `internal/appcore/build.go:23-51` (`BuildEngine` switch on `res.Engine`: `auto` → `BuildAutoChain`, `smartauto` → `SmartAutoFromConfig`, `google`, `llm`, or a named provider). Default `chain.order` is `["copilot", "ollama", "google", "dict"]` (`internal/config/config.go:251`); default providers are `copilot` at `http://localhost:4141/v1`, `ollama` at `http://localhost:11434/v1`, `openrouter` (`config.go:254-271`).

**Streaming** — two wire protocols in `llm.go`:
- OpenAI `/chat/completions` SSE — `translateOpenAI` `llm.go:471-553`, parser `readSSE` `llm.go:657-695`
- Anthropic `/v1/messages` SSE — `translateAnthropic` `llm.go:556-642`, parser `readAnthropicSSE` `llm.go:702-749`; routed whenever the model id starts with `claude` (`isAnthropicModel`, `llm.go:228-230`)

Two gotchas worth carrying into a Raycast design:
- **Structured modes never stream** — `llm.go:481` and `llm.go:566`: `stream := req.Stream &amp;&amp; !req.Learn &amp;&amp; !req.Bilingual`.
- **Truncation is detected, not silently accepted** — `markTruncated` (`llm.go:464-468`) sets a `Warnings` entry `"output was cut off before completion (stream truncated) — press Enter to retry"`; `max_tokens` scales with input via `outputTokenBudget` (`llm.go:174-183`). Also `docs`/`pitfalls/llm-stream-truncation-silently-rendered-as-complete.md`.
- copilot-proxy **buffers** Claude `/v1/messages`, so visible token cadence is coarse for Claude regardless of transport (`internal/server/sse.go:23-25`).

---

## 4. `translate define &lt;word&gt;` — local dictionary first, LLM only as fallback

`cmd/define.go:22-89`. Engine choice via `appcore.DefineEngine` (`internal/appcore/build.go:186-195`): plain offline dict, or `smart-dict` when a provider exists and `[smartdict] define_default` is set; `--plain` / `--smart` force either.

Data is **local**: CC-CEDICT (zh→en) and **ECDICT** (en→zh, 770k-row SQLite) — `internal/engine/localdict.go`, `ecdict.go`, `cedictdb.go`. The gloss language is stamped honestly, not echoed from `--to` (`internal/engine/localdict.go:170-173`):

```go
const (
	cedictGlossLang = "en"    // CC-CEDICT defines Chinese in English
	ecdictGlossLang = "zh-CN" // ECDICT defines English in Simplified Chinese
)
```

On a hard miss the smart-dict engine falls back to the LLM with `PresetDictionary` and stamps a warning `"no dictionary entry for %q — defined via %s (LLM)"` (`internal/engine/smartdict.go:106-129`). A too-far fuzzy match also falls back (`smartdict.go:89-102`).

**Output structs** — `internal/engine/engine.go:116-135`:

```go
type DictEntry struct {
	Word      string    `json:"word"`
	Phonetic  string    `json:"phonetic,omitempty"`
	Meanings  []Meaning `json:"meanings,omitempty"`
	SourceURL string    `json:"source_url,omitempty"`
}

type Meaning struct {
	PartOfSpeech string       `json:"part_of_speech"`
	Definitions  []Definition `json:"definitions"`
	Synonyms     []string     `json:"synonyms,omitempty"`
	Antonyms     []string     `json:"antonyms,omitempty"`
}

type Definition struct {
	Text    string `json:"definition"`
	Example string `json:"example,omitempty"`
}
```

Plain-text rendering is `renderDict` (`cmd/define.go:92-119`), which caps at 4 definitions per part of speech. Note: `translate define --plain &lt;miss&gt;` **exits 1 with no JSON** (documented in `backlog/look-up-word.md:51-54`), while `translate dict search` exits 0 with `[]`.

---

## 5. `--json` — one struct for both commands

Both `translate &lt;text&gt; --json` (`cmd/root.go:487-492`) and `translate define &lt;word&gt; --json` (`cmd/define.go:75-79`) marshal the **same** `*engine.TranslateResult` with `SetIndent("", "  ")`. Full definition, `internal/engine/engine.go:72-113`:

```go
type TranslateResult struct {
	Translation    string   `json:"translation"`
	DetectedSource string   `json:"detected_source,omitempty"`
	Target         string   `json:"target"`
	Alternatives   []string `json:"alternatives,omitempty"`
	Notes          string   `json:"notes,omitempty"`
	Confidence     float64  `json:"confidence,omitempty"`

	Warnings []string `json:"warnings,omitempty"`

	Truncated bool `json:"-"`

	// Provenance — stamped by the producing engine / chain.
	Engine string `json:"engine,omitempty"`
	Model  string `json:"model,omitempty"`

	Dictionary *DictEntry `json:"dictionary,omitempty"`
	Learn *LearnResult `json:"learn,omitempty"`
	Bilingual map[int]string `json:"-"`
	Suggestions []string `json:"suggestions,omitempty"`

	SuggestDistance int `json:"-"`
}
```

So: `define --json` fills `dictionary` (or `suggestions` on a fuzzy miss); `translate --json` fills `translation` + provenance; **`translate --learn --json` fills `learn`** (see §9). `Truncated` and `Bilingual` are `json:"-"` — SSE re-surfaces truncation as an explicit `warning` event (`internal/server/sse.go:68-73`).

The learn payload — `internal/engine/engine.go:140-170`:

```go
type LearnResult struct {
	Direction   string         `json:"direction"`           // "teach" (native→foreign) | "correct" (foreign→native)
	Original    string         `json:"original"`            // the user's input as received
	Corrected   string         `json:"corrected,omitempty"` // correct-direction: the fixed foreign sentence
	Translation string         `json:"translation"`         // teach: foreign translation; correct: native translation of intent
	Notes       string         `json:"notes,omitempty"`     // short tip/encouragement, in the NATIVE language
	Issues      []LearnIssue   `json:"issues,omitempty"`    // correct-direction grammar/usage fixes
	Vocab       []LearnGloss   `json:"vocab,omitempty"`     // teach-direction glosses
	Examples    []LearnExample `json:"examples,omitempty"`  // teach-direction usage examples
}

type LearnIssue struct {
	Span        string `json:"span"`        // the problematic fragment of the input
	Fix         string `json:"fix"`         // the corrected fragment
	Explanation string `json:"explanation"` // why — in the NATIVE language
}

type LearnGloss struct {
	Term     string `json:"term"`               // foreign word/term
	Pos      string `json:"pos,omitempty"`      // part of speech
	Phonetic string `json:"phonetic,omitempty"` // KK/IPA for English, pinyin for Chinese
	Meaning  string `json:"meaning"`            // meaning in the NATIVE language
}

type LearnExample struct {
	Foreign string `json:"foreign"` // example sentence in the foreign language
	Native  string `json:"native"`  // its native-language translation
}
```

And the headword-search shape (`translate dict search --json`, `GET /v1/dict/search`) — `internal/engine/dictsearch.go:29-49` (`SearchResult{query, script, source, candidates[], notes}` with `Candidate{word, phonetic, preview, pos, rank, match, distance}`).

---

## 6. `--pair` and `--bilingual` / `-2`

**`--pair`** changes the *prompt* (adds a directive) and the *routing* (target selection), not the output shape.

- Directive appended to whichever preset is active — `internal/engine/prompt.go:81`:
  ```
  Bidirectional mode: the text is written in ONE of %s or %s. Detect which of the two it is, and translate it into the OTHER one. ALWAYS translate — never return the text unchanged, even for a single word, a proper name, a technical term, or a loanword.
  ```
  Applied at `prompt.go:105-107` — deliberately *appended* so the concise/contextual/dictionary output format survives.
- Offline routing: `appcore.EffectiveTarget` (`internal/appcore/record.go:15-22`) → `lang.PairTarget(home, away, text)`, script-based for CJK/non-CJK.
- Pair **overrides `--to`** (README:118-130); `--no-pair` exists specifically so the Raycast dropdown can mean what it says (`docs/raycast-extension.md:224-239`).

**`--bilingual` / `-2`** is a *pipe-only reading view*, not a prompt style. Declared `cmd/root.go:88-89`; dispatched only on the stdin branch and only when `!flagJSON &amp;&amp; !res.Learn` (`cmd/root.go:245`). Two strategies via `--bilingual-mode`:
- `doc` (default) — one context-aware call, whole document as numbered segments, model returns `{"1":"…","2":"…"}` (`buildBilingualPrompt` + `finalizeBilingual` at `llm.go:407-442`); requires an LLM provider, non-streaming.
- `blocks` — per-block concurrent (bounded 5) translation, forced concise, any engine; also the automatic fallback (`cmd/root.go:511-591`).

Output: original block verbatim with ANSI intact, translation beneath prefixed `  ↳ `, dimmed on a TTY (`internal/bitext/bitext.go:131-153`, `cmd/root.go:665-671`).

---

## 7. `internal/bitext` — ANSI-safe block splitting for the bilingual view

Package doc, `internal/bitext/bitext.go:1-6`: splits piped terminal input into blank-line-delimited blocks and renders the bilingual view. Three exported functions:

- `Strip(s)` — wraps `charmbracelet/x/ansi.Strip`; applied to **all** piped stdin before it becomes `Request.Text` (`cmd/root.go:239`), so colored input never wastes prompt tokens.
- `Split(raw) []Block` — `Block{Raw, Plain, Kind}` where `Kind` ∈ `Blank|Prose|Code` (`bitext.go:14-32`). Code detection is **relative to the document's base margin** (`codeIndent = 2` deeper), because tldr/man indent their whole body (`bitext.go:41`, `47-108`).
- `Render(blocks, translations, dim)` — interleaves; `dim` is injected as a closure so the package stays presentation-free.

Pure, no engine/TUI imports, unit-tested (`bitext_test.go`). Reusable as-is for any "keep original + translation beneath" surface.

---

## 8. MCP server (`cmd/mcp.go`) and HTTP server (`cmd/serve.go`) — both exist and both shipped

### MCP — stdio, official Go SDK `modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`

`cmd/mcp.go:11-38` registers the command; `internal/mcpserver/mcp.go:32-47` registers exactly three tools:

```go
mcp.AddTool(srv, &amp;mcp.Tool{
	Name:        "translate",
	Description: "Translate text into a target language (faithful, register-aware).",
}, translateHandler(svc))
mcp.AddTool(srv, &amp;mcp.Tool{
	Name:        "define",
	Description: "Look up the dictionary definition of a word or short term.",
}, defineHandler(svc))
mcp.AddTool(srv, &amp;mcp.Tool{
	Name:        "history",
	Description: "List or fuzzy-search recent translation history.",
}, historyHandler(svc))
```

Input schemas are **inferred from Go structs via `jsonschema` tags** — `internal/mcpserver/tools.go:17-32`:

```go
type translateInput struct {
	Text   string `json:"text" jsonschema:"the text to translate"`
	Target string `json:"target,omitempty" jsonschema:"target language code, e.g. en or zh-TW (optional; server default otherwise)"`
	Source string `json:"source,omitempty" jsonschema:"source language code, or auto to detect (optional)"`
}

type defineInput struct {
	Word string `json:"word" jsonschema:"the word or short term to look up"`
}

type historyInput struct {
	Query string `json:"query,omitempty" jsonschema:"fuzzy search query; omit for the most recent entries"`
	Limit int    `json:"limit,omitempty" jsonschema:"maximum number of records to return (default 20)"`
}
```

Structured output is the full `engine.TranslateResult`; text content is a human rendering (`renderTranslation`/`renderDefine`/`renderHistory`, `tools.go:101-153`). **Notable gap: the MCP `translate` tool exposes no `preset`, no `instructions`, no `learn`, no `pair`** — it is the thinnest surface of the three.

### HTTP — `translate serve`, loopback, JSON + SSE + OpenAPI

`cmd/serve.go:14-58` (default port 4155, loopback enforced unless a bearer token is set). Routes — `internal/server/server.go:61-73`:

```go
mux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/translate", h.translate)
mux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/translate/stream", h.translateStream)
mux.HandleFunc("POST /v1/define", h.define)
mux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/dict/search", h.dictSearch)
mux.HandleFunc("GET /v1/history", h.requireToken(h.history))
mux.HandleFunc("GET /healthz", h.healthz)
registerDocs(mux)   // /openapi.json + embedded Swagger UI at /docs
```

Request body — `internal/server/handlers.go:22-31` — carries `text, source, target, preset, instructions, model, max_alts, pair` but **no `learn`**. SSE event grammar is documented at `internal/server/sse.go:13-25` (`token` / `warning` / `done` / `error`, all JSON payloads).

Both adapters sit on `internal/appcore.Service` (`internal/appcore/service.go:21-34`), a warm, transport-agnostic core holding pre-built engines + the history store. `appcore.Params` (`service.go:43-52`) has `Text, Source, Target, Preset, Instructions, Model, MaxAlts, Pair *bool` — again, **no Learn**.

## 9. Yes — there is already a full "explain / learn" mode. There is NO `[learn]` config section.

`internal/config/learn_test.go` tests a **boolean**, not a section. The real config surface:

- `internal/config/config.go:79` — `Learn bool \`toml:"learn"\`` inside `[general]`, comment: *"learning mode: teach (native→foreign) or grammar-correct (foreign→native)"*
- `internal/config/config.go:66` — `Learn *bool \`toml:"learn,omitempty"\`` in the per-front-end `[cli]`/`[tui]` `Overlay` (so the TUI can default learn on while the CLI stays off — `learn_test.go:21-30`)
- `internal/config/resolve.go:151` — `Learn: o.Learn || g.Learn || envVal("TRANSLATE_LEARN") != ""`
- `internal/config/resolve.go:159-163` — **learn implies pair**:
  ```go
  // Learning mode is inherently bidirectional; it reuses pair's home/away
  // direction routing, so enabling learn enables pair.
  if r.Learn {
  	r.Pair = true
  }
  ```

How it runs:
- CLI flag `cmd/root.go:87`: `--learn` → *"learning mode: teach (native→foreign) or grammar-correct (foreign→native)"*
- The one-shot CLI **bypasses smart-auto/dictionary** and runs a bare LLM (`cmd/root.go:203-210`, `appcore.LearnEngineFromConfig` at `build.go:178-180`); fails with `"learn mode requires an LLM provider"` when none is configured.
- Away language auto-picked when unset — `defaultAway` (`cmd/root.go:676-681`): English home → `zh-TW`, everyone else → `en`.
- Parsing is defensive: markdown fences and leaked reasoning are tolerated (`extractJSON`, `llm.go:446-460`), and a parse failure degrades to raw text + warning `"learn: could not parse structured output — showing the raw reply"` (`llm.go:363-389`). The model's own `direction` guess is **overwritten** by the offline detection (`llm.go:380`).
- Plain-text rendering: `renderLearnCLI` (`cmd/root.go:684-743`) — `✔ corrected`, `↳ translation`, `✎ issue`, `• vocab`, `ⓘ notes`.
- TUI: `^n` toggles it (`internal/tui/keys.go:35`, `update.go:211-220`), status bar shows `learn zh-TW⇄en` (`view.go:126`), renderer `view.go:249+`.

**The key finding for your Raycast plan:** `translate "&lt;text&gt;" --learn --json` already emits the full structured tutor payload. In `oneShot` the switch at `cmd/root.go:486-501` puts `case flagJSON:` *first*, and `TranslateResult.Learn` is a marshalled field — so a Raycast AI tool can get explanatory output today with zero Go changes. Learn is reachable **only** via the CLI/TUI, though: neither the MCP tool schema nor the HTTP `translateRequest` has a `learn` field (the OpenAPI schema *documents* `LearnResult` at `internal/server/openapi.json:202,254` as a possible response field, but nothing can request it).

Learn mode is also **undocumented in README.md** (no heading; only two incidental mentions at README:130 and :150).

## Bottom line for the two Raycast AI options

**(a) plain-translate tool** — trivially served today. `translate &lt;text&gt; --json` → `TranslateResult`, or `POST /v1/translate` if you want the warm server. An MCP `translate` tool already exists with a usable schema, so if Raycast can bridge to MCP you may not need new Go code at all.

**(b) interactive explanatory / "learn while you ask"** — the prompts, the JSON schema, the offline direction routing, the defensive parser, and the CLI `--json` surface all already exist as `--learn`. The gaps are: (i) `learn` is missing from `appcore.Params`, the HTTP `translateRequest`, and the MCP `translateInput` — three tiny additions if you want it off the server or via MCP; (ii) learn is single-turn and non-streaming by design (`llm.go:481`), so a conversational "ask follow-ups" flow has no existing prompt; (iii) `--instructions` is the zero-code escape hatch for an ad-hoc explanatory tone, injected into the system prompt at `prompt.go:108-110`.</result>

# Windows portability + a Quick AI (`@translate`) layer for the Raycast extension

## Context

Two questions, both answered "yes, with bounded work".

**Windows.** The extension is a local-CLI wrapper, which the Raycast platform docs
put at 70–90% shared code. Verified here: no `menu-bar` command, no
`runAppleScript`, no `sips`/`open`/`osascript`, no `process.platform` branching
anywhere in `src/`, and every subprocess call is already `execFile` with an argv
array (never `shell: true`). On the Go side `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build`
succeeds today (ran it), `internal/tts/native.go` already branches to PowerShell,
`internal/store/flock_other.go` is the `!unix` fallback, and `internal/xdgpath`
uses `os.UserHomeDir()` so config resolves to `%USERPROFILE%\.config\translate\`.
The blockers are three concrete things, listed in Part 1.

`backlog/raycast-extension.md:35` currently records the opposite — *"the binary
shell-out doesn't work on Raycast's iOS/Windows clients"*. That is wrong for
Windows; `execFile` of a user-installed binary is supported there. Correcting it
is part of this work.

**Quick AI.** `@translate` in Quick AI / AI Chat needs a `tools[]` array and an
`ai.yaml`. Neither exists; `docs/raycast-extension.md:22-29` deferred the whole
idea because "the AI API requires Raycast Pro". That reason is stale — Raycast
Settings → AI also offers a free message allowance, Ollama, and Custom Providers
(GitHub Copilot is listed), so the same copilot-proxy backend this CLI already
uses can back Raycast AI. The correct gate is `environment.canAccess(AI)`, and a
`tools[]` entry needs no gate at all, because Raycast only invokes it after the
user has cleared whichever gate applies.

The motivating failure is real and reproducible:

\```console
$ ./translate "shim" --to zh-TW --json
"translation": "n. 填片, 万能开锁片"        # a carpentry wedge — routed to the dictionary engine

$ ./translate "shim" --to zh-TW --learn --json --instructions "in the context of API rate limiting"
"translation": "墊片（在軟體工程中指用來相容或攔截 API 呼叫的小型程式碼層）"
\```

And the tutor prompt is already ~80% written: `internal/engine/prompt.go:186-208`
(`learnTeachPrompt`) has the warm-tutor tone and a `vocab[]` schema carrying
`pos` / `phonetic` (KK/IPA) / `meaning` — the 詞性/KK音標/意思 triple from the GPT
prompt — plus `examples[]` and `notes`. `--instructions` is injected into the
system prompt at `prompt.go:108-110` for all three prompt families, which is the
zero-code lever for domain context.

## Decisions taken

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | Port the code **and** declare `"platforms": ["macOS", "Windows"]` now |
| Learning mode | Both, staged: `ai.yaml` persona first (Part 2), Go `explain` direction second (Part 3) |
| Tool surface | **Minimal — two tools.** Intelligence lives in the prompt |

On the third: "先純tool prompt就好 不然感覺其實有點重複" is read as *keep the tool
surface small and do the work in the prompt*. So **no `learn-text` tool** (the
`ai.yaml` persona already tells the model to teach, so a tool that also teaches is
the duplication) and **no `search-history` tool** (duplicates the History command).
Two tools ship: `translate-text` and `look-up-word`. Both earn their place by
being things the model *cannot* do itself — reach the user's configured engine,
and read authoritative ECDICT phonetics.

**One flagged risk, not a blocker.** Declaring Windows ships code neither of us
has run on Windows hardware. Part 1 ends with an explicit manual verification
checklist and a README caveat rather than silence.

**One tension worth re-litigating separately.** `docs/raycast-extension.md:135`

not 'study modes' (Anki / Vocabulary Builder already exist in the store)"*. That
predates this idea. It does not block anything here (the extension is

if it ever goes to the store the listing copy and this feature disagree.
