◆ 軟體工程中的「墊片/中介層」用法
在 rate limiting 的情境下，「shim」指的是一層薄薄的中介程式碼（wrapper），插在呼叫端與實際的 API 或函式之間，用來攔截呼叫並附加額外邏輯——例如限流（rate limiting）、重試、記錄日誌等——而不需要修改原本的程式碼或介面。這個用法源自機械上的「墊片」概念：一個薄薄的填充物讓兩個本來不完全吻合的零件能順利接合。在程式設計裡，shim 常用來讓新舊系統相容，或在不動到底層邏輯的情況下「插入」新行為，例如：在呼叫外部 API 前先經過一個 shim，由它檢查目前的請求頻率，超過限制就延遲或拒絕請求。
  • shim (n.) /ʃɪm/ — 薄的相容層或轉接程式碼，用來攔截並修改行為
  • wrapper (n.) /ˈræpər/ — 包裝函式，功能類似，常與 shim 互換使用
  • throttle (v./n.) /ˈθrɒtl/ — 節流，限制請求速率的動作
  • middleware (n.) /ˈmɪdəlwɛr/ — 中介軟體，常用來實作 rate limiting 等橫切關注點
  ✎ We added a shim in front of the API client to enforce rate limiting.
    ↳ 我們在 API 客戶端前面加了一層 shim 來強制限流。
  ✎ The shim intercepts every request and checks it against the rate limit before forwarding.
    ↳ 這個 shim 會攔截每個請求，先檢查是否超過限流，再轉發出去。
  ⓘ shim 和 middleware、wrapper、interceptor 這幾個詞常常可以互換，差別只在於語境習慣：shim 強調「相容/插入」的性質，middleware 常指整個框架層級的機制，interceptor 則常見於 gRPC、HTTP client 等明確有攔截 API 的系統。

// translateRequest is the POST /v1/translate body. Only text is required; the rest
// fall back to the server's resolved defaults.
type translateRequest struct {
	Text         string `json:"text"`
	Source       string `json:"source,omitempty"`
	Target       string `json:"target,omitempty"`
	Preset       string `json:"preset,omitempty"`
	Instructions string `json:"instructions,omitempty"`
	Model        string `json:"model,omitempty"`
	MaxAlts      int    `json:"max_alts,omitempty"`
	Pair         *bool  `json:"pair,omitempty"`
}

func (r translateRequest) params() appcore.Params {
	return appcore.Params{
		Text:         r.Text,
		Source:       r.Source,
		Target:       r.Target,
		Preset:       r.Preset,
		Instructions: r.Instructions,
		Model:        r.Model,
		MaxAlts:      r.MaxAlts,
		Pair:         r.Pair,
	}
}

func (h *handlers) translate(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	var req translateRequest
	if !decodeJSON(w, r, &req) {
		return
	}
	if strings.TrimSpace(req.Text) == "" {
		writeError(w, http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, "empty_input", `field "text" is required`)
		return
	}
	res, err := h.svc.Translate(r.Context(), req.params())

func TestLearnDirection(t *testing.T) {
	// CJK input (home) → translate into the away side → teach.
	if got := learnDirection(zhEnLearnReq("我想學英文")); got != "teach" {
		t.Errorf("Chinese input direction = %q, want teach", got)

	}
}

```text
```

Precedence is `--no-pair` > `--pair` > `TRANSLATE_PAIR` > `[general] pair`. Learn
mode is inherently bidirectional and still implies pair. The TUI toggles the same
thing with `^g`; the Raycast target dropdowns expose it as an **Auto** entry.

### Bilingual mode (`--bilingual` / `-2`)

Pipe colored docs and read both languages at once — inspired by Immersive
Translate. `cmd | translate --to <lang> --bilingual` keeps each original block
verbatim (its ANSI/color intact) and prints the translation beneath each **prose**
block, dimmed on a TTY:

=== MCP section ===
## MCP server (`translate mcp`)

Expose translate as tools to any MCP host (Claude Desktop/Code, Cursor, …) over
**stdio** — no port, no token, history never leaves the pipe. Register:

```json
{ "command": "translate", "args": ["mcp"] }
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-07-28 06:32:41Z)**_

Everything is green. Here's where things landed.

## 1. Windows — yes, and it's done

The extension had no structural blocker: no `menu-bar` command, no AppleScript, no `process.platform` branching, and every subprocess call was already `execFile` with an argv array. What I changed:

- **`src/lib/platform/{index,macos,windows}.ts`** — branches once at import time, never in a component. Carries `binaryName` (`translate.exe`), `probeDirs` (Scoop / Chocolatey / `%LOCALAPPDATA%` / `%ProgramFiles%`), install hints (Homebrew is macOS-only, so Windows sees `go install` alone) and config paths.
- **`src/lib/shortcuts.ts`** — all 20 hardcoded `cmd` bindings replaced with the two-branch `{ macOS, Windows }` form, plus a `label()` helper so the ⌘-glyph UI copy derives from the same table instead of restating it.
- `platforms: ["macOS", "Windows"]`, per your call.

The Go side needed nothing — `GOOS=windows go build` already worked, `internal/tts` branches to PowerShell, `internal/store` has a `!unix` flock fallback.

**Three things you should know:**

- **The `binaryPath` platform-keyed placeholder was rejected** — `ray lint` says `must be string`. That form works for some manifest fields but not `placeholder`. I fell back to a neutral string and put both platforms' probe lists in the `description`.
- **Your `package-lock.json` pointed at `registry.npmmirror.com`** in all 254 entries. That's a store-rejection condition, and it only surfaces under `CI=true` — your old `raycast-lint` recipe ran without it. Rewritten to `registry.npmjs.org`; I verified `npm ci` still succeeds from a clean dir, so the integrity hashes were unaffected (same tarballs).
- **Three of your shortcuts don't work during development.** Raycast injects a Debug section under `ray develop` using ⌘R, ⇧⌘S, ⇧⌘X — and its entries win. So Reload, Load Selection and Clear silently do nothing while you're dogfooding, and work fine in an installed build. I documented it in `shortcuts.ts` and `raycast/README.md` but did **not** rebind them, since that changes your muscle memory.

## 2. Quick AI — shipped, minimal surface

Two tools (`translate-text`, `look-up-word`) plus `ai.yaml` carrying your GPT persona. I took "先純tool prompt就好" as *keep the tools small, do the work in the prompt* — so no `learn-text` tool and no `search-history`.

One thing worth flagging: I first put the tool-level JSDoc above `type Input`, and `--print-tool-schemas` showed it was **silently dropped** — the extractor only reads JSDoc on the *default export*. Both tools now carry their `instructions`, `preset` extracts as a proper `enum`, and no parameter is undocumented.

Then stage 2 in Go, since you chose "both, staged": a third `explain` direction beside teach/correct, reachable via `--learn-mode explain`, plumbed into `appcore.Params`, the HTTP body, and a **separate MCP `explain` tool** (a boolean buried in `translate`'s schema would never be discovered by an LLM host). Your exact question now works end-to-end:

```
$ translate '"shim" 在 rate limit 中是什麼意思' --learn-mode explain --to zh-TW
◆ 軟體工程中的「墊片/中介層」用法
  • shim (n.) /ʃɪm/ — 薄的相容層或轉接程式碼…
```

`--learn` had never been documented in the README at all; it is now.

## 3. The table screenshot

Root cause was worse than a missing option: `renderTranslation` dropped raw model output straight into `Detail`'s markdown with no fencing and no normalization. Fixed at both ends — a `tableDirective` in the Go prompt (gated on a new `bitext.IsTabular`) asking for GFM *structure* instead of padding, and `src/lib/markdown.ts` repairing anything that arrives without it. Your table now renders correctly. Written up as a pitfall, since the underlying rule — padding can't be portable between a terminal and a proportional renderer — will otherwise be re-learned.

## Two things I found that weren't in scope

- **17 pre-existing type errors**, invisible because `ray build`'s dev environment strips types without checking them and you had no `tsc` stage at all. Mostly React 19's `useRef` now requiring an argument — but one was real: `TranslationDetail`'s `usePromise` fetcher took 0 parameters while 5 dependencies were passed, i.e. closure captures instead of arguments. That's the bug where switching target language keeps serving the previous translation. All cleared.
- `just raycast-check` is the new gate (verify → build → tsc → lint → dist). Build runs *before* tsc deliberately: `raycast-env.d.ts` is gitignored here, so a fresh clone has no `Preferences` globals until something generates them. I verified the gate passes after deleting that file. If you'd rather follow the Raycast convention of committing it, that's a one-line `.gitignore` change — I left your existing choice alone.

`metadata/` screenshots remain the only store blocker, and that needs Raycast's Window Capture — no CLI can do it.

# translate

[`translate`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/translate) is a terminal translator —
one-shot from the shell, or an interactive TUI — backed by a fallback chain over your
local LLM providers, a free web API, and an offline bilingual dictionary.

It is the same tool the cross-platform
[dotfiles](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles) install on macOS (Homebrew tap) and
Linux (`go install`). This repo brings it to native Windows.

Enable it with the **translate** init prompt (on by default for the `workstation`
role).

There is no scoop or winget manifest for it, and no prebuilt Windows release, so
`.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` builds it from source:

```powershell
go install github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@v0.5.2
```

# agent-history-hygiene

Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.

Three surfaces, separated by purpose:

| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |

## Core invariants

1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
   history back.

## When to use this skill

Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:

- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
  chat history".
- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.

## When NOT to use

- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
  skip this skill entirely.
- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).

## Integration with existing infrastructure

This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
already has. It does not duplicate:

- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
  config the wrapper expects to find.
- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
- **chezmoi's `scripts/redact_secrets.py`** — remains the upstream
  source of truth. The skill bundles a copy so non-chezmoi users get
  protection; sync procedure in
  [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).

What this skill **adds**:

- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the "find my
  current transcript among many" problem.
- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
  committing.

## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene

Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
chat/plan artifacts.

```bash
# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is "ours" — mostly
#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh

# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.
git add path/to/feature/file.ts
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh
# Use --session-only if you want ONLY the current SpecStory + newest plan;
# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.

# 3. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
  exit 1
}

# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets
#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.
git commit -m "feat: ..."
```

## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project

For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
installed. Runs once per repo.

```bash
cd /path/to/new/project
bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit

# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
pre-commit run --all-files
```

What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:

1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
   (skips if already present unless `--force`).
2. Writes `scripts/redact_secrets.py` (bundled copy; use
   `--from-chezmoi` to symlink the chezmoi source so fixes propagate).
3. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
4. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
5. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
   one-line patch if missing.
6. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls
   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every
   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.

## Workflow C: post-leak remediation

When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
committed / pushed a secret":

1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
   become worth discussing.
4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.

## Gotchas

- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
  syntax everywhere.
- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
  `find-session.sh`.
- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
  agent artifacts, not after.
- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
  empty fields signal absence).

- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.

- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.

- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` + the redactor
  into the current repo, then run `pre-commit install`. Audits
  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
  (warns, never silently edits).

## Bundled assets

- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact
  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode
  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and
  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`
  regex.
- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal
  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +
  standard hygiene hooks.
- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi
  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for
  agent artifact dirs.
- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — bundled copy of chezmoi's
  `scripts/redact_secrets.py`. Chezmoi version is upstream; sync doc
  in `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.

## Reference files

  — SpecStory / Claude session layouts and the `$PWD → slug` algorithm.

- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)
  — three-layer defense (redact → gitleaks → `scan-staged.sh`),

The skill ships with a three-level test suite under
[`tests/`](tests/README.md). Run from repo root:

```bash
make test-skill
```

- `test_redact_secrets.py` — pytest for pure redactor functions.
- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus fixtures staged in tmp git
  repos, asserting real-key shapes fire and example shapes are
  allowlisted only inside configured artifact dirs.
- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
  `scripts/scan-staged.sh` (0 / 20 / 30 / 2).

The corpus + shell tests skip gracefully when `gitleaks` isn't on
`PATH`. See [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for what each
regression the suite locks in.

feat(engine): emit table structure, and add an "explain" learn direction

Two changes that share the same root observation: meaning and layout are
both context-dependent, and a faithful translation is not enough on its
own.

TABLES. A terminal table aligns its columns with space padding measured
in terminal cells, and a CJK glyph occupies two of them — so translating
one into Chinese destroys the alignment no matter how good the
translation is, and any consumer rendering in a proportional font
destroys it again. Padding cannot be portable; markdown table structure
can. bitext.IsTabular detects tabular input offline (pipe rows, or three
lines sharing a field-start column) and buildTranslatePrompt appends
tableDirective, using the same append-don't-replace mechanism as
pairDirective so the active preset's output shape survives.

EXPLAIN. --learn knew two directions, both routed offline by script:
teach (native input) and correct (foreign input). Neither answers a
QUESTION about a term, which is the case a plain translation gets most
wrong — asked about "shim", the dictionary engine returns 填片, a
carpentry wedge, which is correct and useless to someone reading about
rate limiting. The new direction is opt-in via --learn-mode because it
cannot be detected: a bare foreign term looks identical whether the user
wants it corrected or explained. Its prompt requires a `sense` field, so
the model has to commit to which meaning it is explaining.

Learn was previously reachable only from the CLI and TUI. It now flows
through appcore.Params, the HTTP /v1/translate body, and a dedicated MCP
`explain` tool — dedicated rather than a flag on `translate`, because an
LLM host picks tools by description and a boolean buried in a schema
would never be found.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

WINDOWS. platforms is now ["macOS", "Windows"]. Nothing structural

(translate.exe, plus Scoop / Chocolatey / %LOCALAPPDATA% / %ProgramFiles%
probes) and owns the install and config-path copy, branching once at
import time rather than inside any component. src/lib/shortcuts.ts holds
every shortcut in the two-branch {macOS, Windows} form: the one-binding
form takes a flat modifier list with no platform in the type, so a
hardcoded "cmd" compiles everywhere and is then dropped in SILENCE on
Windows, with no error, no lint failure, and no key beside the action.
label() derives the inline ⌘-glyph copy from the same table so the hint
text cannot drift from the binding.

Note three shortcuts (⌘R, ⇧⌘S, ⇧⌘X) collide with the Debug section
Raycast injects while an extension is in development, and Raycast's
entries win — so Reload, Load Selection and Clear do nothing under
`ray develop` and work in an installed build. Documented, not rebound.

QUICK AI. Two tools under @translate: translate-text (routes through the
user's own configured engine, presets and fallback chain) and
look-up-word (the offline dictionary, whose phonetic field is real data
rather than a model's guess). ai.yaml carries the bilingual tutor
instructions. Deliberately a small tool surface — the intelligence
belongs in the prompt, and a tool that merely restates it is duplication.
runTranslate gained --preset and --instructions passthrough, which the
CLI has always supported and the extension never used.

TABLES. renderTranslation put raw model output straight into Detail's
markdown with no fencing and no normalisation, so a translated table
arrived as reflowed ──── runs and orphaned pipe rows. lib/markdown.ts
rebuilds table-like runs into well-formed GFM and fences pipe-less
aligned blocks; StreamView defers the repair to onDone, because a
half-arrived table has no header row to normalise against. An action
toggles back to raw. This pass is needed even with the CLI-side fix,
since the extension talks to whatever binary the user has installed.

`ray build` in its default dev environment strips types without checking
them and the extension had no tsc stage at all. Most were React 19's
useRef now requiring an argument, but one was real: TranslationDetail's
usePromise fetcher took no parameters while five dependencies were
passed, i.e. closure captures instead of arguments — the shape that
keeps serving the previous target's translation. `just raycast-check`
now gates verify → build → tsc → lint(CI=true) → dist; build precedes
tsc because it generates the gitignored raycast-env.d.ts. The CI-mode
lint immediately caught package-lock.json pointing every resolved URL at
registry.npmmirror.com, which the Raycast store rejects; rewritten to

## 你的問題：會，但你現在測不到今天的東西

The Windows dotfiles **do** install `translate`, automatically:

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:48` | `installTranslate` prompt — **on by default** for the `workstation` role |
| `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl:530` | `$translateVersion = 'v0.5.2'` → `go install ...@v0.5.2`, installs `go` via scoop itself |
| `justfile:42` | `just upgrade-translate` → `go install ...@latest` |
| `backlog/translate-windows-distribution.md` | P2: GoReleaser + scoop bucket, to make this a one-line `Scoop-Install` |

**The problem: both paths resolve to a tag, and today's work is on `main`, 5 commits ahead of `origin` and 5 commits past `v0.5.2`.** So `chezmoi apply` gives you v0.5.2, and even `just upgrade-translate` (`@latest`) gives you v0.5.2 — neither has `--learn-mode`, the table directive, or the MCP `explain` tool. The Raycast extension would then be talking to a binary that predates everything it now relies on, which is exactly the permanent-skew case `pitfalls/raycast-extension-uses-installed-binary-not-working-tree.md` warns about.

Three ways out, cheapest first:

1. **Push `main`, then on Windows:** `$env:GOBIN="$HOME\.local\bin"; go install github.com/daviddwlee84/translate@main` — fastest, no release ceremony. Add `GOPROXY=direct` if the module proxy hasn't picked up the commit yet.
2. **Tag `v0.6.0`, push, bump `$translateVersion`** in the dotfiles script. Editing that variable re-renders the template, which is what re-fires the `run_onchange` — that's the intended upgrade path and it's what the pinned floor is for.
3. Clone + `go build` on the box directly.

One thing that lines up nicely without any change: the dotfiles install to `$HOME\.local\bin\translate.exe`, and `~/.local/bin` is **first** in the Windows probe list I wrote — so the extension will find it with no `binaryPath` preference needed.

Worth flagging before you test: I've never run any of this on Windows. `raycast/README.md` has the checklist, but the two I'd genuinely expect to bite are `getSelectedText()` (undocumented on Windows — both call sites already fall back to the clipboard, so please just record which happens) and whether Raycast for Windows exposes AI Extensions at all, which no Raycast doc states either way.

Correcting myself: I truncated my own search earlier, and Raycast **is** installed. Here's the accurate picture.

## Line 48 vs line 29

They're two different prompts, and you're asking about the wrong one:

| Line | Prompt | Installs |
|---|---|---|
| `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:29` | `installWindowsApps` | **Raycast** (+ VSCode, Cursor, Notepad++, Terminal, Alacritty, PowerToys) |
| `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl:48` | `installTranslate` | the `translate` CLI only — `go install`, no GUI |

So for the extension test you need **both** toggles on. Both default to `$full` (on for the `workstation` role), so a standard workstation apply gets you both.

## How Raycast actually gets installed

`run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl:406`, inside the `{{ if .installWindowsApps }}` block (line 378):

```powershell
Winget-InstallStore '9PFXXSHC64H3'   # Raycast
```

Not the community winget source — **Microsoft Store product id**, because Raycast has no winget manifest. Three consequences worth knowing before you apply:

- **It's a Store beta.** The script says so, and has a fallback: *"if it fails to install, Flow Launcher is the fallback"*. If that install fails you have no Raycast to test against.
- **Alt+Space collides with PowerToys Run**, and `installWindowsApps` installs PowerToys in the same block. The script emits a `Write-Warning` about it — you'll need to disable PowerToys Run or rebind.
- **`msstore` ignores `--scope`**, per the comment on line 118, so it installs per-user.

## What this means for your test

The pieces line up, with one gap:

- Raycast → Store install ✅
- `translate.exe` → `~\.local\bin\translate.exe`, which is **first** in my Windows probe list ✅
- The extension itself → **not covered**. Nothing in the dotfiles installs or registers a Raycast extension; you'll need to clone this repo on the Windows box and run `npm install && npx ray develop` from `raycast/extension`. That needs Node ≥ 22.14 and npm ≥ 7 — worth checking whether the dotfiles install Node before you get there.
- The binary will be **v0.5.2**, which predates everything I committed today — so `--preset`/`--instructions` passthrough works (old flags), but you'd be testing the extension against a CLI that lacks the table directive. Push `main` and `go install ...@main` first, or the table fix will only be half-present (the extension-side repair will still fire, which is exactly why I built both halves).

One caveat I can't resolve from here: I don't know whether Raycast for Windows exposes AI Extensions at all. No Raycast doc states it either way, and the only evidence is that the store accepts `platforms: ["macOS", "Windows"]` alongside `tools[]`. If `@translate` doesn't appear in Quick AI there, that's the likely reason rather than anything in our manifest.

Node is covered, and I found a real problem with what I shipped.

**Node:** `nodejs-lts` is in the ungated base scoop block (`run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl:171`) — always installed, no prompt. So that concern is resolved; `npm install` will work.

## Recommendation: clone separately for the first test

A recipe is the wrong shape *right now*, for four reasons:

1. **`ray develop` is a long-running foreground watcher, not an install step.** Wrapping it in a recipe hides that it never exits. You'd hit Ctrl-C and wonder whether it worked. (It does persist in root search afterwards — but that's a side effect of running it, not something a recipe makes clearer.)
2. **You're debugging untested code.** The first Windows run is where you find out whether `getSelectedText()` works, whether the probe dirs are right, whether AI Extensions exist there at all. Indirection is exactly what you don't want in that loop.
3. **Both dotfiles precedents produce a binary in `~/.local/bin`** — `upgrade-translate` (`go install`) and `specstory-build` (`pwsh -File ./scripts/build-specstory.ps1`). A Raycast extension isn't an artifact; it's a registration inside an app, and there's no `ray install` to make it idempotent.
4. **Where does the clone live?** That's a decision the dotfiles repo would have to encode, and you don't know yet whether you want it on that box permanently.

**Afterwards, yes — add one.** The repo's convention is a thin recipe delegating to `scripts/*.ps1`, plus a `backlog/` entry first (that repo has the discipline for it). By then you'll know the clone path and whether the thing works at all, which is precisely what the recipe would need to hardcode.

## The problem I introduced

**`just raycast-check` will probably not run on Windows**, and that's my fault. Compare:

```make
# windows-dotfiles/justfile — explicit
set windows-shell := ["pwsh.exe", "-NoLogo", "-Command"]

# translate/Justfile — nothing
raycast-check:
    cd raycast/extension && ([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) && npx ray build
```

`[ -d node_modules ] || npm install` is POSIX test syntax. `just` defaults to `sh`, so this only works if git's `sh.exe` is on PATH — and if you set `windows-shell` to pwsh to be safe, every one of those recipe bodies breaks instead. It's the trap the cross-platform reference names directly: *"just runs fine on Windows, but the recipes assume a POSIX shell."*

**For the test, sidestep it** — run the stages directly from `raycast/extension`:

```powershell
npm install
npx ray build          # generates raycast-env.d.ts
npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
npx ray develop
```

Two options for a real fix, and I'd want your call before doing either: keep `sh` and just document the git-bash dependency (zero code change, works today if scoop's git is installed), or add `set windows-shell := pwsh` and rewrite the five `raycast-*` recipe bodies in PowerShell (more work, no hidden dependency). The second is more correct; the first is honest about a repo whose primary target is macOS.

Want me to do one of those, and push `main` so `go install ...@main` picks up today's binary?

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-07-28 08:30:31Z)**_

Answering the question directly: **one Justfile, auto-detecting.** Two files aren't needed, and `just` 1.46 has first-class support for this — I verified it against the binary rather than trusting memory.

## The mechanism

```make
[unix]
_raycast-deps:
    @[ -d raycast/extension/node_modules ] || npm --prefix raycast/extension install

[windows]
_raycast-deps:
    @if (-not (Test-Path raycast/extension/node_modules)) { npm --prefix raycast/extension install }
```

The **same recipe name** declared twice with `[unix]` / `[windows]` attributes — `just` defines only the matching one, and `just --list` still shows it once. The leading `_` makes it private, so it stays out of the listing entirely.

## What actually had to be split: two recipes, not ten

That was the interesting part. pwsh 7 **does** support `&&`, so `cd X && npx foo` runs identically under `sh` and PowerShell. Only genuinely POSIX-specific syntax needed twins:

| Recipe | Why it needed splitting |
|---|---|
| `_raycast-deps` | `[ -d … ] \|\| …` is POSIX `test`; no pwsh equivalent |
| `raycast-lint` | `CI=true cmd` is a POSIX env prefix; pwsh spells it `$env:CI='true'` |

Everything else stayed single. `raycast-verify`'s `\` line continuation became one long line (pwsh uses a backtick, and `just` runs each line in its own shell anyway), and `raycast-check` now calls `just raycast-lint` as a sub-invocation rather than inlining `CI=true`, so that one platform difference is spelled in exactly one place.

The single most important line is the one that isn't a recipe:

```make
set windows-shell := ["pwsh.exe", "-NoLogo", "-Command"]
```

Without it `just` reaches for `sh` on Windows — its default on *every* platform — and a POSIX-only recipe fails with "program not found" rather than anything that points at the actual cause.

I also marked `install` / `clean` / `raycast-scripts` as `[unix]` (they use `mkdir -p`, `install -m`, `chmod`, and Script Commands are bash), gave `clean` a Windows twin, and added `[doc(…)]` attributes — without those, `--list` was showing the last line of each explanatory comment block as the description, which read as nonsense.

Gate re-run from a cleared `.build/`: green. Committed as `c27cdef`.

So the Windows dev loop is now just `just raycast-check` then `just raycast-dev`, same as here — I've updated `raycast/README.md`'s checklist accordingly and added a seventh item: confirm whether `@translate` shows up in Quick AI at all, since no Raycast doc says whether AI Extensions exist on Windows.

Still outstanding from earlier, and still your call: **push `main`** so `go install ...@main` gets today's binary onto that box — otherwise you'll be testing the extension against v0.5.2, which predates the table directive and `--learn-mode`.
